source: H. Graetz, Kritischer Commentar zu den Psalmen nebst Text und Uebersetzung, Breslau: Schottlaender, 1882-83

entries.note: בתורת ה' … ובתורתו in the same verse is intolerably tautological, avoided even in prose; so read ובתעודתו — תעודה (from עוד hiphil, 'warn, instruct') is used synonymously with תורה: 'warning, prohibition, law'.

entries.graetz_verse: 4 (as printed; lemma דרך תאבד is MT v. 6)
entries.note: דרך תאבד ('the way perishes') is not quite fitting and harsh; perhaps read תאבדם. In the same note יודע ה' is rendered 'beachten, animadvertere'.
entries.flag: verify verse label digit and pointing of תאבדם at high res

entries.note: ריק is an adverb (so Aquila: κενῶς). יהגו ('mutter, devise') cannot be right — too weak against the preceding רגשו; read יהמו 'to be restless, growl'. He likewise emends יהגה to יהמה in Isa 31:4 and compares Isa 59:11 (interchange of ג and מ, cf. Einleitung p. 131).
יתיצבו would state that the nations had already risen in revolt, whereas the following verb and the psalm's ending show they were only at the stage of deliberation; so read יתיעצו.
יסד can never mean 'take counsel'; read נועדו for נוסדו — graphic interchange of ס and ע (cf. Einleitung p. 134). The nations hold a 'Verabredung' (appointed meeting).

entries.emendation: אספרה אליכם חק ה׳, ה׳ אמר אלי
entries.note: V. 7a is inexplicable as transmitted and must be emended: 'I will declare to you the decree of the Lord; the Lord said to me…' — חק in the sense of something fixed, an unalterable determination (like Ps 81:5; 105:10).
וגילו ('rejoice' with ברעדה) gives no sense at all; read וחילו 'tremble' (so also Ewald).

נשקו בר is inexplicable. LXX (δράξασθε παιδείας) and Targum (קבילו אולפנא) preserve the true reading החזיקו במוסר (cf. Prov 4:13). Corruption: the ה of החזיקו was absorbed by the preceding ה of ברעדה; ח became נ (graphic interchange as 2 Sam 11:25), ז was confused with ש (cf. Einleitung p. 124), yielding נשקו; of במוסר the three middle consonants fell out, leaving בר. Peshitta already reflects the christological reading ברא 'son'. Dyserinck's emendation נשקו בו is unacceptable, since נשק never means 'pay homage'.
לנפשי means 'to myself'; instead of לו read לי. The Peshitta has לכי, i.e. לך, 'which fits much better' (cf. Einleitung p. 129).

מרים ראשי is without analogy and yields no graspable sense; perhaps read וקרן ישעי as in Ps 18:3 ('horn of my salvation' — his translation column renders accordingly). He also renders מגן בעדי as 'shield behind me, for my protection' (Frankel-Graetz Monatsschrift 1879, p. 49 ff.).

אקרא is imperfect, and the corresponding verb in the b-clause must express the same (hypothetical/future) time: 'were I to call, He would answer me' — the psalm sets his confidence against his enemies' claim.
entries.flag: verify exact pointing of the repointed form at high res

entries.note: יסמכני is not quite correct — 'for awaking one needs no support'; read יסבבני or יסבני ('He surrounds/protects me', matching his translation 'der Herr würde mich schützen').
entries.flag: verify verse label digit and which alternative forms at high res

entries.note: אלהי צדקי gives no sense; read אלהי צדק as in Ps 17:1 and like אלהי משפט.
The perfect הרחבת disturbs the train of thought; read the precative הרחיבה (ת and ה often interchanged, cf. Einleitung p. 132).

The reproach in a. ('you shame my honor') has no logical connection with b. ('you love vanity'). The LXX preserve the more correct reading of a.: ἕως πότε βαρυκάρδιοι, ἵνα τί = עד מה כבדי לב למה תאהבו — the psalmist addresses the 'hard-hearted' (his translation: 'Herzenshärtige, warum liebt ihr Leeres?').
הפלה … לו strikingly recalls the parallel Ps 31:22 הפליא חסדו לי; so the text must be emended here too to חסד לי ('the Lord has shown me wondrous kindness'), which בקראי in b. also supports.

ואמרו gives no sense — what should these hard-hearted ones say? Perhaps read יראו 'fear (the Lord)'; ודמו = remain silent, wait (like 1 Sam 14:9). Sense: 'fear the Lord when you complain of want on your beds, and be silent — cease complaining.'

The form נסה is 'eine Unform'. The Peshitta (נהורא דפרסופה, i.e. אור פניו, attaching ה׳ to the next verse) leads to the reading כסה עלינו אור פניו — a continuation of the nobles' complaint: 'the Lord has veiled His light from us' (cf. Lam 3:44).

מעת cannot possibly be comparative; read עת (the מ a dittograph of the final ם of בלבם): 'You gave joy in their heart at the time when their grain and wine were abundant' — i.e. while they still had plenty. LXX (ἐλαίου) and Peshitta (ומשחהון) additionally attest 'and their oil'.
יחדו cannot be a mere filler here, since it is only used of two or more parties set in relation of equality; perhaps read וְחֶדְוָה 'in joy'.
לבדד is not correct — it means only 'isolated, separated from others'; read לבדך ('Du allein, Herr').
תושיבני ('make me dwell') does not fit the context of lying down to sleep; read תשכיבני ('lässest mich in Sicherheit liegen').

יגרך cannot be correct: derived from גור it is intransitive and means only chance, temporary sojourn. A transitive verb must be substituted, perhaps חבר — יחברך 'evil is no companion to you', as in Ps 94:20.

תאבד ('you destroy') is too strong — that is only prayed for in v. 11. A verb matching יתעב in b. is needed, stating merely that God abhors such persons; perhaps read תנבל 'du verwirfst' (so his translation: 'Du verwirfst die Trugredenden').
entries.flag: verify first letter of תנבל at high res

entries.note: Instead of the incongruent singular בפיהו, all the ancient versions had the reading בפיהם before them.
Perhaps read נכוחה ('what is right/true', as Isa 59:14) for נכונה — ח and נ interchanged (cf. Einleitung p. 132). הוות = 'destruction' (cf. Ps 91:3).

יפלו ממעצותיהם is unsuitable. Dyserinck emends to יִפָּלוּ מעצתיהם, but without analogy; perhaps read a verb meaning 'may their counsels ruin them' (his translation: 'mögen ihre Rathschläge sie verderben (?)').
entries.flag: verify exact form of the proposed verb at high res

entries.note: תעטרנו is miswritten for the Piel תְּעַטְּרֵנוּ ('You surround him [with favor] as with a shield'). כצנה stands for כבצנה — after comparative כ the prepositional syllables are suppressed.
חנני stands for חַיֵּנִי ('revive me' — his translation 'Belebe mich, Herr'); the two are often interchanged, cf. Ps 119. אמלל = 'crushed, ground down' (LXX συντετριμμένος).

In vv. 9–10 the perfect שמע obscures the sense, as if the psalmist were appealing to past pardon; read ישמע (the י absorbed by the preceding letter, cf. Einleitung p. 139) = future, parallel to יקח ('Gott wird meine flehentliche Stimme erhören').
Same emendation as v. 9: read the future ישמע, parallel to יקח ('der Herr wird mein Gebet annehmen').
ישבו יבשו is not well intelligible; read בוש יבושו ('utterly ashamed') — the י of ישבו arose by dittography from the preceding י of איבי.
כוש is probably a scribal error for קיש (Krochmal): '[the son of] Kish, the Benjaminite' — this superscription was erroneously guessed from the content.
The plural cannot be right, since the psalmist throughout means only one enemy (vv. 6, 13–17) who bitterly hates and pursues him; so probably read מנכלי רדפי 'from the wiles of my pursuer'.

פרק = 'to free, release' here; following LXX (μὴ ὄντος λυτρουμένου) and Peshitta (ולית דמפרק) read ואין פרק ואין מציל — 'no one frees and no one rescues' (his translation: 'ohne Befreier und ohne Erretter').
זאת is too indefinite — 'this'! what then? Read זִמָּה (interchanges of מ/א and ה/ת, cf. Einleitung pp. 130, 132); עשה זמה is genuine Hebrew style.
LXX read the plural שוֹלְמַי, equivalent to אנשי שלומי 'those at peace with me'.
צוררי, whether singular or plural, is not parallel to שולמי; another word must be substituted, perhaps מֵרֵעַי 'my friends'.
Instead of ואחלצה read ואלחצה 'oppressed' (so Krochmal and Dyserinck): 'or if I have oppressed my adversary without cause'.
The anomalous pointing ירדף arose from doubt between the vocalizations יִרְדֹּף (Qal) and יְרַדֵּף (Piel).
Instead of ישכן read יַשְׁכֵּב (ב and ן often interchanged): 'lay my honor in the dust'.
בעברות צוררי can hardly be explained meaningfully; the sense requires בעברותך על צוררי 'in Your wrath against my adversaries'.
entries.flag: adjacent clause 'Gewiss muss …עורה emendirt werden' partly unclear — verify at high res

entries.note: משפט צוית is likewise incorrect; perhaps read משפט צדק ('erwecke mir gerechtes Gericht'), cf. Ps 71:3 where תמיד צוית is miswritten for מצודות.

שובה is an irregular form for שְׁבָה from ישב ('take Your seat on high, to judge'), like Num 10:36 שובה ה׳ רבבות, which Menachem b. Saruk rightly explained as שְׁבָה. Cf. the parallel Ps 9:5 ישבת לכסא שופט צדק.
Read the apostrophe דַּיַּן עמים 'O Judge of the peoples' (his translation: 'Herr, Richter der Völker, richte mich').
עלי is idle here; Dyserinck emends to וכתם פעלי ('the integrity of my deeds') — adopted in his translation ('die Unschuld meines Thuns').
With the ancient versions read בֹּחֵן as apostrophe: 'Du Prüfer von Herz und Nieren'.
Dyserinck rightly emends על to עלי: 'my shield rests upon God' ('Mein Schild bei Gott, dem Beistand der Herzensgeraden').

entries.emendation: וארך אפים ובל זעם בכל יום
entries.note: LXX have the noteworthy plus: ὁ Θεὸς κριτὴς δίκαιος καὶ ἰσχυρὸς καὶ μακρόθυμος καὶ μὴ ὀργὴν ἐπάγων καθ᾿ ἑκάστην ἡμέραν; Peshitta likewise has the negation (לא רגז). Retroverted: אלהים שפט צדיק וגבור וארך אפים ואל זעם בכל יום — so the Greek translator's Hebrew text read. Perhaps וגבור (unsuitable in context) → ונבר 'lauter'; and since the participle cannot construe with אל, read ובל or ולא: 'He is long-suffering and does not rage every day' (concessive, against the low notion of an ever-angry God; cf. Nah 1:3).
Between vv. 12 and 13 a verse appears to have fallen out, for vv. 13 ff. presuppose a person as subject not previously named — probably the 'enemy' of v. 6.

לדלקים can only connect with דלק 'pursue' — every other explanation is forced; but then one must read לְדֹלְקָיו 'for his pursuers', or perhaps an abstract form 'for his own pursuit' (his translation: 'seine Pfeile zur eigenen Verfolgung geschmiedet', like שמורים, עשוקים).
entries.flag: verify pointing of the abstract alternative at high res

entries.note: Instead of ויפל the future וְיִפֹּל must be read: 'so wird er in den Abgrund fallen'. חפר seems to mean 'dig deeper' than כרה.

The Peshitta renders כצדקו by איך זדיקותי ('according to my righteousness'), so probably better read כְּצִדְקִי — 'when He justifies me, gives me right against the slanderers'; thus the psalm gains a logical close.

תנה is a non-form ('Unform'). The only reading that fits the sense is נָתַתָּה, confirmed by Peshitta and Targum (דיהבת). The derivation of תנה from 'praise' is untenable, that verb's meaning and reading being uncertain in its single occurrence.

מפי עוללים gives no intelligible sense. מפי is elsewhere twice miswritten for מפני (cf. Einleitung p. 140; he suggests the same at 2 Sam 13:32 and Amos 6:5); so read מפני עוללים ויונקים, the preposition מפני meaning 'because of, in the interest of' — out of pity for the helpless children You have granted Your people strength.

To יסדת עז the word לעמך must necessarily be supplied (as Ps 29:11 ה׳ עז לעמו יתן, also 68:36), probably ousted by the following למען. That preposition means 'against' here; להשבית = 'to thwart, destroy' (never 'to still'). It would be clearer still with the future תְּיַסֵּד.

Before the question one must supply אמרתי or וָאֹמַר ('so I thought: what is man…'), matching his translation '(denke ich)' in v. 4. The parallel Hiob 7:17, Ps 144:3 has a different sense; here man's high station despite his insignificance is meant.

ותחסרהו, though confirmed by all the ancient versions, cannot be right: the Israelite conception of God does not tolerate the notion that weak man lacks only a little to be God's equal (Gen 3:5 depicts it as insolence; cf. Gen 18:27, Job 42:6 עפר ואפר). So probably read ותחסדהו, 'You have graced him, graciously endowed him' — the noun חסד is also used verbally.
מעט 'a little'? Probably read טעם 'understanding, insight' (metathesis) — 'Dass Du ihn mit Einsicht von Gott begnadigt hast'.

Instead of עלמות read על עלמות (LXX ὑπὲρ τῶν κρυφίων shows the word), and instead of לבן, which gives no sense at all, read נבל (cf. Einleitung p. 71). The whole thus reads למנצח על עלמות נבל — 'for the choirmaster, on the Alamot-lyre'.

גוים, three times in this psalm (vv. 6, 16, 21; likewise Ps 10:16), cannot possibly mean 'nations', being used identically with רשעים — these 'evildoers' can only be internal enemies of the oppressed. גוים stands for גֵּאִים 'the arrogant' (as Ps 94:2; 140:6); alongside the usual root גאה there was also גוה (Job 22:29; 33:17; Jer 13:17), whose participle could be גֵּוִים, whence גוים.
אבדת רשע is an incongruent parallelism; the plural רשעים is required (cf. Einleitung p. 139).

entries.emendation: — (lacuna: only האויב survives of a lost verse)
entries.note: From v. 6/7 a gap: only the word האויב remains of what is missing. Two verses have evidently fallen out between vv. 6 and 10 — the complement-verse to ג and the acrostic ד-verse, to which v. 7 (beginning תמו חרבות, reaching to זכרם) belongs as complement; with the following המה begins the acrostic ה-verse. Hence vv. 6–7 are obscure through this lacunous state.

חרבות here can mean what it does in Job 3:14 — pyramids, great tomb-monuments (cf. Gesenius, Thesaurus). But נתש means only 'tear out'; for 'destroy' Hebrew uses נתץ. So read נתצת (confusion of ש and צ, cf. Einleitung p. 123).

V. 8, which decidedly begins with המה (the acrostic ה), needs an antithesis to what follows: supply אבדו or יאבדו, as in Ps 102:27 — so rightly emended by Dyserinck: 'They perish, but the Lord sits enthroned forever.'
לעתות בצרה (also Ps 10:1) is an awkward combination — moreover the plural of עת is always עתים, never עתות; read לעזרת בצרה 'a help in trouble', as Ps 46:2 ('eine Burg zur Hilfe in Nöthen').
Since מרוממי cannot point to an accomplished fact, it can only continue the precatives חנני — ראה; so read ורוממני 'and lift me up from the gates of death'.
הגיון can in no way be connected with v. 17, not even reading הֶגְיוֹנִי ('this my song'); nor can it be a musical term here. It appears to be the ruin-fragment of a lost verse.
יעז אנוש is equivalent to לערץ in Ps 10:18; perhaps also read יערץ here ('that mortal man not defy') — ו for ר (cf. Einleitung p. 128) with ץ lost.
מורה is obscure, since neither 'terror' (מורא) nor 'instruction' (מורה) really fits the verb שית — his translation: 'Setze ihnen Schrecken (Lehre?)'.
תעלים would need עין supplied, or — perhaps better — read the passive תֵּעָלֵם with the Targum (תטמר): 'why do You hide Yourself?'
The close לעתות בצרה must be emended to לעזרה בצרה, as at Ps 9 (his note there: plural of עת is always עתים; cf. Ps 46:2).
דלק can only mean 'pursue' here, but must be turned into the passive following LXX ἐμπυρίζεται (which mistook it for דלק 'burn'): read יִדָּלֵק 'the poor is pursued' — then the construction fits.
Instead of singular רשע read the plural רשעים (cf. Einleitung p. 139); then the second half-verse יתפשו is congruent (namely רשעים as subject).

The three versions have the passive for הלל (ἐπαινεῖται), i.e. מְהֻלָּל, which also occurs with על — 'the wicked is praised for his soul's desires'. בצע is to be taken verbally or participially; ברך is only a euphemism for קלל (as Job 1:5).
The phrase is without parallel; in any case read בְּגָבְהוֹ 'in his arrogance' ('Der Frevler in seinem Hochmuth kümmert sich um Gott nicht').
The verb דרש absolutely requires an object; so necessarily read את אלהים instead of אין אלהים: 'he does not seek God'.

entries.emendation: בכל מזמותיו יצליחו דרכיו בכל עת
entries.note: כל מזמותיו (v. 4 end) means 'schemes', not 'thoughts', and needs completion — it is to be joined with v. 5; and for יחילו, which gives no sense, read יצליחו with the Targum: 'through all his schemes his ways prosper at all times'.

Connecting מרום with משפטיך is inadmissible; following LXX ἀνταναιρεῖται, another version (probably Symmachus, per Syro-Hexapla מרימין) and ἀφανίζεται, read מוּרָם from הרים — in any case a passive, 'removed out of sight' ('entrücket sind Deine Strafgerichte vor seiner Gegenwart'); so also, tactfully, Rashi's explanation.

The common explanation of כל צורריו יפיח בהם is untenable — פוח does not mean 'blow away', and a tmesis of בהם for בכל צורריו is unproven. So read יפחד: 'all his adversaries he sets in terror', בהם = through his schemes.
entries.flag: verify form יפחד (stem/pointing) at high res

entries.note: אשר לא ברע defies all attempts at explanation (in Exod 32:22 he reads פרע for ברע, as v. 25 there). Read אֲשֻׁרַי לֹא אֶכְרַע 'in my steps I shall not collapse' — כרע also means 'fall down'. (Similarly Krochmal, except that he keeps אשר, which makes the verse drag.) The emendation אשרי restores the parallelism.
במארב חצרים gives no sense — farmsteads/villages are no ambush-places; read רֹצְחִים for חצרים and כמארב for במארב: 'he is as in the ambush of murderers'.
Instead of במסתרים יהרג read with LXX (τοῦ ἀποκτεῖναι) the infinitive לַהֲרֹג: 'in hiding places, to kill the innocent'.

Before the puzzling לחלכה can be explained, the verb must be set right: צפן 'hide' does not suit עיניו, but צפה 'look out, lie in wait' does (as Ps 37:32). Rightly LXX ἀποβλέπουσι and Peshitta דיק. So read עיניו יִצְפּוּ (namely לחלכה) or תִּצְפֶּינָה (cf. Einleitung p. 136).

חלכה is enigmatic; the ancient versions' 'poor, weak' is without support. Most acceptable is Rashi's derivation from חיל with suffix: לחלכה = לְחֵילְךָ 'Your host, Your community' — the community of the pious, the Anawim. חיל is used of a swarm (Joel 2:11,25) and of a band of exiles (Obad 20), so חל = חיל defective. (Ibn Ezra's objection that חיל never occurs defectively is refuted by the Masorah to 2 Sam 20:15, which counts five defective occurrences.) A climax lies in the verse-close: his eyes lie in wait for Your whole host, not just individuals.
V. 9 is too long and v. 10 too short, both clumsy and obscure. ודכה is a non-word; the Qere יִדְכֶּה is already better, and the LXX render ταπεινώσει αὐτόν, i.e. יְדַכֵּהוּ 'he crushes him'.
The word בעצומיו is untenable; evidently read a word meaning 'through his schemes' ('es fällt durch seine Anschläge Deine Schaar'). The note continues onto the next page.
entries.flag: verify exact proposed form (במעצמיו/במזמותיו) at high res

entries.note: חלכאים is not compounded of חל כאים (as if = נכאים); the syllable אם is a dittograph of the following אם in אמר (v. 11). What remains is חלכ, i.e. חֵלְךָ 'Your host' — subject of the verbs ישח ונפל. This also restores the balance of vv. 9 and 10: unless יחטף עני in v. 9 is itself a dittograph of לחטף עני, the close במשכו ברשתו belongs to v. 10.
LXX render as infinitive (τοῦ μὴ βλέπειν), i.e. בלי רְאֹה; the infinitive of ראה is attested as רָאֹה alongside רְאוֹת (Gen 48:11).

'Lifting the hands', said of God, is thoroughly unsuitable — at best it would mean raising the hand for an oath. Hence Dyserinck's emendation commends itself, in parallelism with אל תשכח ענוים ('übersieh nicht den Unglücklichen, vergiss nicht die Sanftmüthigen').
entries.flag: verify Dyserinck's exact proposed form (תשיא/תשא) at high res

entries.note: V. 14 must be divided into two verses (see his section II, p. 181). To לתת one should probably supply נקם or גמול ('mit Deiner Hand [Rache] zu geben'). שוב can also mean 'entrust' (Gen 39:6): 'to You Your host (חלכה = חילך, see v. 8) entrusts its all.'

יתום 'orphan' makes no sense here (and still less the pairing יתום ודך in v. 18: 'the orphan and the downtrodden'?). Evidently read תם — here either לְתָם or, with the Peshitta (אנא הו עדורה), היית עוזרו 'You are the helper of the upright'. In other passages too יתום must be changed to תם (cf. Einleitung p. 140).
ורע is probably a dittograph of רשע.

The four Greek translators render תדרש רשעו passively (ζητηθήσεται ἡ ἁμαρτία αὐτοῦ καὶ οὐ μὴ εὑρεθῇ), which suits the sense far better than the active; retroverted תִּדָּרֵשׁ (perhaps רשעתו, or יִדָּרֵשׁ; cf. Einleitung p. 135): 'let his wickedness be sought and not found'.

Instead of מלך LXX have βασιλεύσει, i.e. יִמְלֹךְ as Exod 15:18; consequently אבדו is also to be emended to the future יאבדו ('Der Herr wird für immer regieren, die Hochmüthigen werden von seinem Lande schwinden').
גוים is here too to be emended to גאים 'the arrogant'; the sense is as in Ps 104:35 (see his note at Ps 9:6).
The perfect שמעת would point to an accomplished fact, wholly against the train of thought. The Peshitta has שמע אנת, i.e. שֹׁמֵעַ אתה, or simply read תשמע ('Des Sanftmüthigen Wunsch erhöre Du').

תכין לבם does not fit well. LXX have the substantive ἑτοιμασίαν τῆς καρδίας, but no Hebrew word matches that (Krochmal's תכון is un-Hebrew); perhaps read הגיון לבם 'their heart's musing' (ה–ת and ג–כ interchanges, Einleitung pp. 122, 133).
Evidently read תם ודך 'the upright and the downtrodden' (see at v. 14). אנוש מן הארץ = מן עפר הארץ, 'the man of earthly dust'.

All the ancient versions, including Aquila and Targum, render כמו צפור (ὡς στρουθίον, היך צפורא). If one splits כם off הרכם to form כמו, only הר remains — senseless. On the other side, only masculine singular נוּד suits לנפשי (the singer); the ו-final is idle. From the unexplained consonants ודהר the word מהר can be restored: נוד מהר כמו צפור 'flee quickly like a bird' (so also Krochmal); vv. 2–3 continue the friends' speech.

כמו אפל gives no sense — the persecutors need no midnight darkness for their crimes; read לירות במו אף לישרי לב 'to shoot in anger at the upright of heart', the ל of אפל being a dittograph (of the following ל).

השתות is difficult. Aquila θεμέλιον, Targum אשיתא 'foundations' (like Jer 50:15) — but that would be Aramaic. All other explanations (θεσμοί, διδασκαλίαι) fail because הרס does not suit them. In any case this שתות differs from Isa 19:10, where it means canal-workers (Frankel-Graetz Monatsschrift 1877, p. 374 ff.). His translation: 'die Grundfesten (?)'.
צדיק מה פעל is not quite intelligible; one would expect the future מה יִפְעַל. A sense is easier if taken as substantive: צדיק מה פָּעֳלוֹ 'what avails the righteous man's doing?'
פחים stands for פֶּחָמִים 'coals', as one Greek translator — probably Symmachus — rightly renders: ἄνθρακας ('glühende Kohlen').
ללשננו is like בלשננו; the ל is perhaps even dittographic — Peshitta lacks it, as do LXX, who render τὴν γλῶσσαν, i.e. accusative of respect.
משד is not parallel to מאנקת; perhaps read מִשַּׁוְעַ 'from the cry of the poor' ('Vom Wehklagen der Sanftmüthigen').

The close is enigmatic and must be rectified. One Greek translator (ἄλλος) has ἐν σωτηρίᾳ σου, i.e. לך for לו (cf. Einleitung p. 129), or perhaps לכם; one could then emend to אשית בישע מנוח לכם — 'I will give them rest with help' ('werde mit Hilfe Ruhe ihnen geben').
entries.flag: verify proposed wording (מנוח, suffix) at high res

entries.note: Before כסף the כ of comparison must be supplied — it is often dropped before an identical consonant: 'like silver refined in the crucible'.

In בעליל the final ל is a dittograph of לארץ. עלי (Prov 27:22) means 'mortar', not pestle — in the Talmud עלי is a block (Beitzah I,5) — so עלי can also mean the casting-mould (the explanation Rashi rejected).
לארץ is certainly idle; Dyserinck's emendation כחרוץ 'like gold' commends itself ('wie Gold siebenfach gereinigt').

Read תשמרנו after LXX (φυλάξεις ἡμᾶς) and Peshitta — the suffixes ם and נו are often interchanged (Einleitung p. 125); consequently the following verb must be vocalized תִּצְּרֵנוּ 'You will guard us'.

The last half-verse כרם זלות לבני אדם is enigmatic. The apparent substantive זלות is rendered verbally by the Sexta (ἐξουθένησας 'You have despised'), and LXX's ἐπολυώρησας points the same way; accordingly read the verb זַלּוֹתָ (זלל also has transitive force), with dative לבני אדם for accusative as often in later Hebrew: 'You have held mankind cheap.'

Only כרם remains obscure. After LXX κατὰ τὸ ὕψος σου one would read בְּרוּמְךָ or כְּרֻמְּךָ 'in Your height' ('in der Höhe (?)'). Others emend to 'like a worm' — without analogy; Dyserinck's נכר מולות ('signs of doom'?) is un-Hebrew.

עד אנה followed by נצח is illogical; read עד אנה ה׳ התשכחני נצח with interrogative ה. The last word means 'duration', used adverbially = לנצח 'continually' (Frankel-Graetz Monatsschrift 1880, p. 8 ff.).
עצות does not fit the context; read עַצְּבוֹת 'sorrows' (so also Dyserinck): 'wie lange soll ich Traurigkeit in meiner Seele hegen'.
As parallel to יומם in the first member, לילה must be supplied ('in meiner Seele … (Nachts)').
האירה עיני is an unusual combination — at best 'make my eyes sparkle' (as 1 Sam 14:27,29). So read הָאֵר עָלַי and supply פניך, as Ps 118:27 ('lass Dein Antlitz über mich leuchten').

גמל has the absolute sense 'show kindness' even without טוב. Moreover read יגמל (the י absorbed in כי, Einleitung p. 139): the singer will praise God's grace only when good shall have been shown him ('wenn Er mir Gunst erweisen wird').

The LXX add at the close of this verse οὐκ ἔστιν ἕως ἑνός, i.e. אין גם אחד as in v. 3 (his translation: '(auch nicht Einer)'). On Ps 14 and 53 generally: neither psalm reworks the other; both are partly faulty copies of one correct original, Ps 53 the more corrupted.
Here the reading כלו of Ps 53 is the more correct (against הכל in Ps 14); conversely סר (Ps 14) is more correct than סג (Ps 53), since that verb is not otherwise used in Qal.

אכל לחם is literally inexplicable; it appears figurative, like Aramaic אכל קרצא and the Arabic idiom: 'to slander, accuse' (probably likewise Ps 41:10 and perhaps Amos 7:12). LXX and Peshitta read the substantive (βρώσει ἄρτου, מאכולתא דלחמא), which suits the construction better: אֹכְלֵי עמי אֹכֶל לחם 'who devour my people with slanderous devouring'.
The close ה׳ לא קראו is the dissolved continuation of the apposition — properly ה׳ אין קראים, parallel to the description of those who forget God.
entries.flag: verify the compared phrase (שכחי אלהים?) at high res

entries.note: The recension Ps 53:6 has the plus לא היה פחד after שם פחדו, and LXX have it in Ps 14 as well; the genuineness of this verse-part is not to be doubted — it means the terror was a blind panic ('es war kein Schrecken').
Instead of דור צדיק the Peshitta has the plural (בדרא דזדיקא), בדור צדיקים, which also sounds better, like דור ישרים (cf. Einleitung p. 139).

עצת cannot be right — the rebuke would be too slight if the reprobates merely rejected the poor man's counsel; read עדת (ד/צ interchange, Einleitung p. 127), better plural עדת עֲנִיִּים 'the community of the poor (the Anawim)'. תבישו is also not quite correct but תבאישו 'treat with contempt'; and the reading מאסם (Ps 53) hints that several are meant, so מחסם for מחסהו. The whole sentence correctly: כי אלהים בדור צדיקים (ה)עדת עניים תבאישו? כי ה׳ מחסם — the interrogative ה is often lacking (Einleitung p. 116).

ישועת ישראל is striking — why name only one part of the people here and both immediately after? The word has evidently climbed up from the line below; more correctly read (after Ps 53) the plural יְשֻׁעוֹת.

One would expect בלשונו ('with the slanderer's organ'), or על לשנו is superfluous. Hence the reading presupposed by the Peshitta (לא נכולתן בלשנה) commends itself: רגל is a substantive and would have to be revocalized.
entries.flag: verify the proposed vocalization of רגל at high res

entries.note: לרעהו is plural in sense — read לרעיו, and likewise קרביו for קרבו ('seinen Nächsten … seinen Verwandten').

The commentators have struggled with נשבע להרע, whereas from LXX (ὀμνύων τῷ πλησίον αὐτοῦ) and Peshitta (ימא לחבריה) it is evident that the text originally read נשבע לרעהו 'who swears to his neighbor and does not change' ('Hat er seinen Freunden geschworen, ändert er nicht').

entries.emendation: עשה אלה קים הוא לא ימוט
entries.note: After עשה אלה the Peshitta has כאן הו, 'firm is such a one'; in later Hebrew קַיָּם would correspond: עשה אלה קים הוא לא ימוט.
The versions have the first person אמרתי 'I said to the Lord'. The following אתה אדני is emphatic: You are my Lord and no other.

entries.mt: טוֹבָתִי בַּל־עָלֶיךָ: לִקְדוֹשִׁים אֲשֶׁר־בָּאָרֶץ הֵמָּה וְאַדִּירֵי כָּל־חֶפְצִי־בָם
entries.emendation: טובתי בל עלי כל קדושים אשר בארץ המה ואדירי בל חפצי בם
entries.note: From v. 2b through v. 3 all is unintelligible and can never be explained without emendation. Read: 'my good fortune does not rest upon all the ‚holy ones' in the land, and in my superiors I have no pleasure.' The 'holy ones' are the priestly Aaronides (elsewhere מְקֻדָּשִׁים, 'consecrated', and שרי קדש), censured for their aberrations; אדירים are the clan-heads, patrons (Neh 10:21, Jer 14:3) — Aquila ὑπερμεγέθεις μου, 'my superiors'. As a Levite the singer stood under Aaronide authority but renounces their protection, trusting God alone.

Instead of אחר מהרו read אחרים המירו. The first word was emended by predecessors too (Dyserinck: 'foreign gods'), but the verse-part remains unintelligible as long as מהרו is retained; הֵמִיר (still Qal in Aramaic) means 'to exchange, barter' — 'who have bartered other (gods)', cf. ועמי המיר את כבודי בלא יועיל (Jer 2:11).
ירבו עצבותם is ungrammatical as it stands; revocalize the verb (their sufferings will be multiplied for those who barter other gods).
entries.flag: verify the corrected pointing of ירבו at high res

entries.note: The word מדם, which disturbs the connection ('deren Weinspenden ich nicht giessen (vom Blut?)'), is perhaps a dittograph of the ending ־יהם of נסכיהם.
תומיך is a participle, standing for תּוֹמֵךְ ('You hold my lot'). וכוסי = my 'portion, determination', from כסס (see his note at Ps 11:6).
In בנעימים the ב is disturbing — there is no such thing as a ב essentiae. Instead of נחלת read נחלתי ('auch mein Erbtheil mir werth').

All the verbs must be put in future form, matching ישכן: read ישמח לבי and in any case יָגִיל ('Darum ist freudig mein Herz…' as expectation). בשר has poetically also the sense 'being, self', synonymous with נפשי (like Ps 63:2) — not the 'body' that will rest in the grave.
The singular חסידך of the Qere is more correct than the plural Kethib חסידיך.

Instead of בימינך perhaps read בביתך ('Wonnegefühle in Deinem Tempel dauernd'); ארח חיים = ארח לחיים, the way to life here below, not falling prey to death. Of resurrection and a future life there is no trace in this psalm.
ה׳ צדק cannot be said, since this divine name can no more serve as first member of a construct than proper names can; so read ה׳ אלהי צדק, as at Ps 4:2 ('Höre, Herr [Gott] der Gerechtigkeit').
פקד is synonymous with בחן, but combined with לילה gives no sense. Probably read פקדת כליותי 'You have examined my reins', as Ps 26:2 and Job 7:18 ('erforschtest mein Inneres').

בל תמצא זמתי and what follows is deeply obscure. The Greek-Syriac versions and one Targum recension take זמתי as noun (ἀδικία, עול, שחיתא) and תמצא as perfect — against the form and still more the context (it would have to be זִמָּתִי, feminine, incongruent with masculine בל יעבר פי). The Greek versions join this close with the opening of v. 4 לפעלות אדם. One might emend אדם to אדני and read בל יעבר פי לפעלות | אדני בדבר שפתיך, but biblical literature offers no analogy for 'what I planned did not pass into deeds'; Dyserinck's לפעלותי אדם ('at my doing I keep silent') reads too much into אדם. In short, the close of v. 3 and start of v. 4 are dark.
After אני שמרתי one must read מֵאָרְחוֹת פריץ 'I kept myself from the violent man's paths', as the Peshitta (נטרתני מן אורחתא בישתא).

חסדיך is to be emended to the singular חסדך, as the Peshitta. And since חסה is always construed with ב, the word חוסים belongs with בימינך: construe מושיע ממתקוממים חוסים בימינך 'Savior of those who take refuge in Your right hand from adversaries'.
שדוני 'they despoiled me' is too strong, since what follows complains only of cunning ambush; read צָדוּנִי from צדה 'lie in wait' (interchange of ש and צ, Einleitung p. 123).
Read בנפשי (the י absorbed by the following י of יקיפו), like מתקנש בנפשי (1 Sam 28:9): 'my enemies who encircle me for my life'.
חלבמו סגרו is unintelligible; read חֵלֶב לִבָּמוֹ סגרו 'they have closed the fat of their heart' (so also Dyserinck; cf. Hos 13:8 סגור לבם).

אשורנו is untenable if only because the psalmist laments his own suffering alone; hence the Kethib סבבוני is right against סבבונו. The Peshitta's שבחוני points the way (אשרוני 'they praise [themselves] happy' from אשר) — but it fits not as verb, rather as substantive אָשְׁרָם (נו/ם interchange, Einleitung p. 125), joined to the preceding word: בגאות אשרם 'they speak in the pride of their fortune' (closing v. 10); v. 11 then reads much more correctly beginning עתה סבבוני.

לנטות בארץ cannot be right — one does not stretch or incline a snare; the idiom is טמן with רשת or שחת or פח, 'to lay secretly'. Ruin-fragments of that survive in לנטות: read לטמון רשת ('heimlich ein Netz auf den Boden zu legen').
דמינו כאריה simply cannot be said, nor does דמיון occur. LXX ὑπέλαβόν με, i.e. דמוני — דמה in Piel, like זמם, 'to plot ruin against someone': 'they plot against me like a lion lusting for prey'.
Read יכסף as Niphal (לטרף), since כסף occurs only in Niphal.
The Peshitta, more consistent than LXX, has plurals throughout (קדם אפיהון ואכרך אנון… מן רשיעא), i.e. קדמה פנימו והכריעם… מרשעים — since the psalm has spoken of several enemies all along.
The word חרבך does not fit the connection at all; read חרפיך 'those who revile You' ('rette meine Seele von den Frevlern, die Dich lästern').

None of the ancient translators read מְתִים 'men' — all derive the word from מות (Aquila ἀπὸ τεθνηκότων, Symmachus ἀπὸ νεκρῶν, Peshitta, Targum), i.e. ממתים. But that cannot be right either, since the complement חלקם בחיים can only refer to the living. Aramaic מחה/מחא 'strike' passed into Hebrew (distinct from מחה 'wipe'): read מְמֻחִים/מְמֻחָאִים 'the smitten' — ממחים מידך is good Hebrew like מֻכֵּה אלהים (Isa 53:4). And מחלד, smuggled in from Arabic by the commentators, is by no means assured: read מֵחֳלִי — the whole: 'those smitten by Your hand, Lord, those smitten with sickness' ('von Deiner Hand geschlagen, von Krankheit geschlagen').
Instead of the substantive חלקם LXX and Peshitta have the imperative (διαμέτρισον αὐτούς, תפלוג אנון בחייא), i.e. חַלְּקֵם בחיים 'give them a share in life', cf. חלקי בארץ החיים (Ps 142:6).

The Qere צפונך, or with the versions the plural צפוניך, by no means signifies 'hidden treasures' but those sheltered by God, His protégés (cf. Ps 83:4 יתיעצו על צפוניך). בטן has the figurative sense of קרב: תמלא בטנם is epexegetic accusative for תמלא בטן צפוניך ('Deiner Schützlinge Inneres mögest Du sättigen').

אשבעה בהקיץ תמונתך has been claimed as a proof-text for resurrection — by no means: it would offend against כי לא ראיתם כל תמונה (Deut 4:15). LXX ἐν τῷ ὀφθῆναι points to בהביטי, and Peshitta המינותך to אמונתך; the parallelism runs: אני בצדק אחזה פניך / אשבעה בהביטי אמונתך — the close has the same thought as the opening (v. 2).
רחם does not occur in Qal and cannot be said of men toward God; read ארממך 'I will exalt You' (so older commentators and Ewald). To ה׳ חזקי supply ה׳ אלהי חזקי (as at Ps 17:1).
Vv. 2–3 contain a long series of epitheta ornantia — ten in the 2 Sam 22 recension but only eight here; after משגבי must be supplied מנוסי ומושיעי מחמס (from 2 Sam 22:3).
For the tautologous-sounding מפלטי read מפלט לי (likewise Ps 144:2); אלי (Ps 18) is right against אלהי (2 Sam 22) — though perhaps in both read חילי 'my strength'.

entries.emendation: תושיעני ממהללי אקרא ה׳ ומאיבי אשוע
entries.note: The 2 Sam recension has the verb תושיעני, overlooked by commentators though the ancient versions attest it; it must be housed here, together with the difficult מהלל, before which ancient versions and modern commentators stand helpless. Read מְהֹלְלַי 'my mockers' (as Ps 102:9): תושיעני ממהללי אקרא ה׳ — 'Save me from my mockers, I called to the Lord'; correspondingly in b. read ומאיבי אֲשַׁוֵּעַ for אושע. The verbs אקרא and אשוע are historical (narrative) tenses.
V. 5 grounds the helplessness, so כי אפפוני (2 Sam 22) is more correct; also משברי מות ('breakers of death') is more correct than חבלי מות, since חבלי שאול only comes later (v. 6).
In v. 7 אשוע (Ps 18) is obviously more correct than the repeated אקרא (2 Sam), but וישמע (2 Sam) is more correct than ישמע. LXX ἀπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου — 'from the Temple'.
וישת (2 Sam 22) is better than ישת; otherwise the verse must be divided: וישת חשך סתרו סביבותיו / סכתו חשכת מים עבי שחקים. Naturally סכתו חשכת is better than סכות חשרת (2 Sam).

V. 13 is very simple: 2 Sam lacks עביו, while in Ps 18 עברו stands for בערו ('burned'), and for ברד read ברק ('lightning'): 'from the radiance before Him His clouds kindled into lightning and coals of fire' ('entzündeten sich Seine Wolken in Blitz und Feuerkohlen').
In v. 14 ברד וגחלי אש is dittographic (2 Sam 22:14 lacks it); his translation of v. 14 accordingly: 'Es donnerte im Himmel der Herr, der Hohe liess Seine Stimme ertönen.'
entries.flag: the note's recension label (I./II.) is ambiguous — verify at high res

entries.note: ויפיצם cannot refer to enemies — none have yet been mentioned — but to the lightnings; רָב 'hurl' (from רבב/רבה) is lacking in 2 Sam. ויהמם (Ps 18) is the more correct, likewise of the lightnings, from המה 'hum, whir': vocalize 'He made them whir' ('schoss Blitze und liess sie schwirren').
entries.flag: verify proposed pointing of ויהמם at high res

entries.note: Read אפיקי ימים ('the beds of the seas') for מים (Ps 18) / ים (2 Sam) ('Es zeigten sich der Meere Bette').
The second-person suffixes are disturbing in Ps 18 against the third person of 2 Sam 22:16 ('vor dem Drohen Gottes, vor Seines Hauches grimmem Schnauben').
איבי עז is miswritten in both recensions for מאיבי עזים (the מ absorbed by משנאי); so the Peshitta: מן בעלדבבי עשיני ('von gewaltigen Feinden').
גבר (Ps 18) and גבור (2 Sam 22) are both corrupted from נָבָר 'the pure' (cf. v. 27 עם נבר תתברר).
entries.flag: verify which word-position this נבר correction targets at high res

entries.note: המאזרני חיל (Ps 18) is indisputably more correct than מעוזי חיל (2 Sam); conversely ויתר תמים דרכי (2 Sam) is more correct than ויתן (Ps 18) — derived from נתר 'spring', a kind of double accusative: 'He let me spring my way', explained by the following משוה רגלי כאילות; תמים here adverbial, 'unhurt' ('liess meine Bahn unversehrt durcheilen').
Read במות — the י is dittographic ('stellte mich auf Höhen').
ונחת (2 Sam 22) is better than ונחתה — a double accusative: 'He let my arms press down (the bronze bow)', cf. Ps 38:3 ('dass meine Arme den ehrnen Bogen spannen'); נחת Piel = 'bring down under'.
וענותך תרבני is inexplicable, preserved only in Ps 18 — perhaps a dittograph of וימינך תסעדני (Krochmal's וַעֲנָתְךָ disturbs the parallelism).

נתתה (2 Sam) is an affected form. The etymology of צמת is usually given wrongly: it does not originally mean 'silence'; its base meaning is 'bind' (cf. neo-Hebrew צומת הגידין, לצמיתת), then like אלם in Piel 'bind the tongue, make mute' — 'dass ich meine Hasser verstummen machte'. All occurrences can be explained with this sense.
entries.flag: verify the exact lemma re-division (placement of ו) at high res

entries.note: כעפר על פני רוח (Ps 18) is more drastic than כעפר ארץ (2 Sam). אדקם ('I crushed them', 2 Sam) is better than אריקם (Ps 18); the second verb in 2 Sam is dittographic ('zertrat sie wie Strassenkoth').
entries.flag: verify which 2 Sam form (אדקם/ארקעם) he prefers and calls dittographic

entries.note: Ps 18 has עם, 2 Sam עמי; LXX λαῶν = עמים ('von der Völker Fehden'). תשימני (Ps 18) is better than תשמרני (2 Sam).

entries.mt: לְשֵׁמַע אֹזֶן יִשָּׁמְעוּ לִי בְּנֵי־נֵכָר יְכַחֲשׁוּ־לִי
entries.emendation: order per 2 Sam: בני נכר יתכחשו לי, לשמע אזן ישמעו לי
entries.note: The logic of 2 Sam 22:45 (submission first, then obedience) is probably more correct; on the other hand לשמע אזן (Ps 18) is better than לשמוע (2 Sam). ('Söhne der Fremde heuchelten mir, bei des Ohres leisem Hören gehorchten sie mir.')

יבלו is too strong, and יכלו or יפלו no better; read יִלְאוּ 'they grew faint' ('Söhne der Fremde verzagten'). The verb חרג 'tremble' (Ps 18, better than חגר of 2 Sam) is secured by Aramaic חרגא דיומא and occurs at Ps 76:11; Syriac חרג similarly 'be strongly moved'.
Both וידבר (Ps 18) and ומוריד (2 Sam) are miswritten for a form of רדד 'subdue' (cf. Ps 144:2 הרודד עמי תחתי): 'who subdued peoples under me'.
entries.flag: verify the exact form he restores at high res

entries.note: The close (v. 51) is an apology for David's descendants, standing outside all connection with the preceding content — certainly an addition from a later time, like the historical superscription (v. 1). Ps 18 combines two originally distinct psalms (I: vv. 2–29, an Anawite sufferer's thanksgiving; II: vv. 30–50, a victorious hero-king's), each of which lost its own ending/opening in the combination.
קום 'cord, line' sounds strange; קולם 'their voice' lies near (so also Dyserinck) — 'Geht auf der ganzen Erde ihre Stimme aus'.

The verse-final בהם is unintelligible — it cannot refer to שמים, which stands too far off; and on the singer's view the sun has its tent not in heaven but merely traverses the heavenly course. Read לשמש שם אהל בַּיָּם: in the sea the sun has its tent at night, whence it rises in the morning — whence also the idioms בא השמש and מבוא השמש ('da wo Er dem Sonnenball ein Zelt im Meere errichtet').

יראת ה׳ gives no proper sense: this psalm-section stresses throughout the usefulness of God's laws for men, whereas 'fear of God' is man's affair; nor does עמדת לעד rhyme with it — fear of God ought to be constant but is not always. So read אמרת ה׳ 'God's promise' ('Des Herrn Verheissung ist rein, beständig für immer'); טהורה = 'pure', like אמרת ה׳ צרופה.
איתם is miswritten for אתם from תמם ('then I shall be blameless' — 'dann werde ich schuldlos und rein sein von schwerer Sünde').

ידשנה is incorrect in meaning and form: it makes no sense derived from דשן 'fat' or 'sacrificial ashes' — and then the form ידשנה instead of ידשן! So read ירצנה 'may He accept it with favor' (interchanges ד/ר and ש/צ, Einleitung pp. 131, 123).
נדגל is intelligible neither from דגל 'banner' nor from גדל (versions); read נגיל 'we shall rejoice' ('frohlocken').

Vv. 7–9 are not a triumph-song over a victory actually won but an anticipated song for when the enemy shall have been defeated: supply אז נשיר or נזמרה. And for ידעתי read ידענו, since the following verbs are in first person plural (Einleitung pp. 143, 131).
Peshitta ועננהו, i.e. ויענהו, congruent with the perfect הושיע ('Gott Seinem Gesalbten beigestanden, ihn … erhört hat').
LXX render by μεγαλυνθησόμεθα and Peshitta by נתעשן — thus not from זכר; read נגביר 'we prevail' (interchange of ג and ז): 'wir aber sind im Namen des Herrn unseres Gottes siegreich'.

It is awkward to assume a verb עודד — the two parallel passages (Ps 146:9, 147:6) are likewise obscure. Perhaps read ונתעורר 'we are roused, have rallied' ('wir aber erhoben uns und sind erweckt (?)').

V. 10 continues the prayer of vv. 2–4: המלך is accusative, as LXX σῶσον τὸν βασιλέα ('steh' dem König bei'), and for יעננו read the imperative ועננו, LXX ἐπάκουσον ἡμῶν ('erhöre uns am Tage unseres Anrufens').
The Kethib יגיל is more correct than the Qere יגל; מה — מאד is to be taken separated, as interrogative in place of עד מאד ('ob Deiner Hilfe wie sehr wird er frohlocken!').
ארשת can be no correct word; probably read ומשאלת 'and the request (of his lips)'.

LXX ἐν εὐλογίαις, i.e. בברכות. The forms תקדמנו and תשית are perfects without augment-ו — so rightly LXX προέφθασας, ἔθηκας; the verse means this king came unexpectedly to the throne (Hezekiah was Ahaz's younger son, the elder having been sacrificed to Moloch, 2 Kgs 16:3).
לעת פניך gives no sense; read לעמת פניך 'over against Your face' (like Ezek 3:8 לעמת פניהם): 'wie in einem Feuerofen vor Deinem Angesichte'.
מישועתי emended to משיחתי 'from my plaint' (Dyserinck) — 'bist fern von meinem Flehen'; and to דברי שאגתי a מ must be supplied, dependent on רחוק: מדברי ('von … meiner Klage Lauten').
The parallelism requires a verbal form instead of the noun דומיה; the Peshitta (ולא תבתר לי) points that way ('und Du achtest (?) nicht auf mich').
entries.flag: verify the exact Hebrew form he restores at high res

entries.emendation: ואתה קדוש ישב הכרובים נורא תהלות ישראל
entries.note: V. 4 is kept too short and is unintelligible. Exod 15:11 shows נורא תהלות means 'revered in hymns'; so here too supply נורא before תהלות, and to ישב one must absolutely supply הכרובים. The verse thereby gains measure, intelligibility and roundness ('thronend [über den Cherubim,] [verehrt] durch die Lobgesänge Israels').
יפטירו cannot be right, since פטר means only the bursting open of blossom, womb, or at most a spring; read יפערו, as Job 16:10 פערו עלי בפיהם (interchange of ט and ע): 'sperren den Mund auf'.
גל can only be third person of גלל 'roll' (not imperative); supply דרכו: 'He rolled (his way/destiny) upon God — let Him rescue him' ('Er hat Gott sein (Geschick) gewälzt, mag Er ihn retten').
אתה גחי מבטן, just like Ps 71:6 ממעי אמי אתה גוזי — both words inexplicable, both miswritten for the same word ('Denn Du bist meine Macht von Mutterleib').
entries.flag: verify the restored word (עזי?) at high res

entries.note: Instead of מבטיחי read מִבְטַחִי 'my trust' ('meine Zuversicht an meiner Mutterbrust').
For כחי scholars as early as the Gaonic age (10th century) made the emendation חכי 'my palate' (see Ibn Ezra ad loc.): 'trocken wie Scherben mein Gaumen'.

That מלקוחי means 'palate' is unproven, and the preposition אל or ל to דבק is missing. More correct is Menachem b. Saruk's explanation מלקוחים 'fangs', metonym for teeth; read ולשוני מדבק מלקוחי (or מדבקים, the מ absorbed homoeoarctically): 'an meiner Zunge kleben meine Zähne'.

ולעפר … תשפתני cannot be right, for שפת means only to set the pot on the hearth (Isa 26:12 תשפת שלום is itself a corruption). The Peshitta translates שריתני, i.e. תַּשְׁלִיכֵנִי 'You have cast me into the dust of death'.
LXX κύνες πολλοί — 'zahlreiche Hunde', as v. 13 פרים רבים.

כארי is the notorious dogmatic and exegetical crux interpretum. The converted Masora-collector Jacob b. Chajim claimed to have found the note כתיב כארו וקרי כארי (Masora finalis, s.v. ארי); Heidenheim too records the variant. LXX ὤρυξαν 'they pierced' proves nothing, coming decidedly from a Christian hand to support Jesus' crucifixion from the psalm. But Aquila's first edition ᾔσχυναν ('they disfigured' = כערו) attests the plural verb reading כארו in the early 2nd century, as does the Midrash to Psalms; the later Targum already has כארי. Even כרו could only mean 'dig a pit', never 'pierce'. In his second edition (κατ᾿ ἀκρίβειαν) Aquila rendered 'they bound' (Syro-Hexapla: פכרו אידי ורגלי), followed by Symmachus and even Jerome (vinxerunt): they had before them a codex reading אָסְרוּ — and this is the most correct reading, later corrupted into כארו and כארי: אסרו ידי ורגלי 'they bound my hands and feet' is certainly true to the text (so Dyserinck; Krochmal's כאבו does not fit).
אספר כל עצמותי, 'counting one's bones', is nonsense. The Targum has 'wounds' (הלבשושי), as Ps 147:3 מחבש לעצבותם: read עצבותי 'my pains' ('Zähle ich alle meine Schmerzen auf').

אילותי is a non-word without analogy. The Peshitta has the verse longer: ואנת מריא לא תרחק מני… אילי אילי לעודרני כתר, i.e. אל תרחק ממני אלי אלי אהה לעזרתי חושה (cf. Ps 71:12): 'mein Gott bist Du, eile mir zu Hilfe!'
entries.flag: verify the exact restored wording at high res

entries.note: מחרב does not fit the context at all — sooner מחרפי; but the parallelism with כלב requires מִפָּרִים 'from bulls' (as v. 13; interchange of ח and פ, Einleitung p. 135): 'Rette von Stieren meine Seele, von Hunden mein Leben!'
יחידתי (also Ps 35:17) is only forcedly explained as 'soul'; read חיתי 'my life'.
עניתני is disturbing, since the imperative/imperfect is required; perhaps miswritten for תענני, or better still a form matching his translation 'steh' mir bei' (cf. his note to Ps 23:5).
entries.flag: verify the 'noch besser' alternative form at high res

entries.note: No exegete's art can explain מאתך תהלתי; read אמתך 'Your faithfulness is my praise' (perhaps likewise Ps 71:6 בך תהלתי): 'Deiner Treu gilt mein Loblied'.

The second person in לבבכם shows that the first half-verse must also have stood congruently in second person — imperatives: 'Geniesset, ihr Sanftmüthigen, und sättigt euch, preiset den Herrn.' From here begins the song of praise vowed for the time of rescue, reaching to the psalm's end.
V. 29 is too short. LXX καὶ αὐτὸς δεσπόζει, i.e. והוא מֹשֵׁל ('und Er ist Herrscher über die Völker').

אכלו וישתחוו is the crassest nonsense — eating and prostrating oneself before God! Yet all the commentators let it pass. Simply read אַךְ לוֹ for אכלו (so also Pinsker and Krochmal): 'Ja, Ihm werden sich beugen alle Starken der Erde.' דשני ארץ needs no emendation — it equals משמנים, 'the magnates, opulent ones'.
ונפשו לא חיה is inexplicable; perhaps read ונפש כל חי ('und die Seelen aller Lebenden (?)').

entries.emendation: זרע עבדיו יְסַפְּרוּ פָּעַל אדני לדור יבא
entries.note: V. 31 is also incorrect. The Targum hints at a correct text (זרעא דאברהם יפלחון קדמיו ויחוון כח גבורתא דה׳ לדרא בתראה); to restitute it compare Ps 71:18b and Ps 69:37 (וזרע עבדיו). The Targum had active יספרו for יְסֻפַּר, and before לאדני a construct noun: זרע עבדיו יספרו פעל אדני לדור יבא — 'Die Nachkommen seiner Knechte werden Gottes That dem zukünftigen Geschlechte erzählen' (drawing יבאו from v. 32 to this verse).

With יבאו drawn to the preceding verse, only ויגידו צדקתו לעם נולד remains; and to כי עשה LXX (ἐποίησεν ὁ κύριος) and Peshitta (דעבד מריא) add the subject: כי עשה ה׳, as Ps 118:24, Isa 44:23 — unless one emends to הושע or supplies ישועה elliptically, as the Targum (עבד פורקן) — 'dass der Herr Grosses gethan'.
ינחמני 'comfort me' is unsuitable here of rod and staff; read ינחוני 'they lead me' ('Dein Stab und Deine Stütze würden mich führen').
The perfect דשנת is miswritten for the future תדשן ('salben mit Oel mein Haupt' — the whole verse is conditional-future like the context).
Peshitta דאעמר, i.e. וישבתי 'and I shall dwell in the house of the Lord' ('ich werde im Tempel Gottes auf lange Tage weilen').

The Qere נפשי is more correct than the Kethib נפשו, although all the versions presuppose the latter: נשא לשוא נפש parallels לא תשא את שמי לשוא, and שוא 'the false' (= μάταια) means idols, as does מרמה — so נשבע למרמה is intelligible: 'to swear by the delusive image'. Were it simply 'swear falsely', it would sound strange that mere freedom from perjury should qualify one before God; rather it excludes those who practiced idolatry in Babylonia (Isa 65:11 ff.).
Before יעקב LXX and Peshitta have אלהי, which is necessary ('die Dich anbeten, Gott Jakobs').

After זה must be supplied הוא as in v. 10; and to גבור supply מלחמה, which is executed palilogically at the verse's close. מלך הכבוד is the Ark of the Covenant, from which God reveals himself (Exod 25:22) — hence carried into war until Josiah abolished the practice (2 Chr 35:3).
ושאו must be read as in v. 7, והנשאו, following the versions ('erhebet euch, ihr ewigen Pforten').
To ה׳ צבאות one must always supply (since ה׳ cannot stand in construct) ה׳ אלהי צבאות ישראל; ה׳ צבאות is to be viewed only as an ellipse ('Der Herr der Heerschaaren (Israels)').
The seemingly missing ב of the acrostic is still recognizable if one transposes אלהי בך to בך אלהי (Hupfeld).
הבוגדים רקם is unintelligible; read ריקים, as Jer 14:3 (שבו כליהם ריקם = ריקים). The construction is הבוגדים ריקים with ריקים as subject ('die leichtsinnigen Abtrünnigen').

entries.emendation: insert a ו half-verse, e.g. [ואל תבישני נגד איבי כי] אותך קויתי
entries.note: ו is so extraordinarily easy an acrostic letter that the singer cannot have neglected it; rather v. 5 (ה) must be divided and a half-verse beginning with ו inserted between, roughly: 'lass mich nicht beschämt werden vor meinen Feinden, denn auf Dich hoffe ich' (Hupfeld's proposed supplement is little plausible).
To מעולם supply עד עולם, as Ps 103:17 ('die da für immer sind').

The emphasis of אתה is superfluous here; probably read עתה 'remember me now' (on the interchange of אתה and עתה cf. Frankel-Graetz Monatsschrift 1880, p. 39 ff.) — 'denke mein jetzt um Deiner Güte willen'.
Twice ענוים in the same verse is too much; for the second the Peshitta has מסכנא, i.e. אביונים ('lehrt die Dulder Seine Wege'). ידרך has ê for יַדְרִיךְ by assonance with וילמד.
The ו of ובריתו is a dittograph from ליראיו; the sense: בריתו להודיעם 'his covenant — to make it known to them'. סוד means also 'intimate intercourse' (Prov 3:32, Job 19:19).
יחיד ועני gives no sense; read חסיד ועני, as Ps 86:2 ('denn fromm und elend bin ich').

צרות לבבי הרחיבו is unintelligible; Hupfeld's emendation is not plausible. LXX ἐπληθύνθησαν and Peshitta סגי point to רבו — the ה of הרחיבו is the ruin-fragment of הנה, and the ח slipped in thoughtlessly ('Meines Herzens Qualen sind gross').

entries.graetz_verse: cited as V. 15/17 in his notes
entries.note: The acrostic ק is still recognizable in the doubled ר (vv. 18–19); probably read קְשׁוֹב עניי 'attend to my misery' (קשב occurs in Qal too) — the ראה is dittographic from the following verse.
entries.flag: notes cite this under two different verse numbers — verify at high res

entries.note: Read חנם for חמס: 'they hate me without cause' ('ohne Grund hassen sie mich').
The close with פדה (outside the acrostic) was added later, when the psalm — though markedly individual — was put to liturgical use; cf. Ps 130:8 והוא יפדה את ישראל.

נעלמים cannot mean 'the deceitful' in living usage; from עלם 'veil' one says rather 'veiled, mournful, languishing' (Nah 3:11). The word is probably corrupt — perhaps read a word for 'revelers' ('mit Ausgelassenen (?) ging ich nicht um'), cf. Jer 15:17 בסוד משחקים ואעלז.
entries.flag: verify the proposed form (נעלזים?) and the interchange he cites at high res

entries.note: צרי ואיבי לי is tautological and insipid; read צרי יארבו לי 'my adversaries lie in wait for me' ('meine Feinde mir auflauern'). The very alternation of perfect and imperfect points to hypothesis (vv. 2–3 are conditional).
בזאת leaves the sense indeterminate; perhaps read ביהוה ('bin ich in dem Herrn sicher').

Much untenable has been said about לבקר; the parallel 2 Kgs 16:15 יהיה לי לבקר must be read להקריב = לקרב — so here too לְקָרֵב בהיכלו 'to offer sacrifice in His temple'. The singer was of Aaron's line, as v. 6 also indicates.

בצור ירוממני is vacuous on the common explanation and stands in poetic contradiction to the preceding wish to dwell in His tent; read מצוררי ירוממני 'He will lift me above my adversaries', like Ps 18:49 מן קמי תרוממני ('vor meinen Feinden wird Er mich erhöhen').

This defies all artificial exegesis and makes emendation imperative (the LXX reading does not fit either). To לך supply קול — קולך — and emend לבי to לנו: קולך אמר לנו בקשו פני, 'Your word said to us: seek My face' — קול construed with אמר/הגיד passes from 'voice' into 'command, word' (cf. Eccl 5:5); בקש פני ה׳ is used in later writings for התהלך את ה׳ (Ps 105:4).
אבי ואמי עזבוני points to an accomplished fact, and LXX have the perfect προσελάβετό με for וה׳ יאספני, i.e. אספני ('aber der Herr hat mich aufgenommen').

יפיח/יפח is everywhere a verb (an eased pronunciation of יפח, from פוח/פיח, like πνέω 'breathe out, speak' — clearly in Prov 6:19, 14:5). And חמס means, besides 'violence', also 'falsehood' = שקר (עד חמס like עד שקר; Prov 16:29). So here, beside קמו בי עדי שקר, read the verb ויפיחו with חמס; the missing object-pronoun lurks in the pointed לולא of v. 13 — detach לו and draw it to this verse: ויפיחו חמס לי 'and they breathe out falsehood against me' (so still the Greek translator: ἐψεύσατο ἡ ἀδικία ἑαυτῇ = לה; naturally read לי).

entries.emendation: לא (after לו is drawn to v. 12)
entries.note: V. 13 accordingly begins with לא and is negative: לא האמנתי לראות בטוב ה׳ 'I should not have trusted to see the Lord's goodness in the land of the living…'. Since לו had coalesced with לא, the Masoretes could make nothing of it and set the (extraordinary) points above it to hint it seemed superfluous (cf. Einleitung p. 106). בארץ חיים: the Talmudists rightly recognized the Holy Land here.

יהרסם ולא יבנם does not fit the context at all, even if one emends to the second person with LXX (καθελεῖς … καὶ οὐ μὴ οἰκοδομήσεις). There seems to be a gap here in which buildings were spoken of, as in Isa 5:9 (his translation marks the lacuna: '.... Er wird sie niederreissen und nicht mehr aufbauen').

For ויעלז לבי — which the Greek and Syriac versions do not have — there stands ἀνέθαλεν ἡ σάρξ μου, Peshitta ישוח בסרי, i.e. ויפרח בשרי 'my flesh blossoms' ('[blüht mein Leib]'). Was this perhaps ousted by the similar-sounding משירי that follows?
For משירי the Peshitta has בשירי (as Ps 69:31), and Symmachus ἐν ᾠδαῖς, plural בשירַי: 'with my song(s) I thank Him'.

For למו LXX have τοῦ λαοῦ αὐτοῦ, likewise the Peshitta, i.e. לעמו, as Ps 29:11: 'Der Herr ist Macht für Sein Volk'. (Vv. 8–9 are a later parallelistic close appended to nationalize the individual psalm, like Ps 25:22.)

entries.emendation: supply e.g. ויאירו ברקים תבל / וברקים בערו ממנו
entries.note: V. 7 appears too short against the rest; it is probably lacunose — to be supplied roughly with 'and lightnings lit up the world' or 'and lightnings burned from it' (his translation: 'Die Stimme des Herrn schlug Feuerflammen …').

אילות are probably rather trees (singular אֵלָה — אַיָּלָה), and יחולל from חלל 'wound, strike down', as some commentators explain — better than the far-fetched idea 'brings the hinds to calving' ('Die Stimme des Herrn schlug Terebinthen nieder'). ישרות is poetic plural of יער, or miswritten for יערים.
The participle אמר must be read יאמר (the י absorbed by the ו in כלו): 'in His temple all shall say: Glory!' — repeating the thought of v. 2.
To ישב supply על כסא קדשו (Ps 47:9) — 'The Lord sat (on His throne) at the Flood'; and for וישב read the future וְיֵשֵׁב with the versions (καθιεῖται): 'sitzen wird der Herr als König für immer'.
V. 11 is general and without connection of thought to the preceding — probably a later addition (an epiphonema to nationalize the psalm), like Ps 28:8–9.

The Kethib מיורדי בור is grammatically more correct than the Qere מירדי, which would be a wholly unusual infinitive of ירד (it would have to be מרדתי, as v. 10). The sense: from the 'dead', synonymous with שאול — appropriate only of the nation, not an individual ('mich aus Gruftgesenkten auferstehen lassen').

רגע and חיים are supposed to be antitheses like באפו and ברצונו, which does not work. LXX have ὀργή for רגע, i.e. גערה 'rebuke' ('Anfahren in Seinem Zorn'); but חיים does not fit well either — perhaps read חן ('favor in His goodwill').
entries.flag: verify both proposed forms at high res

entries.note: V. 8 as transmitted is unintelligible, and העמדתה להררי is incorrect — one cannot bring a firm mountain to a standstill. Read הִמְעַדְתָּה from מעד 'totter' (as he emends Ezek 29:7, Dan 11:4, Hos 10:9); but then for ברצונך one must read בחרונך: 'Herr, in Deinem Unwillen hast Du meinen festen Berg wankend gemacht.'

כבוד is certainly wrong. LXX ἡ δόξα μου = כבודי — but that reading cannot be right either, for 'my honor will sing' is without analogy (one does not say נפשי תזמר either). So for כבוד(י) read כנורי 'my harp': 'Damit meine Harfe Dir spiele und nicht schweige.'
After פלטני supply הצילני, following Ps 71:2 (the openings of Pss 31 and 71 are identical) — 'befreie und rette mich!'

פדיתה אותי cannot be right, since the form would speak of an accomplished fact not to be surmised from the preceding. Read ופדיתה אותי (the ו ousted by the preceding letter) as precative perfect: 'und Du wirst mich erlösen, Gott der Treue'.

הבלי שוא is idolatry (cf. Einleitung p. 41 n.), and the verse grounds the confidence of rescue; perhaps read שָׂנֵאתָ 'You hate those who wait upon vain idols' (Dyserinck) — 'Du hassest, die auf eitle Götzen warten'.

entries.emendation: supply a verb, e.g. דבקו לעפר
entries.note: עששה suits עיני (as Ps 6:8) but not נפשי ובטני; a verb must be supplied, roughly דבקו לעפר ('meine Seele und mein Leib (kleben am Boden)').

The verb עשש 'grow dim' does not suit 'bones' here either (cf. at v. 10); read יבשו 'meine Gebeine sind vertrocknet'. (בעוני he retains: the stress on grief and sighs refers to the feeling of sin-guilt, עון interchanging with חטאת.)
LXX παρά, i.e. בכל: 'bei allen meinen Widersachern ward ich zur Schmach'.

The following לשכני מאד seems insipid. Hitzig's emendation מגוד is wrong (it would have to be מנוד ראש), as is Krochmal's מגור; so read מאום 'an abhorrence to my neighbors' (interchange of ד and ם, Einleitung p. 127) — 'meinen Nachbarn zum Abscheu'.
בהוסדם is wrong; read בהועדם 'as they conspire together' — ס and ע were interchanged (cf. Einleitung pp. 134, 157; so too at Ps 2:2).
'My times are in Your hand' is nonsense; emend to עזרתי (cf. his note at Ps 9:10 לעזרת): 'In Deiner Hand ist meine Hilfe, so rette mich'.
entries.flag: verify the emended word at high res

entries.note: ידמו לשאול is harsh and untranslatable; read ירדו 'let them go down to Sheol' ('zur Gruft fahren!').

מרכסי is hard to explain from the root רכס; and איש is not correct — LXX and Peshitta have the plural (ἀπὸ ταραχῆς ἀνθρώπων, דבני אנשא), so read בני איש, like בני אדם earlier ('vor vornehmen Rotten (?)').
For בסכה perhaps read כסכה 'as in a shelter'.
entries.flag: verify the compared/emended preposition at high res

entries.note: בעיר מצור is unintelligible if pointing to a fact. Symmachus ὡς ἐν πόλει = כעיר, and for מצור read מבצר, as Ps 108:11 (parallel 60:11): 'as in a fortified city' — image of impregnability (Jer 1:18) — 'wie in einer wehrgeschützten Stadt'.
נגרזתי might just pass like Lam 3:54; but in combination with מנגד עיניך read נגרשתי, as Jonah 2:5 — the fragment to which v. 7 here also has a parallel ('ich bin vor Deinen Augen verbannt').
To משכיל supply למנצח (cf. Einleitung p. 82): 'Dem kunstverständigen (Chorführer)'.
בשאגתי is not quite fitting — why the roaring? Rather read בשגגתי 'through my (inadvertent) sin' ('morschten meine Gebeine in Folge meines Vergehens täglich').

עון חטאתי is an idle pleonasm, and סלה twice in immediate succession; so read ואתה נשאת עוני וחטאתי סלחתה — 'You forgave my guilt and pardoned my sin' ('Du verziehest meine Schuld, vergabest mein Fehlen').

רק is disturbing in this context. Noting that צ and ק were interchanged (Einleitung p. 127), an excellent sense results reading לעת מצא רצון: Deutero-Isaiah calls the time of approaching decision through Cyrus שנת רצון (61:2) and עת רצון (49:8; cf. 55:6 דרשו ה׳ בהמצאו); the exilic Pss 69:14 and 106:4 likewise name this 'time of favor'. The emendation yields the exact parallel between this psalm and Ps 69 ('in gewärtiger Gnadenzeit'). The following לשטף is absolute: 'at the cataclysm' (Dan 9:26, Nah 1:8), מים רבים its subject.

רני פלט is inexplicable, even if with Hitzig one deletes רני as dittography of תצרני — פלט would then have no support and the verse would be too short. Perhaps read בצור מפלט תסובבני ('mit Fels sicherer Zuflucht schütze mich!').
איעצה עליך עיני is deeply obscure, and Dyserinck's emendation איעצך avails nothing, since עליך and עיני remain inexplicable ('will rathen, auf dich mein Auge (?)').
The plural אל תהיו cannot be maintained, since what follows is singular: read אל תהי; and for אין הבין read אין בינה 'without understanding'.

עדיו is inexplicable. Peshitta מכבשין 'bind' points to ענד 'bind' (Prov 6:21) — perhaps עֶנְדּוֹ, with לבלום (Syriac בלם) 'to muzzle'. And since בל does not occur with the infinitive, read בלי קרב. The sense: as the wild horse and mule must be tamed for lack of insight, so must the sinner be tamed by pains — better to forestall this by repentance.

V. 11 has no proper connection with the psalm's content but sounds just like v. 1 of the following psalm: it appears to have been assigned to Ps 32 by oversight and belongs rather to Ps 33 (which lacks any superscription — Origen and Eusebius attest that LXX, Aquila and Theodotion had none; the dislocation arose from that). והרנינו is Hiphil, so transitive: 'make others too shout for joy', as Aquila αἰνοποιήσατε.
Read בנבל ועשור — two different instruments (cf. Einleitung p. 68): 'mit der Nabla und der Zehnsaite spielet ihm!'

כנד is merely miswritten for כנאד or כנוד 'like a water-skin' (Ewald and others); correspondingly one must also read כְּאוֹצָרוֹת 'as in storehouses' — the sea-floods gathered and enclosed in the sea-bed as in containers ('Er sammelt wie in einen Schlauch die Meeresgewässer, legt wie in Schatzkammern die Fluthen').

The superscription בשנותו את טעמו לפני אבימלך is historically incorrect (the king before whom David feigned madness was Achish of Gath, 1 Sam 21). Therefore leg. אכיש מלך (Krochmal); his translation: 'vor Achisch, König [der Philister]'.

LXX and Peshitta render these verbs as 2nd-person imperatives (προσέλθατε … καὶ φωτίσθητε καὶ τὰ πρόσωπα ὑμῶν; Pesh. חורו לותה וסברו בה ואפיכם) — so vocalize as imperatives and read ופניכם for ופניהם. He adds that נהר 'shine' is Aramaic and only late (Deutero-Isaiah, Job); older Hebrew נהר = 'stream, surge'.

In the alphabetic acrostic the verse beginning with ו is evidently missing — a verse starting with ו would be 'child's play' to form, so a lacuna must be assumed (cf. p. 236), hence the abrupt transition from v. 6 to v. 7. The lost verse seems to have recounted an event from the singer's life, danger and rescue. זה in זה עני is deictic, not demonstrative-topical.
קדושיו would properly mean His 'priests'; therefore leg. דורשיו 'those who seek Him' — matching v. 11 ודרשי ה׳ and his translation 'Verehret den Herrn, ihr, die ihr Ihn aufsuchet'.

מי is indefinite (cf. p. 238) but the construction is anacoluthic: after לכו בנים (v. 12) the 2nd person plural should follow; the acrostic compulsion to form a מ-verse caused the shift, and the singular persists in the following verses. Vielleicht leg. מי אתה האיש. Content parallels Prov 4:10.

צעקו וה׳ שמע (v. 18) does not follow v. 17 (about evildoers) but fits v. 16 (God's regard for the pious): vv. 16 and 17 are evidently transposed. The dislocation arose from the wavering order of פ and ע in the alphabet — Lam 2, 3, 4 (and originally this psalm) put פ before ע, while Lam 1, Prov 31, Pss 111, 112, 145, 25 have ע before פ. Original order: פ פני ה׳ בעשי רע (17), ע עיני ה׳ אל צדיקים ואזניו אל שועתם (16), צ צעקו וה׳ שמע (18). His translation prints 17 before 16.

entries.emendation: יאשמו = zerdehnte form of יֵשַׁמּוּ (from שמם)
entries.note: The etymology of יאשמו is still misjudged and derived from אשם 'be guilty', whereas it can only come from שמם 'be desolate' — how else explain נאשמו עדרי צאן (Joel 1:18)? From שמם also האשם שמרון (Hos 14:1) and ויאשמו מזבחותיכם (Ezek 6:6). It is the stretched form of יֵשַׁמּוּ; his translation: 'die Feinde des Gerechten werden verödet'. Parallel Prov 1:32, 5:22.
The last verse, standing outside the acrostic, is a liturgical addition (cf. p. 236, 269); his translation sets it off after asterisks.

סגר cannot be a verb but is a substantive parallel to מגן וצנה in v. 2 (those defend, חנית וסגר attack). Following Drusius and Hugo Grotius it is now generally taken as the Scythian weapon σάγαρις, the two-edged battle-axe (Herodotus I.215), known in Babylonia after the Scythian invasion — a dating clue for the psalm's exilic origin. But then the verb הרק cannot apply, since it is used only of the sword ('empty the sheath', i.e. draw). Daher leg. הָרֵם: 'Erhebe Speer und Streitbeil'.
LXX add the pronoun αὐτούς — i.e. דֹּחָם 'driving them' (like רוֹדְפָם v. 6); a frequent confusion of ה and ם (cf. p. 132: בָּם = בָּהּ). Translation: 'ein Engel des Herrn sie dränge'.

entries.emendation: רשתם with טמנו; שחת with חפרו
entries.note: שחת רשתם do not belong together; one of the two words strayed from the lower line into the upper (so already older interpreters). Translation: 'ihr Netz gelegt … eine Grube für mich gegraben'.

entries.mt: תְּבוֹאֵהוּ שׁוֹאָה לֹא־יֵדָע וְרִשְׁתּוֹ אֲשֶׁר־טָמַן תִּלְכְּדוֹ בְּשׁוֹאָה יִפָּל־בָּהּ
entries.emendation: תבואם שואה לא ידעו ורשתם אשר טמנו תלכדם ושוחה יפלו בה
entries.note: The singular is incongruent — the whole psalm speaks of several enemies. LXX and Peshitta rightly have plurals throughout (ἐλθέτω αὐτοῖς … οὐ γινώσκουσι … ἔκρυψαν, συλλαβέτω αὐτούς … πέσονται). For the second בשואה, 'pit', leg. בשוחה with the Peshitta (וגומצא דחפרין נפלון בה). The whole verse must be emended accordingly.

The word עני twice in the same verse is one too many; the second is to be struck. גזל here can only mean 'deal violently', as the Peshitta rightly renders with the addition חטף בקטירא 'seize with violence'.
עדי חמס are 'false witnesses' (p. 245); but witnesses hold no interrogation, that they should 'question' me! ישאלוני ist wohl dittographirt statt ישלמוני (anticipating ישלמוני רעה v. 12).

entries.emendation: כשול לנפשי (+ supply a verb, e.g. נתנו)
entries.note: שכול 'childlessness' is nonsense here, and substituting 'orphaning' is too meagre a makeshift. Targum מתקל ('stumbling-block'), similarly Peshitta (ואבדו נפשי מן בנינשא) — i.e. כשול. The second half-verse is moreover too short and disturbs the psalm's elegant parallelism; a verb must be supplied (e.g. נתנו: 'legen meiner Seele einen Fallstrick').
entries.flag: verify proposed reading כשול and supplied verb at high res (pdf 292-293)

entries.emendation: ותפלתי על חיותי (ת from תשוב drawn back; תשוב → שומם to v. 14)
entries.note: ותפלתי על חיקי תשוב is inexplicable and certainly badly corrupted; vielleicht leg. ותפלתי על חיותי 'my prayer was for their recovery' — the ת taken from the following word, חיקי = חַיָּתִי (matching his translation 'in meinem Gebet für ihre Genesung'). The word תשוב (or its remainder שוב) belongs to v. 14 — for what should התהלכתי mean without an adverb? — and is a corruption of שומם 'verödet' (desolate): the whole reads שומם כרע כאח לי התהלכתי ('Ging verstört als Freund oder Bruder umher').
entries.flag: verify חיותי and the reconstructed v.14 opening at high res

entries.emendation: שַׁחְתִּי (from שוח 'lament'); כרע effectively plural (Pesh. להם)
entries.note: Striking that the plural כְּרֵעִים is not used, since a plurality is always in view; hence the Peshitta's rendering איך רחמא 'as were I a friend', i.e. להם. The לי belongs to the verb (לי התהלכתי). And שחותי is wrongly vocalized: קדר already means 'gloomy' (קדורנית), so the verb does not suit or is tautologous; daher leg. שַׁחְתִּי from שוח 'lament, mourn' ('klagte wie in Trauer um eine Mutter').
entries.flag: verify pointing of שחתי at high res

entries.note: נכים is unintelligible; leg. נָכְרִים 'strangers', with ולא ידעתי added — like אשר לא ידעתי: 'es rotteten sich Fremde zusammen, mir Unbekannte'. He distinguishes צלע 'limp' from צלע 'rib' (against Hupfeld's conflation; Arabic and Syriac keep the stems apart).
קרעו ('they tore') is unintelligible; leg. קראו 'they cried out' (so also Dyserinck) — a confusion of ע and א (cf. p. 125, 6): 'riefen laut und hörten nicht auf'.

בחנפי לעגי מעוג is unintelligible even through artificial exegesis. LXX point to the right reading: ἐπείρασάν με, ἐξεμυκτήρισάν με μυκτηρισμόν — 'they tested me and mocked me (with mockery)', a confusion of מ and ל (cf. p. 134, 12). Translation: 'Sie prüften mich und spotteten höhnisch'.
entries.flag: verify exact Hebrew wording of proposed reading at high res

entries.note: משאיהם is unintelligible; leg. משאגתם 'from their roaring' (Dyserinck): 'entziehe meine Seele von ihrem Wuthschrei'. מכפירים = 'the mighty' (cf. p. 271 f.).
יחידתי is unintelligible; leg. חיתי 'my life' (cf. p. 229): 'von Gewaltigen mein Leben'.
The רגעי ארץ are the ענוי ארץ, the humble/poor of the land (cf. p. 21); translation 'über die Ruhigen des Landes' keeps the sense.

entries.emendation: Niphal הֵעָרָה; before לריבי supply a verb (קומה or רומה; Pesh. והביטה)
entries.note: העירה would be transitive, hence to be read as Niphal. Before לריבי a verb is missing to complete the parallelism — roughly קומה or רומה; the Peshitta has וחזי, i.e. והביטה. His translation marks the gap: 'mein Herr....zu meiner Vertheidigung'.
entries.flag: verify Niphal form and suggested verbs at high res

entries.note: האח נפשנו is obscure; the Peshitta (ראתניחת נפשן) points to a form of נוח — etwa Hophal הוּנְחָה: 'beruhigt ist unsere Gier'.
To המגדילים supply פיהם 'who make their mouth great against me' — 'die stolz gegen mich sprachen'.

יגדל (Qal) is too weak; LXX μεγαλυνθείη ('may He be magnified'), i.e. יֻגְדַּל: 'verherrlicht möge der Herr werden'. From החפץ שלום עבדו he infers the psalmist was a person of standing; since the same verse closes Ps 40 (v. 17) and Ps 70 (v. 5) without this addition, those psalms borrowed from this one and are younger.

In the second half-verse the parallelism is not carried through; hence supply ופי יגיד — his translation: 'meine Zunge wird Deine Gerechtigkeit aussprechen, (mein Mund verkünden) alle Tage Deinen Preis'.

נאם פשע is a combination impossible in Hebrew. Leg. נעים, and instead of לבי the older versions have לבו: 'Süss ist die Sünde dem Frevler im Innersten seines Herzens' (cf. Monatsschrift 1881, p. 529 f.).

החליק is transitive, its subject the preceding אלהים; בעיניו refers to the evildoer — 'it seems to him' that God has nothing against him (like Jer 12:1–2). The second half-verse למצא עונו לשנא is so obscure it drives interpreters to despair. Acceptable is the emendation: supply חדל before למצא (as in v. 4, Hupfeld) and for עונו לשנא leg. עון לשונו (Dyserinck), like פימו חטאת — 'Er unterlässt das Unheil seiner Zunge zu finden'.
בהשמים leg. כהשמים, as with the following nouns (v. 7 כהררי אל, כתהום): 'dess Gnade weit wie die Himmel'.
Read כתהום רבה — the כ fell out after the preceding ך of משפטיך; LXX ὡσεὶ ἄβυσσος. He adds משפטים here cannot mean 'punishments' but 'laws, ordinances', synonymous with צדקה.
תושיע 'help' cannot well be joined with בהמה; leg. תשביע 'satisfy, feed' — his translation: 'der Du Menschen und Thiere sättigst'.
entries.flag: verify exact form (תשבע/תשביע) — OCR ambiguous at page break 296/297

entries.note: ובני אדם claims too much — by no means do all men seek God's protection or long for the sanctuary, only the particular class named further on (ידעי ה׳, ישרי לב), i.e. the ענוים and אביונים (p. 21). Daher nothwendigerweise leg. בני אביון statt בני אדם (p. 144g), as Ps 72:4.
entries.flag: verify proposed lemma (בני אביון?) at high res

entries.note: ירוין and תשקם are jussive or precative — 'mögen sich laben' ('O mögen sie sich an Deines Tempels Fülle laben'). דשן is metaphorical 'abundance' (Ps 65:12, Isa 55:2, Jer 31:14), not sacrificial fat; רוה is used only of drink. נחל עדנך is the Eden-stream issuing from the Temple as in Ezek 47.

entries.emendation: plural suffixes per Peshitta; תבואני → תבוסנו
entries.note: The singular (תבואני, תנדני) jars against the preceding plural; leg. plural with the Peshitta (לא תאתא עלין רגלא …). And since תבוא does not really suit רגל, for תבואני leg. תבוסנו 'trample us' (p. 130h): 'Dass uns nicht des Hochmuths Fuss trete'.
entries.flag: verify proposed forms תבוסנו/תנדנו at high res

entries.emendation: — (lacuna before v. 13; supply e.g. ונודה את שמך)
entries.note: This abrupt verse presupposes a lacuna — a song of thanks depicting the fall of the wicked, as Ps 9:21 and often. Roughly to be supplied: ונודה את שמך. The adverb שם has temporal force, 'da, damals'; his translation sets v. 13 in quotation marks after a break.

entries.emendation: שכן (imperat. with future sense) ארץ, וּרְעֵה [אותה] — 'pasture on it'; אמונה adverbial = באמונה
entries.note: V. 3 has been completely misunderstood. שכן ארץ is imperative after the imperatives בטח and עשה, with future force; likewise רעה = 'graze off, nourish oneself from it' (ירעו בשן Mic 7:14; Jer 50:19), object ארץ. אמונה is accusative of respect = באמונה 'in faithfulness and permanence' (Ps 119:75), so rightly Symmachus. שכן ארץ = ירש ארץ (vv. 9, 22, 29, 34), i.e. repossess the land — return from exile (Isa 65:9): 'so wirst du das Heimland bewohnen und es pflegen: treulich!'

entries.emendation: הוֹחֵל / הִתְיַחֵל ('hope'); LXX/Pesh. rather התפלל לו
entries.note: LXX and Symmachus ἱκέτευσον, Peshitta צלא קדמוהי 'implore' — that would be התפלל לו or הַתְחַלֵּה (from חלה פנים); Aquila ἀποκαραδόκει and Targum אוריך 'hope' — that would be הוחל or התיחל, favored by the parallel Lam 3:25–26 (ויחיל ודומם). The required second stich of the ד-distich begins with אל תתחר (the acrostic is distichic).

אך להרע is unintelligible; leg. אף (p. 129), but then the infinitive is unsuitable — read בָּרָע: 'not even over the evil one' ('ereifere dich auch nicht über den Bösewicht'), resuming the thought of v. 1.
entries.flag: verify proposed reading (אף ברע) at high res — OCR garbled

entries.note: Statt מהמון leg. מהון 'than the wealth of' (Krochmal). רשעים רבים are not 'many' but great, prominent evildoers (p. 162): 'als die Fülle angesehener Frevler'.
entries.flag: verify Krochmal's proposed word at high res — OCR unreadable

entries.note: 'The Lord knows the days of the blameless' is not really intelligible; LXX ὁδούς, i.e. דרכי תמימים 'the ways of the blameless' ('Der Herr kennt die Wege der Harmlosen').

entries.emendation: — (the כ stich is missing; v. 20 is its complement)
entries.note: If כי רשעים יאבדו were the כ acrostic, the second stich would be lacking — the verse is not long enough to divide in two; and the כי-clause cannot ground the preceding verse. So the כ stich has fallen out and v. 20 forms its complementary stich.

כיקר כרים would be a fine image, but why not the usual כציץ השדה or חציר גגות? LXX ἅμα τῷ δοξασθῆναι αὐτοὺς καὶ ὑψωθῆναι (= ביקרם וברומם); wohl richtiger leg. כִּירַק, and כרים — whose sense 'meadow' is doubtful — to be changed to הרים (cf. on Ps 65:14): 'wie das Grün der Berge schwinden sie'. For בעשן some codices, LXX and Pesh. have כעשן, as Isa 51:6: 'wie Rauch schwinden sie hin'.

The apparent parallel Prov 20:24 (also Jer 10:23) rests on a different thought — man cannot direct his steps without God. Here the sense must be: the steps are made firm by God so one does not fall (v. 24), because God delights in him. In whom? Surely not in every man (גבר); leg. 'the blameless one' — his translation 'die Schritte des Lautern'.
entries.flag: verify proposed word (תם?) at high res — OCR garbled

entries.note: V. 27 is a résumé; to ושכן supply ארץ — it repeats v. 3: 'so wirst Du (das Heimland) ewig bewohnen'.

entries.emendation: ענוים לעולם נשמרו ופשעים יִרָדְפוּ (supply ענוים; LXX plus ופשעים ירדפו)
entries.note: The ע acrostic is missing and must lurk in v. 28 — but not by emending לעולם נשמרו to עַוָּלִים נשמדו or עריצים as interpreters do, ostensibly after LXX: the LXX in fact have the Masoretic reading plus an addition (ἄνομοι δὲ ἐκδιωχθήσονται), and ἄνομοι always renders פשעים, not עולים. So לעולם נשמרו stands, and the acrostic is completed with ענוים: ענוים לעולם נשמרו ופשעים ירדפו וזרע רשעים נכרת (Hupfeld's two-page discussion entirely mistaken). His translation: '(Sanftmüthige) werden für immer bewahrt, (aber die Abtrünnigen werden verfolgt)'.
אשריו does not agree with the (singular) predicate תמעד; leg. the singular: 'so wankt sein Schritt nicht'. (Vv. 29–30 are wholly borrowed from Prov 10:30–31.)

entries.emendation: כארזי לבנון (LXX, Dyserinck); מתערה = מתעלה (from עלה)
