entries.note: The last two words are unintelligible in this context. LXX ὑπερυψούμενον … ὡς τὰς κέδρους τοῦ Λιβάνου, i.e. כארזי לבנון (so also Dyserinck): 'spriessen wie eine Zeder des Libanon'. מתערה — also a verb in Pesh., supported by the copula ו — cannot derive from ערה, rather from עלה (Hithpael מתעלה, Neo-Hebrew/Aramaic; perhaps also Job 6:16 יתעלם = יתעלה). If עריץ is to be a synonymous verb, its ע must be abstracted as dittograph of the ע in רשע (Dyserinck's עריץ = עריף after Isa 5:30 is untenable). Translation: 'Ich sah einen Frevler sich erheben'.
entries.flag: verify what remains of עריץ after dittograph removal (רץ? רם?) at high res

entries.note: ויעבר, third person, does not agree with ואבקשהו; LXX and Pesh. ואעבר 'I passed by' (p. 195b): 'Ich ging vorüber'.

תם and ישר must be abstracts, leg. תֹּם — יֹשֶׁר. And ראה ישר is incongruous; leg. רעה in the sense 'pursue, strive after' (רעה רוח, Jer 17:16) — so also Schorr and Krochmal: 'Bewahre Schlichtheit und erstrebe Gradheit'. אחרית here and in v. 38 = 'posterity' (Prov 24:20; so Hupfeld; Ewald's 'Nachwelt' wrong).
Leg. with LXX the future forms: 'Der Herr wird ihnen beistehen und sie erretten'.
As in Ps 6:2 the negation אל has fallen out in the second stich: 'nicht in Deiner Zorngluth züchtige mich'.
נחתו (a) is Aramaic-poetic 'come down' (p. 214), בי = 'into my inner being'. But ותנחת in b cannot be right; LXX ἐπεστήρισας, i.e. ותנח 'Du hast Deine Hand auf mich gelegt'.
entries.flag: verify proposed form (ותנח?) at high res

entries.note: Statt הלכתי leg. התהלכתי, as Ps 42:10/43:2 (קדר אתהלך): 'den ganzen Tag schleich ich düster einher'.

The Greek versions and Pesh. derive נקלה from קלון — certainly wrong; equally wrong the derivation from קלה 'scorch'. Targum has קדוחתא 'burning heat', which leads to the reading דלקה (interchange of ר/ד…, p. 131, 5c): 'meine Lenden sind voll von Brand'.
'The groaning of my heart' is a most unsuitable expression; leg. לביא 'of a lioness' (Olshausen), the א absorbed by the following אדני: 'ich stöhne lauter denn der Löwin Brüllen'.
תאותי 'my desire' cannot be synonymous with אנחתי; leg. תאנתי or תַּאֲנִיָּתִי from אנה 'lament': 'gegenwärtig sind Dir alle meine Klagen'.
סחרחר is hapax and cannot come from סחר, which means only 'wander about'; vielleicht a form of 'sich erhitzen' (חרר). Translation: 'Mein Herz wogt'.
entries.flag: verify proposed form (מחרחר?) at high res — OCR garbled

entries.note: ואור עיני גם הם — the plural is incongruent (subject singular); LXX and Pesh. singular; הם flowed together out of הוא: 'mein Augenlicht, es ist auch nicht bei mir'.

וינקשו is incorrect; there is no root נקש, only יקש (Ps 9:17 נוקש is Niphal; Deut 12:30 פן תנקש leg. תוקש; Ps 109:11 ינקש leg. יבקש; 1 Sam 28:9 מתנקש leg. מתעקש). So here too ויעקשו 'they act cunningly': 'Listig sind, so nach meinem Leben trachten'.
לא אשמע beside לא יפתח פיו is incongruent; leg. לא ישמע (confusion of the pronominal prefixes א and י, p. 135b): 'wie ein Tauber, der nicht hört'.

Not a tautology of v. 14: it means one who has no hearer (2 Sam 15:3 ושמע אין לך; Job 31:35 מי יתן לי שמע לי). So leg. here אשר לא שמע לו 'who has no one to hear him'. תוכחות = 'justifications' (Hupfeld), frequent in Job. Translation: 'wie ein Mann, der keinen Zuhörer hat'.

In vv. 17–19 the train of thought is unrecognizable; a verse mediating the transition seems to have fallen out before v. 17. In v. 17 עלי הגדילו is hypothetical, not factual perfect, with the object (פיהם) to be understood. Cf. the extra verse after v. 21 attested in LXX codices (see the v. 21 entry).
כי אני לצלע נכון = 'appointed for the fall' (נכון as Job 12:5, Prov 19:29; צלע 'stumbling, fall'). Statt ומכאובי נגדי besser ומכאוב: 'und Schmerz war mir stets gegenwärtig'.
כי עוני אגיד is no parallel to אדאג מחטאתי; daher leg. a verb of fearing — his translation: 'Denn ich fürchtete meine Schuld, war bekümmert wegen meiner Sünde'.
entries.flag: verify proposed verb (אגור? אחיל?) at high res — OCR garbled

entries.note: For חיים leg. חנם: 'meine Feinde um nichts sind zahlreich' (parallel ורבו שנאי שקר).
ומשלמי רעה is unsyntactic; daher leg. ומשלמים as predicate. ישטנוני, if the text is correct, means 'accuse' (Ps 109:4, LXX ἐνδιέβαλλον); were it 'hate' it would have to be ישטמוני.

entries.emendation: LXX plus: וישליכו את אשר אהבו כפגר נתעב
entries.note: Some LXX codices have after v. 21 a verse missing in the Hebrew text (Cod. 13 margin: καὶ ἀπέρριψαν με τὸν ἀγαπητὸν ὡσεὶ νεκρὸν ἐβδελυγμένον; likewise Syro-Hexapla; cf. Field, Origenis Hexapla on Ps 38:21). It is not invented but surely stems from an old Hebrew codex, displaced on comparison with the canonical text. In Hebrew the verse would run roughly: וישליכו את אשר אהבו כפגר נתעב.
'Way' and 'tongue' do not go together — one cannot possibly say אשמרה דרכי מחטא בלשוני; daher leg. דברי: 'will meine Worte hüten, nicht zu sündigen mit meiner Zunge'.
אשמרה twice in the same verse is inadmissible. LXX ἐθέμην, i.e. אשימה — which also suits the object מחסום better: 'will meinem Munde einen Zaum anlegen'.
בעוד is inexplicable; leg. בעמוד: 'so lange der Frevler mir gegenüber steht'.

החשיתי מטוב has provoked all kinds of forced explanations; it can only be a corruption, מבטא statt מטוב. The stem בטא means 'speak rashly' (Lev 5:4; Num 30; Prov 12:18): 'schwieg, einen unbesonnenen Laut zu sprechen'.
נעכר is not right: the pain is not 'troubled' but the sufferer. Wahrscheinlich leg. נכמר 'burned hot': 'während mein Schmerz brannte'.
בהגיגי is without parallel and obscure (p. 165). The Peshitta has בגושמי, i.e. בגוי 'in my body', like Jer 20:9 (בלבי כאש בערת עצור בעצמתי): 'in meinem Leibe brannte Feuer'.
חלד is an 'Unwort' (p. 208); leg. וחיי: 'und mein Leben ist wie nichts vor Deiner Gegenwart'.
entries.flag: verify proposed word (וחיי?) at high res — OCR garbled

entries.note: In אך כל הבל כל the first כל is dittographed; the stich must equal v. 12b (אך הבל כל אדם). נצב: even the upright-standing, firm man's life is a breath.

If one keeps בצלם one may not explain it as 'shadow-image': צלם means only 'image' and has nothing to do with צל (Aramaic טולא 'shadow' vs. צלמא 'image' — different roots; the Arabic ظلم proves nothing, corresponding to צלמות). If 'shadow' is required, read אך כצל מתהלך איש — the מ of מתהלך dittographed and wrongly attached to צל: 'wie ein Schatten wandelt der Mann'.

יהמיון is incongruent, the subject being singular; leg. יהמה ויצבר — the ו-copulative belonging to ויצבר became ן (yielding יהמיון). The Greek versions rightly have the singular. Under אוספם the object דגן ותירוש is understood: 'vergeblich tummelt er sich und häuft'.

entries.emendation: מה תקותי; and draw אדני to stich b (אדני תוחלתי לך)
entries.note: LXX render substantivally τίς ἡ ὑπομονή μου, likewise Pesh. מנו סברי; also leg. מה תקותי, which gives better sense. The following אדני is to be drawn to b (Herder): אדני תוחלתי לך, with לך = עליך (p. 238): 'was ist meine Hoffnung, mein Herr? Meine Erwartung ist auf Dich'.

מתגרת is hapax and inexplicable; the Aramaic תגרא 'quarrel' it cannot be, since Hebrew does not say ריב ידך either. Leg. תנופת ידך 'the swinging of Thy hand' (communication of Mr. Mos. Schulmann in Lemberg): 'vom Schwingen (?) Deiner Hand bin ich verwundet'.
כליתי is not quite in order — it could only mean 'I have perished and exist no more'! Wohl leg. חליתי 'I have fallen ill' (interchange of כ and ח, p. 126, 7).
After כל אדם supply נצב, as in v. 6: 'Hauch ist jeder auch gefestigte Mensch'.

This verse is decidedly borrowed from Job 10:20, where the thought is carried further. Here as there the first word must be emended: here השע leg. שעה 'look away from me', and in Job the still more corrupted ושית likewise statt שעה. (He notes the etymology of אבליגה remains unsettled; the versions were equally at a loss.)

שאון means only noisy raging, which does not fit; wahrscheinlich leg. שואה — שוחה (cf. p. 276 on Ps 35:8): 'aus des Verderbens Grube'. טיט היון (only here and 69:3) is etymologically unexplained, by sense 'mire', metaphor for dangers.

Taken literally רהבים would mean 'the stormers' and would really have to be רְהָבִים pointed otherwise. Richtig ist wohl הבלים 'vanities, idols' — LXX ματαιότητας — synonymous with שטי כזב (elliptical: those who turn from God to falsehood, p. 41): 'sich nicht den Eitlen (Götzen) zugewendet'.

The long verse divides into three parts: רבות עשית אתה ה׳ אלהי / נפלאתיך ומחשבתיך אלינו אין ערך אליך / אגידה ואדברה עצמו מספר. In (a) אתה ist wohl verschrieben für עתה, since emphasis has no place here (cf. Monatsschrift 1880, p. 491 f.): 'Grosses hast Du jetzt gethan'. אלינו is doubtful, missing in LXX.

entries.mt: זֶבַח וּמִנְחָה לֹא־חָפַצְתָּ אָזְנַיִם כָּרִיתָ לִּי עוֹלָה וַחֲטָאָה לֹא שָׁאָלְתָּ
entries.emendation: זבח ומנחה לוּ חפצת אז שמנים ברותי עולה וחטאה לוּ שאלת
entries.note: The parenthesis אזנים כרית לי gives no sense — in what way would 'dug ears' make sacrifices dispensable? And כרה is never used of ears (one says נטע אזן, Ps 94:9). Severe text damage. Per the parallel Ps 51:18, which LXX rightly render hypothetically (εἰ ἠθέλησας θυσίαν), read לוּ חפצת for לא, likewise עולה וחטאה לוּ שאלת. The apodosis particle או/אז lurks in אז־נים: detach אז, the defective remainder supplies שמנים 'fat beasts' (as 1 Sam 15:9 והמשנים leg. והשמנים); for the obscure כרית leg. ברותי 'I would have chosen for myself' (צאן ברורות? cf. Neh 5:18). The whole: זבח ומנחה לו חפצת אז שמנים ברותי — 'Verlangtest Du Opfer und Gaben, dann würde ich mir Feiste auswählen'.

entries.mt: אָז אָמַרְתִּי הִנֵּה־בָאתִי בִּמְגִלַּת־סֵפֶר כָּתוּב עָלָי
entries.emendation: הנה הֵבֵאתִי כמגלת ספר כתוב; עלי → סלה (?)
entries.note: The final ה of הנה displaced the initial ה of הבאתי: read הנה הבאתי '[behold] I have brought (burnt- and sin-offering)'; and כמגלת statt במגלת — 'according to the written book-roll' (the sacrificial prescriptions): 'sieh da, ich habe gebracht nach der Rolle des geschriebenen Buches'. The following עלי is in any case disturbing; vielleicht verschrieben für סלה (interchange of ע and ס, p. 134, 14) — his translation '(Selah?)'.

בתוך מעי = בקרבי 'I am wholly filled with it' (cf. Ezek 3:3). The emendation בתוך עמי (Krochmal) 'recommends itself strongly', were it not that it would require a dislocation of the verses (בשרתי צדק בקהל רב ותורתך בתוך עמי); his translation keeps 'in meinem Innern'.

entries.emendation: — (composite psalm; vv. 12 ff. a fragment parallel to Ps 70, with a lacuna before v. 12)
entries.note: The psalm has flowed together from two heterogeneous parts: I (vv. 2–11) an exilic thanksgiving, probably from the circle (or hand) of Deutero-Isaiah (בשרתי צדק בקהל רב; צדק/תשועה/בשר as his catchwords); II (vv. 12 ff.) a lament of which Ps 70 is a detached piece — the last five verses coincide with Ps 70. At כי אפפו עלי (v. 13) the fragment begins; v. 12 belongs to it, but something is missing before it — the lacuna must have contained a petition, roughly אליך קראתי, v. 12 giving its continuation and כי the grounding.
עונתי is wohl nicht ganz richtig; dafür leg. צרתי (cf. Ps 130): 'erreicht haben mich Drangsäle'.

לראות would require a prior statement that the psalmist's sufferings darkened his eyes, which is not given; daher leg. לשאת 'not able to bear' (interchange of ר and ש): 'Drangsäle, nicht zu ertragen'.

על עקב בשתם is corrupted, hence unintelligible. The final ב of עקב is dittographed in בשתם; detached, שתם remains, to which מח must be added: על עקב שמחתם 'because of their Schadenfreude' (cf. Ezek 35:15 where שמחה = malicious joy). To this fits האמרים לי האח (Ps 70 lacks לי, which stands for עלי, p. 238). He also notes ישמו here is more correct than ישובו in Ps 70:4. Translation: 'Mögen sie beschämt sein ob ihrer Schadenfreude'.

entries.emendation: אדני (אלהים) חושה לעזרתי — whole verse: אדני חושה לעזרתי עזרי ומפלטי אתה אלהי אל תאחר
entries.note: As in Ps 70:6 leg. חושה statt יחשב (the י dittographed and ב statt ה); and לי is not right but, as Ps 38:23, חושה לעזרתי (missing in Ps 70, while עזרי — correct there — is missing here). The whole verse emended: אדני (אלהים) חושה לעזרתי עזרי ומפלטי אתה אלהי (ה׳) אל תאחר: 'Herr, eile zu meiner Hilfe! Mein Beistand und Zuflucht bist Du'.

LXX add καὶ πένητα, i.e. ואביון, as Ps 72:13, 82:4, 1 Sam 2:8 — terms synonymous with עני/ענו, the circle of the sufferers (p. 24 f.). משכיל אל/על = 'attend to, care about someone'. The blessing vv. 2b–4 is the well-wisher's implied speech, with לאמר to be understood (as Ps 40:5).

entries.emendation: Keri יְאֻשַּׁר; ואל תתנהו → ואל יתנהו (3rd person)
entries.note: The Keri יאשר is more correct than the Kethib. בארץ without qualifier = 'in the homeland' Judea (cf. Ps 37:3) — the sick sufferer shall share the happiness promised the exiles on their return. For ואל תתנהו LXX, Symmachus and Pesh. have the third person (καὶ μὴ παραδῴη αὐτόν), 'viel richtiger' (interchange of personal affixes, p. 135, 17).

כל משכבו הפכת בחליו is inexplicable with all arts of interpretation. Leg. על (כ miswritten for ע, p. 134, 14): על משכבו = על ערש דוי, and before הפכת supply the relative אשר: 'auf seinem Lager, das Du in seiner Krankheit verwandelt'.
'Heal my soul, for I have sinned against Thee' is a strange motivation of the plea; leg. כי קראתי לך (interchange of ק and ח, p. 126, 6): 'heile meine Seele, denn ich rufe Dich an!'
While the singer pleads for healing his enemies say רע לי — vielleicht leg. לו, 'weh’ ihm!' ('Meine Feinde aber sprachen: weh’ ihm! wann wird er sterben').

entries.mt: וְאִם־בָּא לִרְאוֹת שָׁוְא יְדַבֵּר לִבּוֹ יִקְבָּץ־אָוֶן לוֹ יֵצֵא לַחוּץ יְדַבֵּר
entries.emendation: plural throughout: ואם באו לראות שוא ידברו, לבם יקבץ און לי, יצאו לחוץ ידברו (יחד עלי drawn from v. 8)
entries.note: V. 7 is conspicuous by its incongruence — before and after, the enemies are plural. Pesh. has the plural, and LXX join יחד (עלי) of v. 8 to v. 7; one cannot say יצא לחוץ ידבר יחד עלי, so the verbs must be plural. Vv. 7–8 should run: ואם באו לראות שוא ידברו / לבם יקבץ און לי / יצאו לחוץ ידברו יחד עלי // יתלחשו כל שנאי עלי / יחשבו רעה לי. אין = עמל 'mischief'; לי of course statt לו. This also explains the heaping of עלי/לי in v. 8.

entries.emendation: supply אמרו before the quote; ואשר → באשר
entries.note: יצוק = 'firmly cast, fixed' (so rightly Hengstenberg and Delitzsch; frequent in Job), so דבר בליעל can only mean moral depravity — the enemies' malicious talk against the psalmist; אמרו must be supplied. And ואשר שכב is inexplicable in the Masoretic form; leg. באשר, the ב softened to ו (p. 122): 'da, wo er liegt, auf dem Siechbette'.

entries.emendation: הגדיל עלי עקבו (draw the ו of ואתה)
entries.note: הגדיל עלי עקב is obscure; עקב seems to mean 'ambush, treachery' here (Josh 8:13), with the ו of the following ואתה drawn to it: הגדיל עלי עקבו, like הרבה: 'vermehrt seine Hinterlist gegen mich'. אוכל לחמי must, for symmetry, be a predicate like הגדיל עלי, hence figurative: 'slander, accuse' (p. 194).

חנני vielfach leg. חיני, as often in Ps 119: 'lass mich genesen'. And ואשלמה is difficult — absolutely it could at best mean 'requite good', but without טוב it stays ambiguous; daher wohl leg. ושלמה imperative (addressed to God): 'richte mich auf und vergilt ihnen'.
entries.flag: verify both proposed forms (חיני, ושלמה) at high res — OCR garbled

entries.note: Since the psalm always speaks of several enemies, the clause must be made congruent: יריעו איבי (plural): 'wenn meine Feinde nicht triumphiren über mich'.

תמכת בי is unintelligible: transitive תמך governs the accusative, and with ב it means to hold fast to someone — which cannot be said of God. Daher leg. תמכתי, first person with בתמי, 'I hold fast to my integrity' (Job 2:3, 9 מחזיק בתמתו; 27:6). The following בי leg. כי, joined to the verb: כי תציבני (the ו of ותציבני dittographed from בי): 'Ich aber halte an meiner Schlichtheit fest, Du haltest mich vor Dir für immer aufrecht'.
בֶּאֱמֹר אלי leg. באמרם, as v. 11: 'wenn sie zu mir alle Tage sprechen: Wo ist Dein Gott?' — spoken by opponents still in the homeland, before the banishment.

entries.mt: אֶעֱבֹר בַּסָּךְ אֶדַּדֵּם עַד־בֵּית אֱלֹהִים … הָמוֹן חוֹגֵג
entries.emendation: אעבר בסוד מְשֹׁרְרִים עד בית אלהים … המון חוגגים
entries.note: בסך אדדם is inexplicable despite all arts of interpretation: סך 'multitude' is hapax (Aramaic סך = 'sum', not crowd), and אֶדַּדֵּם is formally an 'Unwort'. Statt בסך leg. בסוד (interchange ד/ך, p. 129, 1) — the intimate circle is called סוד (סוד משחקים, סוד ישרים, סוד בחורים); in the corrupted אדדם must lurk the second member of the construct, a substantive — משוררים suggests itself most readily (interchange of ש/מ, p. 150; רר corrupted to דד, ש dropped): 'wie ich im Kreise der Sänger zu Gottes Tempel zog'. This fits the close: for המון חוגג LXX and Symmachus have the plural ἑορταζόντων = חוגגים (the ם absorbed by the following מה), apposition to סוד משוררים — a reminiscence of the festal processions of Hezekiah's time.

entries.emendation: read all three times ישועת פני אלהי
entries.note: The refrain occurring three times must of course read identically and the variant be eliminated. ידה governs a double accusative (person and thing): אודנו ישועת can only mean 'thank God for the help (of His countenance)'; פני = the friendly face, goodwill. So read all three times ישועת פני אלהי — statt פניו; the ו of ואלהי dittographed from the י, and in the first occurrence אלהי dropped out: 'für die Gunstwendung meines Gottes'.

Two or more 'Hermons' do not exist (despite Jerome's fable of a little Hermon); rightly Pesh. מן חרמון — the ים is evidently dittographed from the following מ of מהר. And הר מצער 'the little mountain' is suspect — where would it lie? The Hermon was from of old a cult mountain (בעל גד / בעל חרמון, Josh 11:17, 1 Chr 5:23; in Greek times the Paneion, Banias); such a mountain of festal assembly is הר מועד (Isa 14:13). Reading מהר מועד (letter confusion), the phrase is simply apposition to חרמון: 'vom Hermon, dem Festwallberg'.

entries.mt: יוֹמָם יְצַוֶּה יְהוָה חַסְדּוֹ וּבַלַּיְלָה שִׁירֹה עִמִּי תְּפִלָּה לְאֵל חַיָּי
entries.emendation: supply אקרא with יומם; שירה → שִׂיחָה; לאל חיי → לאל חי
entries.note: The verse is not really intelligible: יומם (a) and בלילה (b) are parallel, and something contained in b must be supplied with יומם — roughly אקרא (as Ps 22:3). In b, תפלה and שירה must be synonymous; leg. שיחה 'complaint, plaint'. And statt לאל חיי leg. לאל חי, as v. 3: 'Tags (rufe ich): möge der Herr seine Gnade entbieten, und Nachts ist bei mir die Klage, ein Gebet zum lebendigen Gott'.
למה שכחתני vielleicht leg. למה זנחתני as 43:2; but in any case statt אלך leg. אתהלך as there ('warum soll ich düster einhergehen bei des Frevlers Druck?').

ברצח בעצמותי is unintelligible; leg. כרקב 'like rot in my bones', as Prov 12:4, 14:30 (interchange of צ/ק and ח/ב, pp. 127, 8; 131, 3i). But the verb חרפוני then does not fit; leg. חרפות צררי 'the taunts of my foes' (interchange of ־וני and ־ות): 'Wie Moder in meinem Gebein, so die Lästerung der Höhner'.

The two psalms' belonging together is so striking that it did not escape the ancients — Eusebius already remarks on Ps 43 that by identity of style and train of thought it clearly forms part of Ps 42 (shared refrain, shared למה קדר אתהלך בלחץ אויב). Together they form one lament of a Levite singer banished from the sanctuary — pre-exilic, at the foot of Hermon by the Jordan springs, under Manasseh's persecution.

שמחת גילי is pleonasm, leg. שמחת לבי 'the joy of my heart'. And אלהים אלהי is striking; leg. אלהים אל חי as Ps 42:3 (interchange of ה and ח, p. 126, 6b): 'Gott, lebendiger Gott' — the Levite singer longing to play the harp in the Temple again (v. 3 אורך ואמתך = the Urim and Thummim).

ותטעם has been misunderstood by the interpreters (assuming another object); leg. ותסעם 'uproot' (interchange of ט and ס). תרע is mostly construed with ל, so leg. ללאמים (the ל absorbed). And for ותשלחם LXX ἐξέβαλες, i.e. ותשליכם (p. 196, 7): 'vertrieben und entwurzelt, geschädigt Stämme und sie verbannt'.

entries.emendation: a form of גוח 'fight' (Aramaic אגחא קרבא)
entries.note: Hebrew נגח means only 'gore with the horns', which does not fit here. It is wohl the Aramaic גוח / אגח, which also means 'fight' (אגחא קרבא); cf. Dan 11:40 ויתגח. Daher leg. the corresponding form: 'Mit Dir werden wir unsere Gegner bekriegen'.
entries.flag: verify proposed form (נגיח/נגוח?) at high res — OCR garbled

entries.note: V. 10 forms the transition — אך זנחת, but unrecognizable because of אף (p. 129f). LXX have in addition νυνί, Pesh. השא, i.e. עתה, which makes the construction more pregnant: אך עתה זנחת (parallel Ps 89:39 ואתה זנחת): 'Aber jetzt hast Du verlassen und uns beschämt'.
רבית as Piel of רבה is doubtful; leg. הרבית Hiphil: 'und erwarbst nichts bei ihrem Kaufpreis'.

For מקול leg. מפי (cf. Ps 8:3, p. 140). מתנקם, intensive of נקם 'breathing vengeance', refers to Antiochus Epiphanes, as does מחרף ומגדף — he blasphemed God (1 Macc 1:24; Dan 7:25, 8:11) and wrought a bloodbath in Judea from vengefulness (the psalm is Maccabean; John Hyrcanus removed it from the Temple liturgy, Geschichte der Juden III, p. 120).
entries.flag: verify lemma/emendation (מקול→מפי?) at high res — OCR garbled

entries.note: כי is concessive, 'obwohl'. For דכיתנו leg. דחיתנו 'thrust us away' ('Obwohl Du uns verstossen in Stätten von Ungethümen'); תנים is shortened from תנינים — place of monsters = wilderness, attested by 1 Macc 1:53, 2:29–31 (the pious fleeing to the desert).

entries.mt: רָחַשׁ לִבִּי דָּבָר טוֹב אֹמֵר אָנִי מַעֲשַׂי לְמֶלֶךְ
entries.note: רחש is not quite secure (Hebrew otherwise only in מרחשת; Aramaic it means 'swarm, crawl' — 'bubble forth' is only guessed); דבר טוב is quite unseemly, and אמר אני מעשי barely graspable (hardly ᾔρξατο as all the Greek versions). In short, half-verse a is unclear — his translation marks 'mein Gedicht (?)'.

יפיפית is to be divided יפה יפית ('Schön, schöner bist du als Menschensöhne'). הוצק חן בשפתותיך can only mean possessing graceful, well-set speech, 'poetic eloquence' — the addressed king (Hezekiah, to whom the psalm is dated) must have been a poet.

entries.emendation: על ירכך (with suffix, per LXX); supply היא before הודך והדרך
entries.note: LXX and other versions read על ירך with the suffix (ἐπὶ τὸν μηρόν σου) = על ירכך. The half-verse b seems too short; supply היא: היא הודך והדרך 'es ist dein Schmuck und deine Zier'.

entries.emendation: delete והדרך (dittograph); צלח → (vielleicht) הֵחָלֵץ; וענוה צדק → וענוה וצדק
entries.note: The word והדרך is missing in LXX and Pesh. — it is dittographed (from v. 4). צלחה is unclear: Kal means 'cross over' (= עבר), which does not fit; vielleicht leg. חלץ in Niphal, 'rüste dich' ('Brich auf'). רכב 'ride', figuratively 'rule'. And וענוה צדק — an unclear compound as construct; the Greek versions have וצדק, so leg. וענוה וצדק (ענוה the virtue of the Anawim; Zeph 2:3): 'für das Wort der Wahrheit, der Milde und Gerechtigkeit'.
עמים תחתיך יפלו with the following בלב is awkward; leg. יפלו … כל איבי המלך: 'werfen Völker unter Dir nieder, alle Feinde des Königs'.

אלהים אלהיך is dittographed. And מחברך is unintelligible, especially in the singular (per the Masora), which cannot be a superlative; leg. ויבחרך, cf. Isa 49:7 קדש ישראל ויבחרך 'He has preferred, chosen you' — fitting Hezekiah, who as a younger son reached the throne (anointing occurred precisely at contested successions): 'darum salbte dich Gott mit Jubel-Oel und erwählte dich'.

כל בגדתיך is certainly corrupt, since the plural of בגד is exclusively בגדים; wohl leg. a word for 'treasuries/costly things' — his translation 'deine Gewürzkammern (?)'. And מני שמחוך can no more be a stringed instrument here than a preposition — why lyre-playing at a coronation rather than horns and flutes? Vielleicht leg. a word for songs/music ('aus dem Palast von Elfenbein erfreuen dich Lieder').
entries.flag: verify both proposed words (גנזיך? מנגינות?) at high res — OCR garbled

entries.note: Over the reading ביקרותיך the Masoretes themselves disagreed (cf. Norzi, מנחת שי ad loc.); gewiss leg. לקראתך: 'Königstöchter kommen dir entgegen'. And בכתם אופיר wahrscheinlich leg. בכתר אופיר 'with the crown of Ophir', as Song 5:11 כתם פז leg. כתר (Dan 10:5 likewise corrupt). שגל is the legitimate queen (Neh 2:6).
Pesh. more correctly ברתי, i.e. בתי — the psalmist addresses the queen familiarly, 'meine Tochter'. ושכחי עמך: עם here means not 'people' but 'family' (Monatsschrift 1874, p. 1 f.).

entries.mt: וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִי־לוֹ׃ וּבַת־צֹר בְּמִנְחָה פָּנַיִךְ יְחַלּוּ עֲשִׁירֵי עָם
entries.emendation: והשתחוו לך בנות צור במנחה / פניך יחלו עשירי עם (עמי הארץ) בכל כבודם
entries.note: כי הוא אדניך gives no intelligible motivation — a small lacuna seems to be in v. 12. LXX draw והשתחוי לו to the following verse, in the plural (καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν αὐτῷ θυγατέρες Τύρου), and Pesh. similarly repeats the verb at v. 13; LXX also begin half-verse b with פניך יחלו. Keeping this, reading לך statt לו, and drawing כל כבודה of v. 14 to v. 13 as בכל כבודם (ם/ה interchange, p. 132), vv. 12–13 take an unforced shape: the verse enumerates all who will do homage to the queen — Tyre's daughters (colonies) and the richest of the peoples with all their wealth. בת צר is thus not vocative — no Tyrian princess, still less Hitzig's Cleopatra.

entries.mt: כָּל־כְּבוּדָּה בַת־מֶלֶךְ פְּנִימָה מִמִּשְׁבְּצוֹת זָהָב לְבוּשָׁהּ
entries.emendation: בת מלך פנינים במשבצות זהב לבושה
entries.note: בת מלך is not the addressed queen — she was no princess but a commoner raised by her beauty (v. 12), addressed simply as בתי (v. 11) — but an actual king's daughter, subject of vv. 14–15 (hence אחריה v. 15; otherwise it would be אחריך). פנימה 'into the interior' gives no sense; leg. פנינים 'corals/pearls' (so also Krochmal; cf. פניים Prov 3:15), and ממשבצות leg. במשבצות: her adornment as she is led to the queen — 'Die Königstochter mit Perlen, in goldner Einfassung ihr Gewand'. (כל כבודה goes to v. 13 as בכל כבודם.)

entries.emendation: ברקמות (joined to לבושה); למלך → לְמוּלֵךְ 'dir entgegen'
entries.note: Nearly all the Greek versions connect לרקמות with לבושה, reading ברקמות 'in embroideries'. And תובל למלך 'led to the king'? The address is to the queen! Daher leg. 'toward you' — the king's daughter with her virgin companions is led to the queen as companion-servants. Vv. 14–15: בת מלך פנינים במשבצות זהב לבושה ברקמות / תובל למולך בתולות אחריה רעותיה מובאות לך.
entries.flag: verify the emended word for למלך (למולך?) at high res

entries.mt: תַּחַת אֲבֹתֶיךָ יִהְיוּ בָנֶיךָ תְּשִׁיתֵמוֹ לְשָׂרִים
entries.emendation: feminine forms: תחת אבתיך יהיו בניך תשיתימו — addressed to the queen
entries.note: V. 17 has been utterly misunderstood as an address to the king, whereas it continues the address to the queen — so Pesh. with feminine forms (בניכי, אבהיכי); the punctuators mistook the gender and misled the interpreters. Only addressed to the queen does the prospect make sense: she cannot forget her father's house — well, in its stead she will see sons as princes in all the land. (For the king, what would תחת אבתיך even mean?)

entries.mt: אַזְכִּירָה שִׁמְךָ בְּכָל־דֹּר וָדֹר עַל־כֵּן עַמִּים יְהוֹדוּךָ
entries.emendation: בניך יזכירו שמך …; על כן → עד כי
entries.note: Remarkably LXX have for the first person singular the third plural μνησθήσονται (Alexandrinus + καὶ ἀντιλήψονται), Pesh. passive דנתדכר שמך — the continuation of the address to the queen: בניך יזכירו שמך, her sons perpetuating her name through the generations (interchange of personal prefixes, p. 130, 17). In b, על כן is not quite correct: the Masoretes already noted interchange of על and עד (Monatsschrift 1881, p. 218 f.), and כן stands not seldom for כי (p. 133, 10); leg. עד כי עמים יהודוך לעולם ועד 'so that peoples will praise you for ever'.

נמצא 'findable' — who lets Himself be found by eager seeking (Jer 29:14) — but נמצא מאד is odd; leg. תמיד, Pesh. בכל זמן (frequent confusion of מאד and תמיד; cf. Ps 112:1 חפץ מאד leg. תמיד): 'Hilfe in Nöthen, findbar stets'.
בהמיר as transitive of מור 'change' with ארץ as accusative (Olshausen) is possible; besser בהמס ארץ 'when the earth melts' (Krochmal) — his translation 'wenn die Erde schmilzt'.

entries.emendation: supply the refrain ה׳ צבאות עמנו משגב לנו אלהי יעקב סלה
entries.note: The psalm has three strophes of four verses each with the same refrain; before סלה of v. 4 the refrain — which forms the fourth verse — has been effaced and must be supplied (Hupfeld). His translation prints it in parentheses. (In v. 4 מימיו: the suffix cannot refer to ימים, so either read בלב ים singular or take ימים as collective; בגאותו refers to God.)

נהר פלגיו is an impossible construction, and even a construct state would not help much, since the predicate ישמחו is plural; to be read as a verb, Hiphil הנהיר, with the ה absorbed by the preceding סלה: 'Er liess Seine Bäche strömen, dass sie erfreuen die Gottesstadt'. קדש משכני = superlative, the holiest of God's dwelling-places.

מטו ממלכות can only mean 'the kingdoms sank', so המו must be synonymous, as LXX and Pesh. render passively (ἐταράχθησαν, אשתגשו) 'were thrown into confusion' — thus a Pual form of המם, regularly הממו, shortened המו with dagesh in the מ: 'Verwirrt wurden die Nationen, es sanken die Reiche'.

'Devastations' God did not work then — on the contrary, He destroyed the instruments of devastation (v. 10). שמות is surely corrupt: the syllable שמ is dittographed from שם. LXX τέρατα, Pesh. 'wonder-signs'; folglich leg. שם אותות statt שמות: 'wie er Wunder gethan im Lande' — most naturally the sudden destruction of Sennacherib's army in Hezekiah's time.

תקע כף means calmly placing one's hand in another's, hence 'pledge, stand surety'; for joyful clapping Hebrew says הכה כף אל כף or מחא כף. The reading is therefore doubtful — כף is perhaps a wreck of תקעו ב[שו]פ[ר] 'blow the shofar', to which stich b (הריעו לאלהים) fits better; his translation: 'Alle Völker, stosset in das Horn'.

The tempora ידבר and יבחר leave it doubtful whether past or future is meant; the old versions are decisive — LXX and Pesh. render them as historical tenses (ὑπέταξε, ἐξελέξατο). Both verses refer to the remotest past, the conquest of the holy land: 'Er hat Völker unter uns gezwungen … Er hat unser Erbe uns erwählt'.

עלה אלהים is not to be understood here; the interchange of ע and ס (p. 134, 14) leads to the imperative סלו 'extol' (as Ps 68:5) — the word עלה arose through the neighboring word. With a plural imperative leading, all the following imperative forms fit: 'Preiset Gott mit Drommetenschall'.

משכיל = 'one skilled in art', as Ibn Ezra already rightly explained; but congruence demands משכילים — the ם absorbed by the following מלך (v. 9): a summons to the art-skilled Levites (p. 82): 'lobsinget, ihr Kunstverständigen!'
leg. ישב as participle, LXX κάθηται: 'Gott sitzt auf Seinem heiligen Throne' — the throne being Zion or the Temple (Jer 17:12).

entries.mt: נְדִיבֵי עַמִּים נֶאֱסָפוּ עַם אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם … מְאֹד נַעֲלָה
entries.emendation: supply אל (or על) before עם; complete נעלה על כל אלהים
entries.note: The preposition to נאספו is evidently missing — אל, perhaps originally על, displaced by the following עם. But עם itself is necessary (against LXX μετά and Pesh. לות = עִם): the princes gathered not to God but to the people of God — אלהי אברהם alluding to the fulfilment of Gen 12:3. And the close מאד נעלה is lacunose: complete נעלה על כל אלהים (cf. p. 327, per the parallel Ps 97:9): 'Er ist hoch erhaben (über alle Götter)'.

נוף is isolated and its meaning 'height' unsecured (the Arabic analogy means something else). Leg. יפה ענף 'beautiful branch/bough', as Ezek 31:3, apposition to הר ציון: 'Schöner Zweig, Freude des ganzen Landes ist der Berg Zion'.

entries.emendation: supply נשא: הר ציון נשא מירכתי צפון
entries.note: The apposition ירכתי צפון is unintelligible — Zion lay neither as city-quarter nor as temple in the far north, and a Hebrew singer cannot have called Zion the 'mountain of the gods' of the far north (Isa 14:13; against Olshausen and Hupfeld). A word seems missing — נשא — whose supply makes the verse elegant: 'Mount Zion is more exalted than the god-mountain in the farthest north, city of a mighty king' (קרית מלך רב referring to David, who built Zion; cf. Isa 29:1 קרית חנה דוד).
עברו יחדו is unintelligible; leg. חברו, as Gen 14:3: 'die Könige … haben sich zusammen verbunden'.

דמינו can be taken quite literally — 'we pictured Thy grace to ourselves as we pleaded in the Temple for rescue from the threatening danger'; vielleicht gar zu lesen קוינו 'we hoped' — his translation: 'Wir erhofften, Gott, Deine Gnade im Innern Deines Tempels'.

entries.emendation: שמך → (vielleicht) שמעך; על קצוי → עד קצוי; supply a parallel word (משפט) in the close
entries.note: כשמך כן תהלתך = as Thy repute as helper, heard of historically, so Thy now-proven fame (cf. Ps 138:2); vielleicht at both places leg. שמעך statt שמך. Selbstverständlich על קצוי must be read עד קצוי, as often עד קצה — so also Pesh. עדמא (on the interchange of על and עד, p. 127, 9): 'bis an der Erden Enden'. The close צדק מלאה ימינך lacks parallelism; vielleicht supply משפט — which would then suit למען משפטיך in the following verse (the judgments on the allied kings).

פסגו is isolated, corrupted from פקדו 'observe': vv. 13–15 have been misunderstood by all interpreters as pointing to Zion's strong defenses — but v. 15 (God alone wrought the rescue) and v. 4 (אלהים נודע למשגב) contradict that; the psalm means to display Zion's weakness (cf. Zech 2:8–9): go around Zion, count how few towers it has, note how weak its citadels — that posterity may learn God alone protected it.

entries.emendation: עלמות belongs to the superscription of Ps 49 (על עלמות)
entries.note: The Masora reads על מות as two words; the Talmudists and Targum read one word ('youth'), LXX εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας (= עולמות, one word — a false rendering, but proof that their text had עלמות undivided and preceded by a preposition, אל or על; so also Symmachus εἰς τὸ διηνεκές). This על עלמות cannot be placed in this verse: it has evidently strayed up from the superscription of the next psalm and belongs after לבני קרח as designation of the instrument (p. 71; so also Krochmal) — Ps 49's heading must read למנצח לבני קרח על עלמות, like Ps 46:1. With it removed, הוא ינהגנו lacks its duration term and must be slightly adjusted.
entries.flag: verify Graetz's adjusted wording of the remaining verse-end at high res (pdf 352)

entries.note: ישבי חלד is unintelligible; LXX οἱ κατοικοῦντες τὴν οἰκουμένην, i.e. תבל (ת confused with ח, ב with ד, and the ל transposed): 'lauschet, alle Bewohner des Erdkreises!'
והגות לבי is not really fitting; symmetry (with פי ידבר חכמות) requires ולבי יהגה תבונות — the transmitted form modeled on חכמות: 'Mein Mund soll Weisheit sprechen und mein Herz Sinniges hegen'.

Stich b is unintelligible and no exegetical device explains it. At best עקבי can be explained by transposition as קבעי 'my oppressors' (Pesh. בעלדבבי 'enemies') — though the verb יסבני still does not fit well. V. 7 (הבטחים על חילם) is then apposition to קבעי: 'dass Tücke meiner Bedränger mich umgeben wird, so auf ihr Gut vertrauen'.
LXX τῆς λυτρώσεως τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ, i.e. נפשו — were one's own redemption costly, the covetous man would forgo it for ever: 'Wäre hoch im Preise die eigene Auslösung, so unterbliebe sie für immer'.

entries.emendation: קברם (their grave); supply אשר before קראו בשמותם
entries.note: The Talmudists and the old versions read קברם (or קבריהם) 'their grave is their house for ever' — 'Ihr Grab ist ihr Haus für immer'. At the close, supply אשר before קראו בשמותם עלי אדמות.

נדמו is obscure — surely from דמם 'be still, dumb', Niphal 'be silenced, destroyed'; referred to בהמות it is superfluous, and referred to אדם it would have to read נדמה or ידמה. The verse closes the thought of v. 6: nothing to fear, since man does not remain in his pomp. (Vv. 8–12 are properly a digression.)

דרכם כסל למו is a shortened construct (דרך כסל, cf. Ps 45:7); ואחריהם best rendered by Symmachus οἱ μετ᾽ αὐτούς 'their successors'. בפיהם is unintelligible; leg. כמוהם. The reading ירצו is doubtful (Aquila רצו 'ran', Pesh. ירעו כצאן), none satisfying. One might read for the disturbing סלה (with interchange of ס and ע and a dropped ו) עַוְלָה = עוֹלָה 'iniquity' (like עלתה Job 5:16): ואחריהם כמוהם ירצו עולה, 'and those after them will like them take pleasure in iniquity'.

entries.mt: כַּצֹּאן לִשְׁאוֹל שַׁתּוּ מָוֶת יִרְעֵם וַיִּרְדּוּ בָם יְשָׁרִים לַבֹּקֶר וְצוּרָם לְבַלּוֹת שְׁאוֹל מִזְּבֻל לוֹ
entries.emendation: כצאן לשאול שחו מות ירעם וירדו כמו רפאים לקבר ויצורם למלאות שאול מזבלם
entries.note: The darkest verse of the psalm; apart from מות ירעם everything is unintelligible. שתו is an impossible form (active lacks an object; passively שית occurs only in Hiphil); wohl leg. שחו 'they sink' (cf. Prov 2:18 שחה אל מות ביתה) — 'like a flock they sink to Sheol, Death shepherds them'. In stich b, vocalize וירדו differently, statt לבקר leg. לקבר, and בם emends easily to כמו; the term of comparison ישרים is evidently not correct — the emendation רפאים offers itself (Prov 2:18, 9:18, 21:16): וירדו כמו רפאים לקבר. For the darkest part: all old versions have a plural pronoun (even Aquila ἀπὸ κατοικητηρίου αὐτῶν), so מזבלם 'their splendid dwelling' (זבול is a stately residence — Sheol will be their mansion); for לבלות LXX = לכלות בשאול, Aquila (and the Talmudists, RH 17a) לכלות שאול — too bold a metaphor, hence recommends itself למלאות שאול 'to fill Sheol' (cf. on Ps 92:11); and וצורם (Qere) is best taken as the verb וִיצוּרֵם 'He will pen them in'. His translation: 'Wie eine Heerde werden sie in die Tiefe sinken, der Tod wird sie weiden, und sie werden gleich Rephaim (?) in die Gruft fahren, und Er wird sie einengen, die Grabeswelt zu füllen, ihre Wohnung.'

entries.emendation: אך לו אלהים יפדה נפשי (draw לו from v. 15); כי מיד שאול inverted from מיד שאול כי יקחני
entries.note: V. 16 is intelligible but stands abrupt and isolated, seemingly indicating a lacuna. The לו of the preceding verse — impossible to place there — appears to be the wish/conditional particle joined with אך: leg. אך לו, 'Wenn doch Gott meine Seele erlöste!'. Stich b as LXX ἐκ χειρὸς ᾅδου ὅταν: the particle כי is inverted, standing for מיד שאול כי יקחני; לקח here = 'take away, withdraw' (Hos 13:14 מיד שאול אפדם) — no trace of resurrection in this psalm either.

entries.emendation: אל תתחר or אל תֵּרֶא ('look with envy')
entries.note: אל תירא is not right — to fear when someone grows rich sounds odd. If not אל תתחר ('Ereifere Dich nicht'), then leg. a verb of envious looking.
entries.flag: verify second proposed reading (תרא?) at high res — OCR garbled

entries.note: For the plural, LXX and Pesh. have the singular ἐξομολογήσεται. And כי תיטיב לך gives no sense; LXX αὐτῷ, Pesh. לה, so leg. לו — the address being to God: 'er bekennt Dich nur, wenn Du ihm Gutes erweisest'.

entries.emendation: תביאהו (Pesh.) or יבא (LXX); דור = 'dwelling'; לא יראה (singular)
entries.note: Either read with Pesh. תביאהו (God as subject — his translation 'Du wirst ihn zur Wohnung seiner Väter bringen') or with LXX εἰσελεύσεται the third person יבא (p. 135, 17). דור is here, like Aramaic דירה, 'dwelling' (cf. Ps 84:11). For לא יראו אור, Pesh. and Quinta have the singular לא יראה.
The ו of ולא is to be drawn to ביקר — ביקרו, and the rest as v. 13: 'Der Mensch bleibt nicht in seiner Ehre, er ist gleich den stummen Thieren'.

דבר ויקרא ארץ is unintelligible, since קרא would require the preposition אל before ארץ, as v. 4. Leg. ויברא ארץ 'and created the earth', so Targum (interchange of ב and ק, p. 130, 3g): 'sprach und schuf die Erde'.
For נשערה, per Targum and Pesh. read a plural form (cf. p. 136e): 'und ringsum stürmen gar sehr!'.
entries.flag: verify proposed form (ישערו?) at high res — OCR garbled

entries.note: Leg. per LXX the future: 'Dann wird der Himmel seine Gerechtigkeit verkünden, dass Gott Richter ist'.
עוף הרים is without parallel — always עוף שמים; so also LXX and Pesh. (τοῦ οὐρανοῦ). Daher leg. שמים. (זיז שדי, only here and Ps 80:14, is probably an animal at home in Egypt.)
LXX and Pesh. have διάψαλμα at the close, i.e. סלה — quite fitting, since with v. 16 a new train of thought and thus a new strophe begins (his translation marks the break with asterisks).

אמר אלהים is not fact but wish (as v. 4), which can be given with the perfect; vielleicht gar leg. יאמר — his translation 'Und zum Frevler spräche Gott'. ולרשע addresses a whole class (the singular kept from strophe II; v. 22 has the plural). בריתי = ספר בריתי, the covenant book of Josiah's reform (2 Kgs 23:2–3).
LXX, Pesh. and Targum read a form of רוץ 'you ran with him' — his translation 'Sähest du einen Dieb, du liefest mit ihm' — not רצה 'be pleased'.
פיך שלחת is an impossible phrase. LXX ἐπλεόνασε, so leg. מלאת (interchanges of ש/מ and ח/א, p. 194, 6): 'Deinen Mund hast du mit Bosheit gefüllt'.

תשב באחיך yields a sense, but better and more symmetrical is תדבר באחיך (Krochmal), matching תתן דפי 'utter slander' (דפי isolated but secured by Neo-Hebrew and Aramaic usage): 'Schande redest du gegen deinen Bruder'.

היות אהיה is not really intelligible. LXX ἀνομίαν = דמית הוות 'you devised mischief', like הוות תחשב (Ps 52:4) — his translation 'Du hast Unheil ersonnen'. Also כמוך does not really fit: from God's silence toward misdeeds it cannot be concluded that He is like the evildoer.
ושם דרך is unintelligible; leg. per Symmachus a reading meaning the blameless way ('den Weg der Lauterkeit'). אראנו בישע = בישעי, pregnant, God being the speaker.
entries.flag: verify proposed reading (ותם?) at high res — OCR garbled

entries.emendation: draw הרבה to v. 3: מחה פשעי הרבה
entries.note: The imperative הרבה/הרב does not fit at all; leg. the adverb, drawn to v. 3 — 'lösche meine grosse Schuld!' — so that v. 4 begins with כבסני.

The old versions read בדבריך statt בדברך — a form chosen for paronomasia with בשפטך; but the latter too must be emended to במשפטך. The למען-clause grounds not the preceding stichs but v. 8: 'damit Dein Wort und Dein Ausspruch, dass Du die Reue des Sünders wünschest, sich bewähre' — an allusion to Ezek 33:11 f.

entries.mt: הֵן־אֱמֶת חָפַצְתָּ בַטֻּחוֹת וּבְסָתֻם חָכְמָה תוֹדִיעֵנִי
entries.emendation: הן אמת חפצת בְשָׁבִים ובספר חכמה הוֹדַעְתַּנִי
entries.note: Extraordinarily obscure. The apparent parallel Job 38:36 (where טחות must be a constellation) does not help; LXX here τὰ ἄδηλα καὶ τὰ κρύφια, Pesh. with a possessive. This much is certain: the final verb may not stand in the imperfect but, as LXX (ἐδήλωσάς μοι), in the 2nd person perfect הודעתני. חפץ is construed with ב, so the ב of בטחות is the preposition; setting ש for ט, ב for ח, and the plural ending ים- for ות- (p. 134, 13) yields בַּשָּׁבִים = שבי פשע 'the penitent', and statt ובסתם leg. ובספר. The whole: 'Sieh da, in Wahrheit hast Du an Reuigen Wohlgefallen, und im Gesetzbuche hast Du mich Weisheit gelehrt'.

entries.emendation: מאזוב (parallel to משלג); or transpose תחטאני ואטהר מאזוב
entries.note: The psalmist cannot have demanded that God Himself sprinkle him with hyssop; daher leg. מאזוב — 'more (pure) than hyssop' — as the parallelism with משלג requires; perhaps also to be transposed: תחטאני ואטהר מאזוב. His translation: 'Entsündige mich, mehr als mit Ysop werde ich lauter'.

מדמים is unintelligible — 'blood-guilt' resists the context, and it cannot stand for אנשי דמים since the psalmist does not complain of persecutors; he fears only the consequence of his sinfulness, which by the era's view (Ezek 33:8 f.) is death. Also wohl to be read ממות, as Ps 56:14: 'Rette mich vom Tode, Gott'.

Hypothetical, LXX εἰ ἠθέλησας — so לו (cf. p. 300 on Ps 40:7): 'Denn wünschtest Du Opfer, ich würde sie geben; aber Brandopfer magst Du nicht'. (Vv. 20–21, the plea for Jerusalem's walls, belong integrally to this exilic psalm and are no later appendix — against Olshausen and Hupfeld.)

entries.mt: מַה־תִּתְהַלֵּל בְּרָעָה הַגִּבּוֹר חֶסֶד אֵל כָּל־הַיּוֹם
entries.emendation: הגבר; חסד = 'Schmähung' (Aramaic חסדא), with על + noun per Peshitta
entries.note: What the 'hero' should be doing here is incomprehensible; leg. הגבר 'o Mann', as v. 9. And חסד: LXX took it not as grace but as wickedness (ἀνομίαν), more aptly Aquila and Symmachus as reviling (ὄνειδος) — the Aramaic חסדא. Then כל היום fits well but אל not at all; Pesh. has the preposition על plus a preserved noun (the reviled pious one), giving the verse a logical run: 'Was rühmst du dich der Schlechtigkeit, o Mann? der Schmähung für den Unschuldigen Tag für Tag?' The רעה of stich a governs; the psalm's target is a priest, not Doeg (the historical superscription rests on a false guess).
entries.flag: verify the noun read from Peshitta (חסיד/חסין?) at high res

entries.mt: הַוּוֹת תַּחְשֹׁב לְשׁוֹנֶךָ כְּתַעַר מְלֻטָּשׁ עֹשֵׂה רְמִיָּה
entries.emendation: divide: הוות תחשב ‖ לשונך כתער מלטש; עשה → עֲשׂה (infinitive)
entries.note: Translators and interpreters joined הוות תחשב with לשונך without reflecting that the 'tongue' cannot plan; the verse must be divided otherwise: הוות תחשב — לשונך כתער מלטש (so M. Sachs). And the participle עשה does not fit; leg. the infinitive: 'Unheil sinnest du, deine Zunge ein Messer, glatt geschliffen, Arglist schaffend'.

entries.emendation: יתשך (from נתש); יְחִתְּךָ (from חתת); מאהל → מאהלו
entries.note: יתצך cannot derive from נתץ, which is used only of demolishing a building; daher leg. יתשך from נתש 'uproot'. Of יחתך the interpreters give a bad etymology (חתה means only 'rake'); it derives from חתת 'shatter' and must be pointed accordingly. And מאהל is absolutely unclear; gewiss leg. מאהלו, the ו from the following word — from His, God's, tent, the Temple: the psalmist's enemy frequented the Temple, i.e. belonged to the priesthood (fitting the climax ושרשך מארץ חיים, the holy land, cf. Ps 27:13). Symmachus and Pesh. read מאהלך, but it would be strange had the older translators missed a ך; a ו is more easily overlooked.

entries.emendation: a verb of rejoicing; add ויאמרו at verse end (versions)
entries.note: Why should the pious feel fear at the sight of the wicked man's downfall? Surely rather joy, as Ps 107:42, Job 22:19; so also Pesh. 'they will rejoice'. וישמחו can hardly have been corrupted into וייראו — more likely a closer form. And three old versions read at the verse's close ויאמרו (LXX καὶ ἐροῦσιν, Pesh., Targum), introducing the quotation of v. 9.
entries.flag: verify the proposed joy-verb at high res — OCR garbled

entries.note: יעז בהותו gives no sense. Pesh. בקנינה, Targum בממונו — also leg. בהונו 'in his wealth': 'trotzte auf sein Vermögen'.

ואקוה שמך is ungrammatical — לשמך would be required. Daher leg. אחוה 'proclaim' (interchange of ק and ח, p. 126, 7), which suits נגד חסידיך: 'in Gegenwart der Frommen werde ich verkünden', and cf. Ps 54:8 אודה שמך כי טוב.

In Ps 53 עלילה (so rightly Ps 14:1) is corrupted into עָוֶל, which is pleonastic beside the preceding verbs; likewise התעיבו (Ps 14) is right against והתעיבו (Ps 53). עלילה is poetic (except in Deuteronomy) for פֹּעַל.
סר (Ps 14:3) is more correct than סג, since that verb is not otherwise used in Qal; conversely כלו here is better than הכל of Ps 14.

entries.mt: פִּזַּר עַצְמוֹת חֹנָךְ הֱבִשֹׁתָה … אֱלֹהִים מְאָסָם
entries.emendation: בדור צדיקים עדת עניים תבאישו כי ה׳ מחסם
entries.note: The text of Ps 53:6b gives no sense at all — what חנך should mean cannot be determined, and it misled the Greek and Syriac translators into absurd renderings. Evidently פזר arose out of בדור, the word צדיק fell out, and עצמות חנך arose out of עצת עני; further תבישו was corrupted to הבישתה and מחסהו/מחסם to מאסם. Ps 14's text (emended — see there) gives the better sense.
בשמך is suspect; leg. בימנך, as Ps 138:7 (ש and י similar in Old Hebrew script, and a מ dropped): 'Gott, stehe mir mit Deiner Rechten bei'.

entries.mt: זָרִים קָמוּ עָלַי … לֹא שָׂמוּ אֱלֹהִים לְנֶגְדָּם
entries.emendation: זדים (per Ps 86:14); שמו → שמוך with אלהים as vocative
entries.note: The parallel passage Ps 86:14 has זדים 'the insolent' — Targum reads so here too. And in b the parallel there has ולא שמוך, so that אלהים is vocative: 'sie halten Dich, Gott, nicht gegenwärtig'.

entries.mt: הִנֵּה אֱלֹהִים עֹזֵר לִי אֲדֹנָי בְּסֹמְכֵי נַפְשִׁי
entries.note: הנה אלהים עזר לי sounds factual, but the whole psalm is petition. Daher leg. היה עזר לי (as Ps 30:11; interchange of ה and נ, p. 136e): 'Sei Gott mir Beistand'. And statt בסמכי נפשי leg. במבקשי — 'gegen die, so mein Leben suchen'.

The Keri ישיב (Hiphil) is incongruent, since God is addressed only in the second person; correct is ישוב Kal, so also the versions: 'Möge das Böse auf meine Gegner zurückkehren'. And באמתך הצמיתם gives a skewed sense; leg. בחמתך (Schorr): 'in Deiner Zornesgluth hemme sie!'
Striking, since נדבה is itself a kind of sacrifice. Parallel Jonah 2:10 בקול תודה אזבחה, where evidently leg. אזמרה; likewise here בנדבה אזמרה = ברוח נדיבה: 'Mit Hingebung will ich Dir singen'.
ראתה, third person, is likewise incongruent; LXX ἐπεῖδεν, Pesh. — read the second person ('Du hast mein Auge sehen lassen').
entries.flag: verify proposed form (הראתה?) at high res — OCR garbled

entries.emendation: אריד = corruption of אמרר; ואהימה → ואהמה
entries.note: The stem רוד/ריד can mean neither 'roam' nor 'lament'; it is a corruptel of מרר (or מרד) — he similarly emends Jer 2:31 (רדנו → מרדנו), Isa 15:3 (ירד בבכי → מרר בבכי), even Judg 11:37 (וירדתי → ומרתי 'bitterly lament'). אריד בשיחי is like Isa 22:4 אמרר בבכי — so rightly LXX ἐλυπήθην. And ואהימה is certainly miswritten for ואהמה (v. 18) or ואהמיה (Ps 77:4): 'ich klage bitterlich in meinem Unmuth und wimmere'.

entries.mt: מִפְּנֵי עָקַת רָשָׁע … כִּי־יָמִיטוּ עָלַי אָוֶן
entries.emendation: עקת → צעקת or צוקת; ימיטו → יעמיסו
entries.note: For עקת leg. צעקת or צוקת, since עקה (Aramaic for צוק) is without example in Hebrew: 'des Frevlers Wuthgeschrei'. And ימיטו עלי און can be derived neither from מוש nor from נסה; leg. יעמיסו 'they load upon me' (cf. Ps 73:8): 'wenn sie mir Unheil aufbürden'.
פלצות 'shuddering' cannot 'cover' — its verb is אחז. LXX σκότος, better Pesh. טללי מותא, i.e. צלמות; likewise Ezek 7:18 (וכסתה אותם פלצות leg. צלמות), cf. Ps 44:20: 'bedeckten mich mit Düsterheit'.

entries.mt: אָחִישָׁה מִפְלָט לִי מֵרוּחַ סֹעָה מִסָּעַר
entries.note: אחישה מפלט gives no sense; leg. אבקשה 'I would seek myself a refuge' (interchange of ב and ח, p. 130, 3). And in b, for סעה unzweifelhaft leg. a storm-word (סופה): 'vor wehendem Winde, vor Sturm'.
entries.flag: verify second emendation (סופה?) at high res — OCR garbled

entries.note: As transmitted it cannot be right — first destroy the tongue and then divide it! Pesh. has for פלג the substantive (פלוגתא), i.e. פֶּלֶג לשונם 'the dividedness of their tongue'; and statt בלע leg. בלל 'confound' — an allusion to the confusion of tongues, Gen 11:9: 'Verwirre, mein Herr, theile ihre Sprache'. עיר is of course Jerusalem (unless בעיר ה׳ is to be read). The construction requires joining the first part of v. 11: כי ראיתי חמס וריב בעיר יומם ולילה יסובבוה על חומותיה.

entries.emendation: strike one בקרבה; read ואון ועמל בקרבה הוות ולא ימיש
entries.note: To set the construction right, one of the two occurrences of בקרבה must be struck — neither LXX nor Pesh. has both. Read ואון ועמל בקרבה הוות ולא ימיש. The remaining word הוות is still unintelligible; vielleicht an emendation with ה/ח and י/ז interchange (pp. 126b, 132, 7).
entries.flag: verify his proposed replacement for הוות at high res

entries.mt: כִּי לֹא־אוֹיֵב יְחָרְפֵנִי וְאֶשָּׂא לֹא־מְשַׂנְאִי עָלַי הִגְדִּיל וְאֶסָּתֵר
entries.emendation: לוּ איב יחרפני ואשא לוּ משנאי עלי הגדיל ואסתר
entries.note: The hypothetical sense that forces itself on the reader is confirmed by LXX (εἰ ἐχθρὸς ὠνείδισέν με … εἰ ὁ μισῶν …) yet missed by all interpreters: read לו twice — 'Denn schmähte mich ein Feind, so ertrüge ich es …'. To הגדיל עלי supply פיו or עקב (cf. p. 306 on Ps 41:10).

Vv. 13–15 and 21–22 speak of a single, personal enemy, while before and after (vv. 16, 20) several enemies are in view; the singular verses disturb the connection and must be moved together — in the order 12, 16–20, 13–15, 21–22 (so also Hupfeld). Before 21–22 there is wohl a lacuna, to be supplied roughly as Ps 41:10 (גם איש שלומי … הגדיל עלי עקב).

ערך means 'row, order, valuation'; here it can only be 'of my order, my station' — the same class of singers (like ממחלקות הלויים), for both moved in the Temple; the psalmist being a Levite singer, so too was his false friend. אלופי from אלף 'be accustomed', consuetus, confidant; מידעי wohl miswritten for מודעי (as Ruth 2:1, Kethib מידע, Keri מודע).
ברגש is unintelligible (LXX ὁμονοίᾳ 'concord' is mere guessing). Wohl leg. ברנה, the ש dittographed from the following word: 'in Gottes Haus mit Jubel gingen'.

entries.mt: יַשִּׁימָוֶת (כתיב) / יַשִּׁיא מָוֶת (קרי) עָלֵימוֹ … כִּי־רָעוֹת בִּמְגוּרָם בְּקִרְבָּם
entries.note: Kethib one word, Keri ישיא מות, so also the versions — but they explain ישיא oddly as 'come upon'. One can keep the text and explain ישיא as from נשה 'make forget' (also with א, Jer 23:39 ונשיתי אתכם נשא), only statt עלימו leg. עמלמו 'their misery' (often so miswritten): 'Möge der Tod ihr Elend vergessen machen' — to which ירדו שאול חיים is parallel. The close כי רעות במגורם בקרבם remains unintelligible (neither 'dwellings' nor 'assemblies' gives an unforced sense; cf. Job 18:19).
leg. the future, as v. 20: 'und er wird meine Stimme hören'.

entries.mt: פָּדָה בְשָׁלוֹם נַפְשִׁי … כִּי־בְרַבִּים הָיוּ עִמָּדִי
entries.note: פדה cannot be perfect (of a fact) but must be imperative, as Targum פרוק — the content of the psalmist's prayer. And כי ברבים היו עמדי gives absolutely no sense; leg. כַּבִּים or כְּרַבִּים 'like archers' (both forms occur: רבב קשת; Job 16:13 רַבָּיו); עמדי, like עם, also in hostile sense: 'denn wie Pfeilschleuderer waren sie mit mir'.

entries.mt: יִשְׁמַע אֵל וְיַעֲנֵם וְיֹשֵׁב קֶדֶם סֶלָה אֲשֶׁר אֵין חֲלִיפוֹת לָמוֹ
entries.emendation: וִיעַנֵּם 'humble them'; ישב כרובים (or ישב בשמי קדם); סלה → כַּלֵּם; חליפות → חֲמָלוֹת
entries.note: ויענם leg. Piel 'humble them' (LXX ταπεινώσει). ושב קדם is without analogy; leg. either וישב כרובים ('Du, Thronender auf den Cherubim') or ישב בשמי קדם. The סלה in mid-verse is certainly wrong (p. 94; Pesh. lacks it); leg. כלם 'destroy them' (cf. Ps 76:4). And חליפות is unintelligible — it would best suit the parallelism as 'mercy' or 'faithfulness' (Hupfeld); but then one must read חמלות (cf. לחמלה): 'vernichte sie, da kein Mitleid bei ihnen ist'.

entries.mt: חָלְקוּ מַחְמָאֹת פִּיו וּקְרָב־לִבּוֹ … וְהֵמָּה פְתִחוֹת
entries.emendation: חלקו מחמאות פניו; וקרב → וחרב; פתחות = פְּתִיחוֹת 'daggers'
entries.note: חלקו מחמאת פיו is incongruent; leg. פניו (LXX πρόσωπον, Pesh.; interchange of פיו and פניו, p. 140) — parallel to רכו דבריו — and in a leg. the plural מחמאות (so rightly Gesenius, who only mistook פיו): 'Glatter denn Rahmblume ist sein Gesicht'. וקרב לבו 'his heart is war' is too bold a metaphor; leg. וחרב 'a sword'. And פתחות are not 'drawn' but, as Aquila (λόγχαι) and the Quinta to Mic 5:5 (πατεφθείας) show, 'daggers, lances' — פתיחות (cf. Mic 5:5 בפתחיה leg. פתיחיה; perhaps also Job 41:21 תותח leg. פותח = פתיח).

entries.emendation: — (context obscure; perhaps the enemy's ironic words)
entries.note: The train of thought is again dark. Perhaps these are the enemy's ironic words ('Wirf nur …'), as Ps 22:9, Isa 66:5 (אמרו אחיכם שנאיכם … יכבד ה׳ ונראה בשמחתכם). The word יהבך is obscure.
לא יחצו is emended — his translation: 'sie werden ihre Tage nicht vollenden. Ich aber vertraue auf Dich.'
entries.flag: verify proposed verb at high res — OCR garbled

entries.note: שאפני the versions rightly render 'tread on' (LXX κατεπάτησε; cf. Amos 2:7, from שוף Gen 3:15). But לחם ילחצני cannot be right — the participle cannot serve as nomen agentis; leg. לחם ילחמני (Kal as Ps 35:1) or לחץ ילחצני: 'den ganzen Tag bedrängt er mich'.

The כי-clause is striking since it merely restates the fact; but רבים here means 'the great' (p. 162), and statt מרום leg. per LXX (ἀπὸ ὕψους) ממרום 'from their height, high station', as Ps 73:8: 'denn Mächtige befehden mich aus der Höhe'.

entries.mt: יוֹם אִירָא אֲנִי אֵלֶיךָ אֶבְטָח … בֵּאלֹהִים אֲהַלֵּל דְּבָרוֹ (vv. 4–5, 10–12)
entries.emendation: יום אקרא (Hupfeld); refrain both times: ביום אקרא אני אליך אבטח זה ידעתי כי אלהים לי באלהים אהלל תמיד באלהים בטחתי לא אירא מה יעשה אדם לי
entries.note: יום אירא is nonsense; leg. אקרא as v. 10 (Hupfeld). But then vv. 4–5 must be made wholly equal to vv. 10b–12 as identical refrains — what is missing in the one supplied from the other (זה ידעתי in v. 4 from v. 10; אני אליך אבטח in v. 10 from v. 4); only so is the train of thought coherent (trust → certainty אלהים לי [supply עוזר לי, cf. Ps 54:6] → praise → no fear of creatures). In the refrain באלהים אהלל דבר is obscure — since neither דבר nor דברו (v. 5) fits, wohl leg. תמיד, as Ps 44:9 באלהים הללנו כל היום (interchanges ת/ד, ד/ר, ב/מ, pp. 122, 123d, 131d): 'Gottes rühme ich mich stets'.

'My words grieve'? Unintelligible. Targum has for דברי the version 'on my account', i.e. על דברי; and יעצבו Pesh. renders מתמלכין, i.e. 'they take counsel' — giving a simple sense matching the parallel member: 'Den ganzen Tag halten sie meinetwegen Berathung'.

entries.mt: יָגוּרוּ יִצְפּוֹנוּ (קרי) הֵמָּה עֲקֵבַי יִשְׁמֹרוּ כַּאֲשֶׁר קִוּוּ נַפְשִׁי
entries.emendation: יגודו; המה → חכה ('the hook'); supply לאבדני at the close (or קוו → אוו)
entries.note: יגורו is unintelligible; leg. יגודו 'they band together', as Ps 94:21 (so Symmachus συνήγοντο; likewise he emends Ps 59:4 יגורו עלי, Hos 10:5, and Hos 7:14 יתגוררו → יתגודדו). And המה יצפינו — 'what do they hide? and why the emphasis they?' — leg. חכה 'the hook' (also used of catching men) statt המה, which suits יצפינו: 'legen heimlich Fussangel'. At the close, to כאשר קוו נפשי supply לאבדני (as Ps 119:95), or vielleicht leg. אוו statt קוו.

entries.mt: עַל־אָוֶן פַּלֶּט־לָמוֹ בְּאַף עַמִּים הוֹרֵד אֱלֹהִים
entries.emendation: אל תתן פלט למו; עמים → עריצים
entries.note: על און פלט למו has found no satisfying explanation (the emendation פלס is false — that verb means only 'weigh exactly'). A radical cure is needed: אל תתן פלט למו (confusion of אל and על, p. 195, 6): 'Gewähre ihnen keine Rettung'. And עמים הורד is gewiss miswritten for עריצים: 'im Zorne stürze die Gewaltigen, Gott!'

entries.mt: נֹדִי סָפַרְתָּה אָתָּה שִׂימָה דִמְעָתִי בְנֹאדֶךָ הֲלֹא בְּסִפְרָתֶךָ
entries.emendation: צעדי ספרתה עתה שימה דמעתי לנגדך הלא בספר תכתב
entries.note: The hardest verse of the psalm. The versions had other readings of נדי (LXX τὴν ζωήν μου, Symmachus τὰ ἔνδον μου, Pesh. תודתי); the Greek shows a צ stood where נ now stands, leading to צעדי ספרתה 'Thou hast counted my steps' (Job 14:16; 31:4, 37 צעדי יספור). Further, the idle אתה must be read עתה (cf. Ps 40:6). For דמעתי the versions have the plural; בנאדך LXX render ἐνώπιόν σου, Pesh. קדמיך — they read לנגדך. And for הלא בספרתך Pesh. has 'in the book': the word divides בספר + תך, the latter a fragment of תכתב. Since הלא stands for הא in lively speech and construes with the future, the whole runs: צעדי ספרתה עתה שימה דמעתי לנגדך הלא בספר תכתב — with אלהים drawn over from the preceding verse. To write in 'the book' is בספר זכרון (cf. Ps 139:16): 'Meine Schritte hast Du gezählt, jetzt lege meine Thränen vor Dich, ja, schreibe sie in das Buch (der Erinnerung)!' Then v. 10a fits: when God notes the singer's tears, the enemies will retreat (perhaps supply further as Ps 9:4).

נדריך is gewiss incorrect, since otherwise only נדרי occurs; Pesh. also has the first-person suffix. The ך of נדריך is a lengthened ו belonging to the following verb: עלי אלהים נדרי ואשלם תודת לך: 'Aufgelegt habe ich mir Gelübde, und werde Dir Dank zahlen'.

entries.mt: כִּי הִצַּלְתָּ נַפְשִׁי מִמָּוֶת הֲלֹא רַגְלַי מִדֶּחִי … בְּאוֹר הַחַיִּים
entries.emendation: כי חלצת נפשי ממות את עיני מן דמעה כלא רגלי מדחי … בארץ החיים
entries.note: The parallel Ps 116:8–9 has חלצת and adds את עיני מן דמעה — which gives the right text here: the mention of 'tears' could least of all be lacking, given the weight laid on them in v. 9, and to tears suits חלץ 'free', not הציל; so חלצת is the more correct here. With הלא רגלי מדחי the interpreters can do nothing; leg. כָּלָא 'kept my foot from falling'. And באור החיים is per the parallel to be emended בארץ החיים (so Pesh. בארעא דחיי) — the holy land (p. 247). The whole is an anticipated song of thanks.
גמר 'vollenden' (an Aramaism) disturbs the sense; LXX εὐεργετήσαντι, i.e. גמל — 'zur Macht, die mir wohlthut'.

entries.emendation: move סלה from mid-v.4 to end of v.3
entries.note: LXX and Pesch. have διάψαλμα (סלה) at the close of v.3, and LXX lacks the סלה in the middle of v.4, where it is in any case suspicious (so too Aquila and the Sexta, per Field's Hexapla). In v.3 סלה was pushed out by the preceding עלי and slipped a line down into the middle of v.4.

LXX had the same word but as feminine noun (εἰς ὄνειδος = לחרפה), so it cannot be right; leg. מכף 'from the hand of', and for שאפי Pesch. has the plural (בעלדבבי), i.e. שֹׁאֲפַי — his translation: 'wird mich aus des Feindes Hand retten'.

'Unter Löwinnen' is too strong an image, and the plural of לביא is לבאות, not לבאים. Targum rightly במצע שלהובין 'amid flames'; cf. ארץ תלאובות 'heat'. With following להטים (Targum supplies גחלים) a correct image results: 'inmitten von Flammen und lodernden Kohlen'.
Statt אשכבה leg. אשכנה 'I dwell', gaining pregnancy of expression via Isa 26:9 (his translation: 'Ich weile unter Flammen').
All the ancient versions read the Kal רומה, yet the Piel רוממה is necessary, transitive governing כבודך: 'Erhebe über die Himmel ... Deine Herrlichkeit'. Likewise in the refrain v.12.

entries.emendation: a verse has fallen out, perhaps אזמרה לשמך
entries.note: After v.6 a verse introducing v.7 must have dropped out, since v.7 gives the motive of the song (the foes' plots foiled); etwa אזמרה לשמך.
כפף is in any case incorrect; LXX κατέκαμψαν, i.e. plural כפפו. (שיחה = שוחה = שחת; נפלו בתוכה is anticipation, as at Ps 35.)

כבוד taken as 'soul' is inadmissible even as metaphor; the parallel Ps 108:2 (אף כבודי, without עורה) is even less intelligible. Necessarily read a word meaning 'my song' (his translation: 'Erwache, mein Lied') via letter-confusion from כבודי.
entries.flag: exact proposed form (שירי?) and the letter-substitution details garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.note: The article on הנבל is incongruent beside anarthrous כנור; the ה is a dittograph of the preceding עורה.
Refrain; as in v.6, leg. the Piel רוממה.
אלם is unintelligible; leg. אלים 'Mächtige, Fürsten' (o. S. 250) — the question is addressed to the princely judges. Dyserinck likewise reads אלים but in the sense 'gods', which is unfitting.

V.3 forms the antithesis to the question of v.2, hence leg. אך statt אף (o. S. 199). And בלב ... תפעלון is nonsense — one cannot 'do, act' in the heart; Pesch. כלכון, i.e. כלכם: 'Indess begeht ihr alle Ungerechtigkeit'.
זרו is likewise unintelligible; read a verb parallel to תעו in the second half ('Es freveln die Ungerechten von Mutterschooss').
entries.flag: proposed form garbled in OCR — likely זדו (ד/ר confusion), verify at high res

entries.note: יאטם is a strange form, and the Hiphil of this verb is unused; therefore simply leg. the participle אטם ('so ihr Ohr verschliesst'), matching the participial description of the deaf adder.
entries.flag: proposed form partly garbled in OCR (אטם?) — verify

entries.note: כמו per Targum אמטולהון 'on their account', so leg. למו 'against them'; and since ידרך has no subject it must be imperative, addressed to God: 'drücke Pfeile gegen sie ab'.
Statt יתמללו leg. יתחוללו 'may they be wounded' ('mögen sie verwundet werden'). ימאסו = ימסו (so all interpreters); יתהלכו למו is a second predicate, not a relative clause to מים.
The כ is to be drawn to נפל, i.e. כנפל 'wie die Fehlgeburt'; תמס is accusativus respectus, 'im Zerfliessen'.
If אשת here is 'woman' (not 'mole', as the Talmud takes it), the form is in any case construct (cf. Deut 21:11, 1 Sam 28:7), so a word has perhaps fallen out after it.
Leg. בלי חזות שמש 'ohne die Sonne zu schauen', since the plural חזו would be disturbing (the subject is singular).

Since סירות means only 'pots' (not 'thorns' — the old Greek versions confused it with סירים), יבינו cannot be right: pots cannot understand. Read a verb meaning 'zubereiten, gar machen' ('Ehe eure Töpfe die Stachelpflanze gar macht'); אטד is an edible thorn-plant (per the Talmud) — evidently a proverbial phrase.
entries.flag: proposed form garbled in OCR (יכינו? יבשלו?) — verify at high res

entries.note: The first (כמו־חי) is dittographed and missing in Pesch. as well; for the last leg. חרול, a kind of thistle ('wie Dornstrauch').
ישערנו is unintelligible; LXX and Aquila read otherwise (reading garbled in OCR).
entries.flag: LXX/Aquila reading illegible in OCR — verify at high res

entries.note: Leg. imperfect יחזה: 'so er Strafe sieht' (future contingency, not past).
'Spalten' (ימחץ) does not fit; read with Krochmal a verb meaning 'röthen' — his translation: 'seine Füsse wird er in des Frevlers Blut röthen' (cf. Isa 63:1 חמוץ בגדים).
entries.flag: proposed form garbled in OCR (יחמץ?) — verify at high res

entries.note: The plural שפטים beside אלהים is unfitting; leg. singular with suffix שפטם 'der sie richtet auf Erden'. (פרי in a. is not fully intelligible, since it does not otherwise mean 'reward'.)
Leg. יגודו 'they band together' ('es rotten sich gegen mich Freche zusammen'), as he emends the same verb at Ps 56:7 (cf. Ps 94:21). לא פשעי as Gen 31:36 — the psalmist asserts his innocence.

The petition against the foes begins only in v.6 with a solemn invocation, so v.5b cannot already contain one. לקראתי is meant in a hostile sense; instead of the Niphal read Piel יכוננו 'they prepare', עורה must be a substantive as its accusative (etwa ארב 'ambush'?), and statt וראה leg. ורעה: 'bereiten mir entgegen Schrecken(?) und Leid'.
entries.flag: the proposed noun for עורה garbled in OCR (ארב?) — verify at high res

entries.note: כל הגוים is as unfitting here as in Pss 9-10; leg. הגאים 'the arrogant', parallel to בגדי און (cf. Ps 9:6). His translation: 'heimzusuchen die Hochmüthigen'.
ישובו does not fit the picture (developed from v.15-16, the fuller doublet): leg. ישבו, and statt לערב leg. לארב — 'Sie sitzen zur Lauer, knurren wie die Stadt umkreisende Hunde'. Likewise v.15.

ינועון (as v.16 המה ינועון לאכל) is evidently more correct than יביעון, since what follows in the doublet suits it: the insolent, compared to dogs, roam the city to devour — figuratively, as Prov 30:14 (לאכל עניים מארץ).
The continuation בפיהם חרבות בשפתותיהם has its parallel in Prov 30:14 (חרבות ... מאכלות); wohl leg. בשפתותיהם מאכלות 'auf ihren Lippen [Messer]'.
At the close supply אמרים ('und sprechen, wer hört's?'), as Pesch. אמרין מנו שמע.
As in v.6, leg. הגאים 'spottest aller Hochmüthigen'.

entries.emendation: עֻזִּי ... אֲזַמֵּרָה; draw אלהי חסדו from v.11 into the refrain
entries.note: V.10 is evidently the refrain, identical with v.18, so both must read alike: leg. עזי as vocative and אזמרה statt אשמרה, and אלהי חסדו of v.11 still belongs to the refrain ('Meine Macht, Dir will ich singen ... Gott meiner Gnade').

entries.emendation: חַסְדְּךָ(?) as subject of both verbs
entries.note: With אלהי חסדו drawn to the v.10 refrain, v.11 would run short; substitute the noun still hinted at in the Ketib חסדו and preserved in Pesch. (טיבותך 'Deine Gnade') as subject of יקדמני and יראני. Of the two adjacent like-sounding words one was pushed out, the other corrupted.
entries.flag: whether he prints חסדך or חסדו garbled in OCR — verify

entries.emendation: add תּוֹרָתְךָ: פן ישכחו עמי תורתך
entries.note: LXX (μήποτε ἐπιλάθωνται τοῦ νόμου σου) and some codices of Symmachus preserve the old reading, confirmed by Jerome (Epist.): the Hebrew had 'populi mei', not 'populi tui' — hence אל תהרגם פן ישכחו עמי תורתך 'sonst vergässe mein Volk Deine Lehre'. The singer wishes the sinners not sudden death but continued life in abasement as a lesson.

בחילך cannot be right — the word is never used of God (as if = בגבורתך). Rather leg. מנחלתך (cf. Jer 17:4): from God's inheritance, the holy land, he shall banish and scatter them ('zerstreue sie von Deinem Erbe').
מגננו with plural suffix is striking, since the psalmist otherwise speaks only in the singular (משגבי, אלהי חסדי); leg. מגאונם, as v.13 בגאונם — 'erniedrige sie von ihrem Hochmuth, mein Herr!'.
Before חטאת פימו a verb is evidently missing ('[Störe] ihres Mundes Sünde').
entries.flag: proposed verb garbled in OCR (הכשילם?) — verify at high res

entries.note: מאלה ... יספרו is unintelligible; leg. יסורו 'von Fluch und Lug werden sie lassen'.

כלה cannot mean 'vernichte sie', which would contradict אל תהרגם (v.12); it stands for כלא 'hemmen' (cf. Gen 23:6, where יכלה is to be read יכלא), and per Pesch. with suffix, כלאם. ואינמו likewise cannot be right, for they are not to perish; read a verb — 'Hemme mit Ingrimm, hemme sie und zerstreue sie'. The apodosis וידעו כי משל fits this excellently.
entries.flag: replacement for ואינמו garbled in OCR (והניעמו?) — verify at high res

entries.note: As v.7; here in the sense 'mögen sie sitzen' (jussive).
LXX and Aquila γογγύσουσιν, i.e. 'so murren sie' (from לון 'murmur', not לין 'lodge'): unsatisfied, they grumble at not having done enough.
Pesch. ('denn Du bist') = כי אתה אלהים; so also in the v.10 refrain — 'denn Du, Gott, bist meine Wehr'.

The clause is dark; whatever תשובב means, at the opening it must continue the complaint, not yet be a petition (so the Greek versions render it as past: Aquila, Symmachus, Sexta). Moreover אנפת lacks its complement ב with suffix, which surely lies in לנו — leg. בנו — and the remaining verb must also govern ב.
entries.flag: the proposed verb garbled in OCR (הבאשת?) and does not obviously match his translation 'Dich von uns abgewendet' — verify at high res

entries.note: LXX τὴν γῆν, i.e. הארץ: the final ה of הרעשתה belongs to ארץ.
פצמתה is a hapax legomenon; leg. פצחתה 'spalten'. So apparently also Symmachus — the Syro-Hexapla rendering 'Du hast sie gespalten' refers to פצמתה, not (as Field wrongly gives it) to הרעשת.
Must be read as construct יין תרעלה 'Taumelwein'. V.5 shows the preceding description was figurative — the sufferings are a national calamity.

Taken categorically the verse is unintelligible; it is still the complaint, framed as a question — the ה (from the end of the preceding word) is to be drawn to נתתה: 'Hast Du Deinen Verehrern ... gegeben?'

נס as 'banner' does not fit at all; cf. Isa 31:9 (ונסו), which Symmachus rightly renders φυγή 'flight'. Perhaps there and here read a noun meaning 'Zuflucht' ('eine Zuflucht, sich vor dem Bogen zu flüchten').
entries.flag: proposed form garbled in OCR (מנוס? נוס?) — verify at high res

entries.note: No doubt that statt קשט is to be read קשת 'bow', as LXX and Symmachus (ἀπὸ τόξου) and Pesch. (קדם קשתא) read: a flight before the bow has taken place (להתנוסס).
The Ketib ועננו 'erhöre uns' is better than the Qere ענני, for it is the nation that laments and petitions.

אעלזה yields absolutely no sense — 'Ich soll frohlocken? Worüber? Und wer? Gar Gott?' If text-damage is to be assumed anywhere, it is here. Read אעלה זה 'ich soll hier hinaufziehen': through the Masoretes' habit of joining short words, אעלזה arose from אעלה + זה (as מזה from מה זה) and the punctuators made אֶעְלֹזָה of it. The nation speaks this and all that follows; אחלקה 'divide' also means 'possess', likewise אמדד 'measure out' = repossess these districts. עמק סכות is likely the same as עמק בית שאן (Josh 17:16).

'The strength or protection of a head' is a figure without analogy. The מ of מעוז is dittographed from אפרים; the remaining עוז, since ז and ר are often confused (o. S. 128), can be the fragment of a word meaning 'Krone': Ephraim 'meine Krone', while among the tribes Juda shall be the lawgiver, i.e. king.
entries.flag: reconstruction (עטרת?) partly garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.note: Statt התרועעי read with the parallel Ps 108:10 עלי פלשת אתרועע 'soll ich triumphiren'. Cf. Zeph 2:5-9: Philistia, Moab and Ammon shall again belong to Juda — prophesied in Josiah's time, fitting his dating of the psalm.

ינחני must in any case be read for נחני (so LXX τίς ὁδηγήσει); the י was absorbed by the preceding מי (o. S. 139). Pesch. moreover has a more plausible order: מי ינחני עיר ... מי יובילני עד אדום. And since the following verses use the plural, the singular forms may also be emended to יובילנו and ינחנו, the opening plural being resumed at the close. (עיר מצור = the fortified city in Edom, say Petra; parallel Ps 108 עיר מבצר.)
LXX and Symmachus read the phrase differently (δὸς ἡμῖν βοήθειαν ἐκ θλίψεως), 'was richtiger ist'. (ושוא stands for כי שוא, as motivation.)
entries.flag: the reading he prefers garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.note: Leg. the plural נגינות, because elsewhere it is always plural.
The verb עטף in the sense 'to be shrouded in grief, languish' occurs only in Niphal and Hithpael, so here too read the Niphal infinitive.
entries.flag: exact form garbled in OCR — verify

entries.note: Gives no intelligible sense — every rock is higher than the one seeking shelter on it; and lead me whither? Pesch. 'Du hast mich erhöht und getröstet', LXX in part likewise (ὕψωσάς με): leg. בצור תרוממני (interchange of י and ת) or מצוררי 'from my foes', and ותנחמני 'and comfort me'.

entries.emendation: a verse is missing, etwa ואני אשיר עזך
entries.note: כי היית cannot speak of an accomplished fact when rescue is only now being implored; it must be an anticipated song, but then a verse announcing the vow to sing must have preceded (cf. vv.6, 9, which speak of a vow made).

ירשת as 'inheritance, possession' is completely unintelligible. Krochmal's emendation ארשת (as Ps 21:3) is inadmissible, being etymologically dark there as well; wohl, as there, leg. משאלת 'the request of those who fear Thy name'.
Vielleicht leg. תוסף (jussive) — the petition to which Ps 21:5 refers (חיים שאל ממך נתתה לו).
מן is inexplicable; leg. כן (interchange of מ and כ, o. S. 199): 'Gnade und Treue werden ihn so bewahren'. The emendation מה' (in Kennicott) does not satisfy.
The suffix on an infinitive with ל is unusual; either leg. לשלם, or בשלמי 'durch meinen Gesang werde ich mein Gelübde täglich leisten'.
The instrument indication after למנצח על is missing, and statt ידותון leg. לידותון (o. S. 87).

Vv.2-3 are decidedly the refrain, like vv.6-7, so both must read exactly alike: in v.2 leg. דומי as v.6, followed by כי ממנו, and תקותי statt ישועתי, which ought not be repeated in the following verse.

entries.emendation: draw רבה to v.4 as a vocative, etwa יְרִיבַי
entries.note: רבה cannot stand at the close of v.3, or it would differ from v.7 — and the word is senseless anyway ('not totter much? but a little?'). Moreover v.4 lacks the subject of the apostrophe עד אנה: draw רבה over and make of it a vocative ('Meine Widersacher, wie lange...').
תרצחו is a strange form, formally and logically unfitting, and lacks the required accusative; easily emended by transposition to תצריחו 'raise a shout of triumph'.
Etymologically inexplicable; it must be synonymous with צרח. Targum תרגשון 'toben', hence תנהמו or the like (the emendations תתהללו, תתקוממו of Hitzig and Hupfeld do not fit).
entries.flag: second proposed alternative garbled in OCR — verify

entries.note: כלכם belongs to the following clause; statt גדר leg. the feminine גדרה (Olshausen). But דחויה does not fit — it means only 'push away, thrust out', not 'push over'; leg. רפויה 'gelockert' (interchange of ד and ר, o. S. 135).

Only the psalmist himself can have spoken this verse, so leg. להדיחי (objective suffix on the infinitive, = להדיחני), the י drawn from ירצו; what remains, רצו כזב, is to be pointed רֹצֵי כזב 'those who delight in delusion', i.e. idolatry (o. S. 41) — the opponents want to seduce the singer from God's majesty to idolatry. משאתו: the versions waver between third person and first; the former is more correct, referring to God.
בפיו is surely incorrect; the versions have the plural suffix — leg. בפימו.
עם as bare address is without analogy; leg. עמו, God's people, the Anawim (o. S. 26).
'To go up (or bring up) on the scales'? Unintelligible. The frequent interchange of ע and פ (o. S. 134) leads to a verb meaning 'to weigh' (cf. פלס).
