entries.note: Statt מהבל wohl leg. הבל: 'sind sie allsammt nur Hauch'.

'One should not trust in oppression and robbery — do the pious first need that admonition?' Parallel Isa 30:12 (ותבטחו בעשק ונלוז), where נלוז is 'the perverse': in both places leg. בעקש statt בעשק, synonymous with נלוז, and the verse is to be divided otherwise than the punctuators give: אל תבטחו בעקש / ובנלוז אל תהבלו — 'Verlasset euch nicht auf den Verkehrten'.
The close is also unintelligible, since the verb נוב is used only of plants; he proposes another verb ('nimmt er auch an Gut zu').
entries.flag: proposed verb garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.note: Leg. ושתים, as Aquila and Symmachus (καὶ δεύτερον), joining אחת ושתים 'once and twice', i.e. repeatedly — cf. Neh 13:20 פעם ושתים, Job 33:14. זו שמעתי is relative to דבר אלהים: כי עז לאלהים, the power to punish the wicked, with v.13a the grace to reward the good.

entries.emendation: supply אָמַרְתִּי; divide the verse after אֲשַׁחֲרֶךָּ
entries.note: As it stands, an empty tautology; Ps 140:7 has the similar אמרתי לה' אלי אתה, so אמרתי has probably fallen out here. V.2 is in any case too long against the rest, so the part up to אשחרך must be severed as a verse of its own.
כמה is a hapax legomenon; leg. כלה (מ and ל interchanged, o. S. 134), parallel Ps 73:26 כלה שארי.

Symmachus ὡς ἐν γῇ and Pesch. איך ארעא = כארץ; the adjective must be congruent, ועיפה statt ועיף, as Ps 143:6 כארץ עיפה; and בלי מים is tautology — leg. אלי מים 'nach Wasser' (interchange of א and ב, S. 129).

'Schauen zu sehen' can only be excused by artificial exegesis. Statt חזיתך leg. אויתיך (interchanges of א/ח and ו/ז, o. S. 126, 132), giving the parallel of Isa 26:9 and an elegant sequence with v.2: כארץ ציה ועיפה אלי מים / כן בקדש אויתיך לראות עזך וכבודך — בקדש construes with לראות ('to behold Thy might in the sanctuary'), the psalmist being banished from it (cf. Pss 42-43, 61, 84).
'Besser als das Leben ist Deine Gnade' is impossible Hebrew phraseology. Leg. כרב חסדך, a frequent phrase, and לחיים 'for the living' statt מחיים (interchange of מ and ל, o. S. 134).
The incongruence is tolerable (3rd fem. plur. for masc. is frequent, cf. Ps 11:7), but possibly leg. שפתי שבחוך, the י dittographed. The verb שבח is Aramaic, found only in late pieces.
Despite the childish tautology of שפתי and פי the interpreters find nothing to object to. Leg. ושירי רננות (interchange of פ and י, and of ת and ר): 'in Jubelliedern wird mein Mund rühmen'.
'In the shadow of Thy wings I shout for joy' is senseless; leg. אתלונן 'I take lodging' — 'in Deiner Flügel Schatten weilen kann'.
Cannot be right, since דבק requires the preposition ב; leg. דלקה 'pursues after' (o. S. 130).
If b. is to cohere with a., תמכה must be imperative (penultimate stress) with ימינך as accusativus respectus, as Ps 60:7 הושיעה ימינך: 'stütze mich doch mit Deiner Rechten!'.

entries.emendation: לַשָּׁוְא; a verse introducing the foes is missing
entries.note: המה 'they'? — no enemies have yet been mentioned, so a verse speaking of them must have fallen out. And לשואה: LXX εἰς μάτην 'in vain', leg. לשוא.

First make the suffix congruent: יגירום (interchange of ה and ם, o. S. 132); the parallel is Ezek 35:5. The stem must be מגר, as Ps 89:45 מגרתה 'hingeben, preisgeben' — hence leg. a form of מגר here (and correspondingly in Ezekiel).

The foes themselves are surely not the jackals' portion — jackals are no man-eaters but haunt ruins. It can only refer to the foes' dwellings: בתיהם must have fallen out ('ihre Stätten werden der Theil für Schakale sein').
'How does the king suddenly get here?' A radical cure is needed: leg. ועבדך ישמח, as Ps 109:28 (interchanges of ע/ה, מ/כ, ד/ל, o. S. 126, 122, 127).

יתהלל requires the preposition ב (Ps 64:11 בו יתהללו כל ישרי לב); precisely because of the following בו the first בו must have fallen out. הנשבע בו means holding true to YHWH against the idol-cult (cf. Zeph 1:5); the close — the advocates of idolatry (דוברי שקר, cf. Isa 9:14, Hab 2:18, Isa 44:20) will be struck dumb.
More correct per LXX (ἐξελοῦ): 'mögest Du meine Seele retten' (the converse case 2 Sam 20:6, where Targum read והצר לנו for והציל).
מרגשת is not congruent with מסוד in a., which means secret plotting, while רגשה means loud raging. Vielleicht leg. a form of רגז, vexatio (the feminine occurs Ezek 12:18 ברגזה ובדאגה).
Unintelligible as it stands. Pesch. 'their words like arrows': leg. כחצים (the כ lost after the כו of דרכו), and strike the ר of מר — דרכו כחצים דברם 'wie Pfeile ihr herbes Wort abgedrückt'.
Pesch. ולא נתחזון, i.e. Niphal יראו 'they show themselves not' (not 'fear').
Grammatically inexplicable as it stands; leg. יתחזקו — they encourage one another with evil words to the evil deed (so Ibn Ezra, rightly).
יספרו 'erzählen'? Does not fit at all; he reads a verb of hiding ('sie verbergen sich, heimlich Fallstricke zu legen').

entries.note: Statt למו Pesch. לן = לנו, or עלינו as Exod 5:21 ירא ה' עליכם: 'Wer wird uns sehen?'.
תמנו is explicable neither as 1st plur. nor 3rd sing. Targum ('to find pretexts to destroy the innocent') read תמימים or תם (as v.5), which fits excellently: they hunt for guilt in the guiltless.

entries.mt: חֵפֶשׂ מְחֻפָּשׂ וְקֶרֶב אִישׁ וְלֵב עָמֹק
entries.emendation: וְחֹפְשִׂים חָפֵשׂ מִקֶּרֶב איש ולב עמוק
entries.note: Wholly insoluble on the received text, but well explicable through Symmachus and Pesch. (Syro-Hexapla): the close read מקרב איש ולב עמוק, and the riddling חפש מחפש is participle with emphatic infinitive — the whole verse: יחפשו עולות תמים / וחפשים חפש מקרב איש ולב עמוק, 'they probe the inmost heart of the harmless to find guilt' (cf. Prov 20:27 חפש כל חדרי בטן).

entries.mt: וַיֹּרֵם אֱלֹהִים חֵץ פִּתְאוֹם הָיוּ מַכּוֹתָם
entries.note: Vv.8ff. become clear once the tempus historicum is turned to future, as the Greek versions partly and Pesch. and Targum consistently render (Aquila, Targum ויתקלון; even היו as future, Symmachus): 'Möge sie Gott mit dem Pfeile treffen'.

ויכשילוהו is correct (against the interpreters), the suffix referring to לשון; but עלימו is incorrect — leg. עמלימו (cf. Ps 55:16): 'ihre Schlechtigkeiten mögen ihre Zunge straucheln lassen', so that they accuse themselves. יתנדדו is from נדד 'weichen' (Ps 31:12), not from נוד ראש; ראה = plural participle ראי.
Symmachus and Syro-Hexapla 'they will see', which is more correct ('Dann werden es alle Menschen schauen'), with the following verbs likewise future.

entries.emendation: הַשְׂכֵּיל, the ו drawn to v.11 (וְיִשְׂמַח צדיק)
entries.note: השכילו is disturbing: unless one reads with Pesch., it is an infinitive pro finito ומעשהו השכיל, the final ו belonging to the next word — וישמח צדיק.
After ויתהללו supply בו from a. (cf. at Ps 63:12, o. S. 394).

That silence should be praise is a thought without analogy in Hebrew scripture — the Psalter constantly says the opposite, that God's praise be loudly proclaimed. LXX σοὶ πρέπει, Pesch. likewise: leg. נאוה as Ps 147:1; בציון metonymic for the Temple.
V.3 generalizes the fact that God hears the prayer of all beings; supply לכן before כל בשר יבאו.
The singular מני is incongruent with פשעינו; LXX plural (ὑπερεδυνάμωσαν ἡμᾶς): 'Hat das sündhafte Verhalten uns übermannt'. דברי עונת is periphrasis for עונות, like דבר רע.

LXX rightly render as perfect; vielleicht leg. לשכון statt ישכן. It refers in any case to the people privileged to dwell in the Temple courts — probably אשרי העם stood originally, as the plural נשבעה shows ('dass wir geniessen').
קדש היכלך is not intelligible (a superlative as in קדש משכני עליון will not do here); leg. as Ps 36:9 מדשן ביתך — here בדשן (ב and ק confused): 'der Fülle Deines Tempels'.

תעננו does not suit נוראות at all, even in the sense 'grant' (Hos 2:24); necessarily leg. תראנו (tempus historicum): 'Wunderbares zum Heile hast Du uns schauen lassen'. Per the parallel Ps 98:1-3 it alludes to the redemption from Babylon; בצדק is a Deutero-Isaianic catchword for the Heilsveranstaltung (cf. Monatschrift 1881).

ים is incorrect; Targum ('islands of the sea far from the mainland') = איי רחוקים 'die fernen Eilande', of which no prophet spoke as much as Deutero-Isaiah (66:19), the island-world (Asia Minor, Greece) having entered the oriental horizon through Cyrus' conquests.
'Girded with might' would be an insipid image beside מכין הרים בכחו; leg. נאדר בגבורה, as Exod 15:6 נאדרי בכח ('verherrlicht durch Allmacht').

entries.emendation: מוֹצָא וּמַעֲרָב(?), or מוּצָאִים 'those led out'
entries.note: Remains riddling: it cannot without more ado mean east and west. One could read מוצא ומערב (cf. Ps 75:7; Ezek 47:8), but מוצאי בקר is pleonastic and un-Hebrew; possibly it refers to those brought out (מוצאים) of the captivity. תרנין is in any case tempus historicum, causative as Ps 32:11.
The form is abstruse; simply leg. ותשקה 'and hast watered it'.

רבת is too much; the versions guessed right (LXX, Targum 'with produce'), but that does not lie in רבת. Its ת is dittographed as the ת of תעשרנה; the remaining רב transposed gives בר 'Getreide': 'mit Getreide hast Du es bereichert'.
פלג אלהים is the (rain-)cloud, a channel — parallel Job 38:25 מי פלג לשטף תעלה; leg. מפלג אלהים 'von Gottes Himmelskanal'.
Statt דגנם leg. דגנה, referred to the earth (interchange of ה and ם, o. S. 117, 132). But כי כן תכינה is inexplicable; vielleicht leg. כמסכן תכינה 'wie eine Vorrathskammer' full of grain.

The hardest verse of the psalm. נחת ('lay down'? 'wash down'?) with גדודיה 'clods'(?) is without analogy; LXX and Pesch. read 'fruits' (i.e. a form of ניב 'noble fruit') and instead of נחת a form of רבה. On that basis read 'Du hast vermehrt' with 'seine edle Frucht', and turn רוה into the perfect 'Du hast getränkt'; תמגגנה and תברך are tempus historicum.
entries.flag: precise proposed forms garbled in OCR (רוית? רבית ניבה?) — verify at high res

entries.note: עטרת is inexplicable in this context; leg. עשרת 'Du hast bereichert'. שנת טובתך is an enallage for שנה בטובתך.
Surely incorrect, for רעף is always joined with שמים and שחקים. Symmachus (Syro-Hexapla) 'from the richness of Thy clouds' — he can only have read a form of ערפל 'dichte Wolken'.
The Kal is simply transitive 'pour'; since it must here mean 'make fruitful', wohl leg. Hiphil.
'To gird oneself with jubilation' is an impossible trope; leg. a verb of singing, as Isa 55:12 ההרים והגבעות יפצחו רנה ('im Jauchzen jubeln die Hügel').
Not properly symmetrical, and כרים never means 'meadow' (o. S. 286); leg. הרים, in contrast to עמקים: 'die Berge sind mit Heerden bekleidet'.
Too tautological; Pesch. renders שימו by זמרו — leg. שירו כבוד (interchange of מ and ר, frequent).
Incongruent; leg. נוראים, the ם absorbed by the following מעשיך.
Incorrect, since the verb in the sense 'do homage, submit' occurs only in Niphal or Hithpael; leg. יכחשו (Niphal).

entries.emendation: supply אִמְרוּ before לכו וראו (per Pesch.)
entries.note: Pesch. has תאמרון before it — the verse (and v.6, save its close) is put in the mouth of the nations paying homage, who marvel at the Exodus and the Jordan crossing; עברו ברגל is perfectum historicum (so Pesch.).

entries.emendation: שָׂמֹחַ נשמחה בו, joined with משל בגבורתו עולם (v.7) as one verse
entries.note: The close belongs neither logically nor formally to v.6 (too long, unsymmetrical), and v.7 is also too long, its opening disturbing the parallelism — both may be joined into one verse. שם can be neither local (two localities are named) nor temporal (נשמחה is future): wohl leg. שמח נשמחה בו, the psalmist's summons 'wir wollen uns Seiner freuen'.
גוים would not be parallel to הסוררים; so here too leg. גאים 'the arrogant' (cf. S. 176, 179, 376).

Ketib ירים and Qere ירומו are both unfitting, and the proposed Niphal נירם after LXX and Pesch. is without analogy. Leg. 'those apostate from God shall be struck dumb' (ידמו, as Ps 140:9, where ידמו is even more necessary since the negation אל is lacking).
entries.flag: details of the redivision (אל → אֵל, attraction of מ) garbled in OCR — verify

entries.note: השם gives no sense; leg. השמר 'Der unsere Seele am Leben erhalten'.
Leg. מצורה 'siege, Drangsal' (cf. Isa 29:3); so Symmachus πολιορκίᾳ.
מועקה is not Hebrew; leg. מוצקה. (במתנינו remains unintelligible; LXX and Aquila 'on our back'.)
Symmachus and Pesch. (לרוחתא) = לרוחה 'zur Freiheit, Erleichterung'.

Before v.13 the portion of this individual psalm that must have contained the thanksgiving proper has evidently been lost; the train of thought — God heard the psalmist's plea, therefore he brings offerings — begins abruptly.

'Incense with rams?' Unintelligible. אילים must denote a land from which spices were imported (cf. Jer 6:20 לבונה משבא); Havilah is a land of gold and spices linked with Sheba and Ophir (Gen 10:29; 2:11-12) — or perhaps אילת, Elath on the Red Sea, where Arabian and Indian wares and spices were unloaded (wares being named after their emporium).
After ואספרה Pesch. has לכון = לכם, out of which כל arose: 'ich will euch, ihr Gottesfürchtigen, erzählen'.
ורומם is correct neither as verb nor as noun; leg. ורוממתו, the תו absorbed by the following תחת — cf. Ps 149:6 רוממות אל.
ראיתי is inexplicable; leg. החבאתי (interchanges of ר/ח and א/ב; cf. Job 31:33 לטמון בחבי עוני): 'Hätte ich ein Vergehen verheimlicht, so würde Gott mein Gebet nicht erhören'.

entries.emendation: move סלה to end of v.3
entries.note: The pause-word סלה in v.2 has strayed to the wrong place and belongs to v.3 (Hupfeld; cf. o. S. 369) — otherwise the text of this psalm is completely correct save one word.
'Lead? Whither?' Leg. תרחם: 'Nationen auf Erden begnadigst Du'.
תנדף is an incongruent form; Pesch. renders both verbs passively — 'wie Rauch verwehet wird, werden sie verweht werden' (interchange in the personal prefixes, o. S. 135).

To let God 'ride through the desert' like a Bedouin only the indestructible per-nefas exegesis could pass; one says רכב שמים and רכב על עב קל. Simply leg. בעבות 'on the clouds' ('den in Wolken Thronenden'). סלו = 'preisen' (Pesch., Targum; Ibn Ezra rightly compares Prov 4:8).
ביה שמו is inexplicable; leg. ברכו שמו, as Ps 96:2 שירו לה' ברכו שמו.
'Einzige' are not 'Vereinzelte', still less 'Arme' or 'Kinderlose'; wohl read a word for fugitives — 'Gott setzte Flüchtlinge in's Haus'.
entries.flag: proposed form garbled in OCR (נדודים?) — verify

entries.note: Out of כושרות nothing else can be made than מוסרות 'bonds' (interchanges of כ/מ and ש/ס): 'führte Gefesselte aus den Banden'.
The perfect would point to an accomplished fact; Pesch. has the future ישכנו 'shall dwell'; צחיחה stands for ארץ צחיחה.

זה fits neither here nor in the original (Judg 5:5, whence vv.8-9 are borrowed); leg. זע 'der Sinai erbebte' (interchange of ה and ע, o. S. 126). In v.9 הרים נזלו of the original appears to have fallen out.
'Regen sprengen' would be little and does not suit נדבות, which must mean 'reichlich'; leg. תטיף 'liessest Du ergiessen' (interchange, o. S. 133).
In what way is the land 'exhausted'? Leg. ומלאה 'sein Erbe und seine Fülle' (Krochmal); the inheritance is the land of Canaan prepared for Israel.

Gives no sense as 'Thiere' or 'Thierchen', as metonym for Israel without analogy, still less as 'Wachtel' (Hupfeld) — the desert is no longer the subject. Leg. מחיתך ישבעו פה (cf. Isa 57:10 חית ידך, leg. מחית ידך); the following relative clause fits excellently: תכין בטובתך, 'von Deinem Nahrungsmittel sättigten sie sich' (cf. Ps 140:14 ישבו leg. ישבעו).
The close לעני is unintelligible; wohl leg. לעם (either עם אלהים or with absorbed article לָעָם, as v.36), and אלהים belongs to the following verse, with תכין as relative (אשר תכין).

entries.emendation: נָתַן אמר הַמְבַשֵּׂר אֶת צבא רב
entries.note: אמר המבשרות is an impossible connection. Leg. המבשר את צבא רב, and statt יתן (which must first be artificially construed as preterite) simply leg. נתן: 'Der Herr gab einen Spruch, so einer grossen Zahl Heilbotschaft bringt'.
ונות בית is inexplicable; leg. וענות — 'die Sanftmüthige des Hauses wird Beute theilen' (the gentle dove being a trope for Israel); שלל also means 'Gewinn' (Ps 119:162).

שפתים = משפתים 'Hürden', as Judg 5:16 (למה ישבת בין המשפתים), so here too leg. שכן statt שכב; the subject can only be the preceding ענות, hence אם תשכן, the ending ־בון dittographed from בין. אם = 'wenn auch': though she rest idle between the sheepfolds, she shall yet have gain — the wings of the gentle dove are covered with silver.

entries.mt: בְּפָרֵשׂ שַׁדַּי מְלָכִים בָּהּ תַּשְׁלֵג בְּצַלְמוֹן
entries.emendation: בפרש שרי מלכי צְבָאוֹת שֶׁלֶג וְצַלְמָוֶת(?)
entries.note: On the received text this is 'zum Verzweifeln', though all old versions had it. Jedenfalls leg. שלג וצלמות (Krochmal; his ברד statt בה lies too far). Since v.12(13) says מלכי צבאות, so probably here too: the undivided letters may be redivided as מלכי צבאת שלג בצלמות. A word is missing — vielleicht ברד, or a verb; in any case a reminiscence of Josh 10:11 (the hailstones on the Canaanite kings). Dyserinck's בהשלחם בצלמות does not commend itself.
entries.flag: letter-details of the redivision garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.note: For the four-fold הר LXX have thrice הרי, and v.17 has הרים גבננים; so leg. הרי. And statt אלהים leg. אלפים 'Stierberge' (o. S. 346): an apostrophe to the peaks of Bashan — 'Ihr Rinderberge, Berge Baschans'.
Durchaus leg. תרקדון 'why do ye leap' (cf. Ps 29:6 ירקידם ... לבנון and o. S. 197).

שנאן is inexplicable; a Greek variant of LXX points to ישרון, so רבתים אלפי ישורון = רבבות אלפי ישראל (Num 10:36), with רכב as 'Thronwagen' and אלפי as 'clans' (not thousands): 'Gottes Thron zwei Myriaden der Familien Jeschuruns'.

entries.emendation: supply: אדני בם יָרַד עַל סיני בקדשו
entries.note: The half-verse remains difficult unless a word-gap is assumed: supply ירד על — אדני בם (= בתוכם, in their midst) ירד על סיני, and בקדש per Pesch. בקדשה 'in His holiness'; so roughly Targum with homiletic paraphrase.

God taking captives on high and receiving gifts among men? Riddling, though each word is clear. In any case באדם must be emended to בארץ or באדמה (o. S. 198): the subject of עלית can be the people (as v.24), למרום has הרים to be supplied, and the מתנות are the allotted portions (גורלות) of the land God gave the tribes — continuing the narrative of the wandering and the conquest.

Pesch. gives the hold ('and apostates shall not dwell before God'): leg. ואך statt ואף, as v.7b, hence ואך סוררים לא ישכנו בה. The stranded אלהים is probably the fragment of a lost verse — from here a transition to another train of thought follows; LXX draw אלהים to the next verse (κύριος ὁ θεὸς εὐλογητός).

'Der uns auflegt'? Not properly intelligible. Vielleicht עומד לנו 'who stands by us' (Koh 2:9), but that is Neo-Hebrew; Pesch. 'who assigns our inheritance' suggests יעמיד לנו ירושתו statt ישועתנו — which would give good sense, v.21 (האל לנו אל למושעות) being otherwise a tautology.
'Exits, ways of rescue' with למות is unusual; ממות would at least be more logical.
קדקד שער is untenable; leg. רשע (Dyserinck, Krochmal). And מתהלך is not pregnant enough; leg. מתהלל 'so sich seiner Schuld rühmt'.

entries.emendation: מִבֵּין שִׁנַּיִם אשיב, אֲשִׁיבֵם ממצלות ים
entries.note: אשיב מבשן, senseless, should long since have been corrected per Pesch. ('from between the teeth' — so too the talmudic exposition): even if held between the teeth of wild beasts God will draw the people out; and from אשיב ממצלות is to be formed אשיבם — parallel 'aus der Meerestiefe'.
Neither מחץ nor רחץ fits; leg. a form of חמץ 'roth werden' (Krochmal): 'Damit Du röthest Deinen Fuss in Blut' (cf. his identical emendation at Ps 58:11).
מנהו is dark: אחד (Dyserinck) and Krochmal's proposal do not satisfy, nor מלא 'sättigen'; perhaps a short word is to be read with letter-interchanges and the ו struck.

Leg. להיכלך עד (interchange of על and עד, o. S. 127): 'Für Deinen Tempel nach Jerusalem werden Dir Könige Gaben bringen'.
Unintelligible; leg. געלי עמים 'who treat peoples with contempt' (cf. Ezek 16:45 גערה אישה ובניה): 'der Völkerverachtenden'. חית קנה is a figure for Egypt, עדת אבירים the horde of Apis-bulls.
מתרפס = מהתרפס, to wallow (רפס = רפש 'Schlamm'; LXX 'not to wallow'); ברצי כסף is probably transposed and mutilated statt בצברי כסף 'auf Silberhaufen'.
Per the versions read the imperative: 'Zerstreue die Völker, so Kriege lieben!'

Leg. תרים ידיה: 'Aethiopien wird seine Hand zu Gott erheben'.

LXX ἀπὸ τοῦ ἐλπίζειν, i.e. מן + infinitive: 'meine Augen schwinden vom Harren'.
Leg. מצמותי 'than my hair-locks' (Ewald), parallel to שערות ראשי: 'reicher als meine Locken meine Feinde umsonst'.

Völlig sinnlos — one cannot assume the psalmist was accused of robbery and held to restitution; reading it as a proverb is a makeshift. A radical cure: statt גזלתי leg. גמלתי (ז/מ), statt אז leg. אך, statt אשיב leg. טוב (ש/ט): 'denen ich nichts als Gutes vergolten'.
LXX συνέκαμψα: leg. ואענה 'Demüthigte ich meine Seele in Fasten'.

Leg. כטוב, cf. Ps 63:4 and 109:21: 'nach Deiner liebevollen Huld'.
The suffix is unfitting; Pesch. לקבל כלהון — read נגד כל, one letter dittographed: 'in Gegenwart all meiner Feinde'.

entries.note: Why the emphatic אתה? For יספרו LXX προσέθηκαν and Pesch. have 'they added': leg. ואל מכאוב חלליך יוסיפו, and a. parallel to b.: כי אֹתָם אשר הכית רדפו — 'die, so Du geschlagen, verfolgten sie, und zum Schmerz Deiner Verwundeten thun sie noch hinzu'.
Unintelligible; leg. יראו (interchange of ב and ר, o. S. 190): they shall not see the promised salvation (צדקה) — 'dass sie Dein Heil nicht sehen'.
משור פר is tautology; Pesch. 'a fattened bull' — leg. שור בריא 'feiste Opferstiere', and מקרן leg. ממקרין.
Pesch. renders as imperatives: 'Seht's, ihr Sanftmüthigen, und freut euch'.

Pss 70-71 form one connected piece, Ps 70 being the close of Ps 40. להזכיר in the heading is a mutilation of לבי עזבני (Ps 40:13b); Ps 40:12-13 accordingly belong to Ps 70, which must have contained more verses at its opening.
In v.2 רצה is in any case missing at the head, as the doublet Ps 40:14 shows.
Old manuscripts read outright מעוז statt מעון (Norzi ad loc.); cf. the parallel Ps 31:3-4.
Parallel אתה גחי (Ps 22:10); both are to be read alike ('von Mutterschooss an').

Ganz unverständlich; leg. כמו פתי 'wie ein Unbeholfener, Rathloser' — his translation: 'Wie ein Thor bin ich den Fürsten geworden'.

Pesch. עלי, which is more correct (cf. S. 238 and Pss 35:19, 39:8, 40:16): 'meine Feinde würden von mir sprechen'.

יבשו יכלו do not fit together; Pesch. נחפרון = יכלמו (the מ having dropped). And שטני נפשי would properly mean 'my accusers' (o. S. 292), of which the psalm knows nothing; leg. שמרי נפשי, as v.10 שמרי נפשי.
איחל fits neither what precedes nor תהלתך in b.; leg. אהלל: 'Ich werde stets loben und vermehren all Deinen Lobpreis'.

Un-Hebrew and not properly intelligible. If the sense is as Ps 40:6 (עצמו מספר), one would have to read the infinitive (referring to צדקה and תשועה), with כי concessive — 'wiewohl ich sie nicht zu zählen wüsste'. But the reading is not assured.
'Ich werde kommen mit der Macht' is geschmacklos; he reads a verb of proclaiming — 'Ich werde verkünden Deine Macht'.

entries.note: לבדך sounds odd; leg. לנגדך: 'werde Deine Gerechtigkeit vor Dir rühmen'.
ועד הנה still belongs to a. (למדתני = 'geleitet', as Isa 40:14); consequently a word is missing in b. before אגיד נפלאותיך.
Joining לדור לכל יבוא (with the versions) is un-Hebrew; the accent-division is right, only לדור means the living generation (like לדור הזה) and must be vocalized as Ps 22:31.

entries.emendation: read the Ketib plurals הִרְאִיתָנוּ, תְּחַיֵּינוּ, תַּעֲלֵנוּ
entries.note: The Ketib is plural throughout (so Aquila and twice Targum): it refers to the whole people's sufferings, surely the Babylonian exile. ומתהומות הארץ seems to designate Babylonia itself — Deutero-Isaiah likewise calls Babylon מצולה (Isa 44:27, where לצולה leg. למצולה): the exiles from the hill-country called the Babylonian lowland 'the deep'; 'Du wirst uns aus dem Tiefland wieder hinausbringen'.

entries.emendation: גְּדֻלָּתְךָ; draw גם אני from v.22 to v.21
entries.note: The verb is precative, and per LXX (ἐμεγάλυνας... σου) read the second person: גדלתך 'Mögest Du Deine Grösse vermehren'. V.21 is moreover exceedingly short and v.22 too long: draw גם אני over — ותסב תנחמני גם אני 'wirst auch mich trösten' (cf. Gen 27:38 ברכני גם אני); תסב means to take another turn, as it were change of mind.
Pesch. renders as future; the י was absorbed (o. S. 139): 'wenn beschämt sein und erröthen werden, so mein Unglück suchen'.
LXX and Pesch.: leg. לעמך 'Frieden Deinem Volke'.
בצדקה is striking, since simply צדקה would have to stand; he reads a word meaning abundance of blessing (his translation: 'die Höhen Fülle des Heils'), a letter having dropped out.

entries.note: Difficult, and doubtful whether the object is God or the king; LXX had a wholly different reading (καὶ συμπαραμενεῖ). Vielleicht leg. ייראוהו — that they revere him, the king.

entries.mt: יֵרֵד כְּמָטָר עַל־גֵּז כִּרְבִיבִים זַרְזִיף אָרֶץ
entries.note: על גז is unintelligible; leg. על גן 'auf Gärten' (Krochmal). And זרזיף is a suspicious hapax legomenon; leg. ירעיפו 'so die Erde befruchten' (Krochmal).
Leg. צדק 'Es blühe in seinen Tagen das Recht' (so also Krochmal).
Leg. צרים 'Gegner': 'Vor ihm mögen Gegner knieen'.
One cannot possibly say אביון twice in one verse (יחס על דל ואביון ... אביונים); at the close wohl leg. עניים or ענוים — 'das Leben der Sanftmüthigen retten'.

entries.emendation: pluralize all the verbs (וִיחְיוּ וְיִתְּנוּ לָמוֹ ...)
entries.note: The singulars are unintelligible if the reference is to the poor, who figure in the plural before. LXX have plural ויתפללו and יברכוהו; accordingly all the verbs must be pluralized: 'Sie werden aufleben ... und sie werden für ihn beten beständig'.
פסת is inexplicable; leg. שפעת (ס and פ interchanged, o. S. 134, and ש dropped): 'Möge Fülle des Kornes im Lande sein'. From v.16 begins the prayer promised by the sufferers.
'Zittern, rauschen' of grain? He reads a verb of abounding: 'auf Bergesspitzen möge reich sein wie im Libanon die Frucht'.

entries.note: Unintelligible — what is the plural subject? Leg. ערים (cf. Isa 25:2 מעיר לגל): 'aufblühen Städte wie Gras des Feldes'.
ינין/ינון is no word; LXX διαμενεῖ, i.e. יכון: 'Angesichts der Sonne aufgerichtet sein Name'.
To ויתברכו בו LXX have the addition πᾶσαι αἱ φυλαὶ τῆς γῆς = כל עמי הארץ: 'sich mit ihm segnen alle Völker der Erde'.
LXX οἱ ὕμνοι, i.e. תהלות, 'was viel richtiger ist' (cf. o. S. 100): 'Zu Ende sind die Lobgesänge Davids'.

entries.note: As it stands neither symmetrical nor clear; redivide לישראל into לישר אל (Ewald, Schorr): 'gütig für die Aufrichtigen ist Gott, für die Herzenslautern'.

entries.note: חרצבות (elsewhere only Isa 58:6, etymologically dark) cannot have the same sense in both places; here leg. עצבות 'Betrübniss' (Targum ומצטערין). The sequel was already emended by predecessors: למו תם ובריא אולם statt למותם — 'ungebrochen und gesund ist ihre Kraft' (against Hupfeld).
Likewise cannot be correct (cf. his note at Ps 59:14 on אינמו).

entries.note: LXX plural περιεβάλοντο, Pesch. likewise: leg. יעטפו; שית means 'Gewand' (Prov 7:10 שית זונה): 'sie hüllen sich in das Gewand der Gewaltthat'.

Extraordinarily dark. עינמו can only be עונמו 'their guilt' (LXX ἀδικία, Pesch.); the verb Symmachus read as plural, so יצאו; and statt מחלב only מלב or מקרב can be read — cf. Hos 8:10(?), Isa 59:13 הרו והגו מלב דברי שקר: 'Sie ziehen aus dem Innern ihre Schuld'.

Pesch. renders משכיות by 'designs', i.e. מזמות (divined by Olshausen); עברו here means 'to be full, teeming' (Job 21:10, Josh 5:11-12 מעבור הארץ, perhaps Jer 5:28 עברו דברי רע): 'sie sind voll von Anschlägen des Herzens'.

ימיקו is inexplicable; leg. יעמיקו as the contrast of ממרום ('Vertieft sprechen sie vom Bösen'). And עשק is unintelligible; leg. עתק — the phrase דבר עתק is frequent (Ps 94:4): 'Trotz von der Höhe sprechen sie'.
תהלך is an abstruse form; leg. תהלל (cf. v.8's הוללים at Ps 73:3): 'ihre Zunge höhnt auf Erden'.

Riddling — a radical correction is needed. LXX and Pesch. read עמי 'my people, my circle'; statt ישוב leg. יתאו, and statt הלם leg. שלום/שלומם: 'darum begehrt mein Volk ihr Glück' (envies them their prosperity).
Must be symmetrical with the first half; restored by reading מְלֹא 'Fülle' statt מָלֵא. ימצו is in any case an incorrect form — either from מצה or ימצו from מצץ 'einschlürfen'.
ושלוי עולם is unintelligible — it cannot be the predicate, which lies in השגו חיל; leg. the verb ישליו, with עולם also emended.

entries.note: Not symmetrical to ואהי נגוע; leg. per Symmachus (ἐλεγχόμενος) the Hophal: 'und werde gezüchtigt jeden Morgen'.

Unintelligible. Pesch. and Targum render כמו by 'like them', i.e. כמוהם, the syllable הם absorbed by the following הנה (which LXX and Aquila secure with ἰδού). And אספרה cannot be right — those introduced as speaking did not 'narrate' but reasoned; leg. אדברה. Nor is אם right (it cannot be a condition): leg. גם — 'Schon sprach auch ich, dass ich der Menge gleich reden will'.

Here too a radical cure: בניך and פניך are interchangeable (o. S. 121), so read הדר פניך (the ה absorbed from הנה), and statt בגדתי leg. כחדתי (interchanges of ב/כ and ג/ח): 'den Glanz Deines Antlitzes hätte ich verleugnet'.
עמל היא is unintelligible; leg. עמק (cf. Job 11:8, Koh 7:24 עמק עמק מי ימצאנו) — a parenthesis: 'schien tief in meinen Augen'.

עד here can only mean 'ehe', priusquam (Gen 48:5, Exod 22:25, 2 Sam 17:22, Ezek 33:22, Cant.); LXX and Pesch. have the singular ἁγιαστήριον: 'ehe ich in den Tempel eingehe' — whose rebuilding is awaited (a mark of the exilic date).

The verbs are incongruent; per LXX ἔθου read שת (the dittographed ת of חלקות made תשית of it) or שוית. And per v.19 (איך היו לשמה) the opening must likewise read איך (so Pesch.) statt אך: 'Wie hast Du sie auf schlüpfrige Glätte gesetzt'. The psalmist anticipates his wishes as accomplished fact.
The form למשואות is unusual and its etymology not quite certain; leg. לשוחות 'in Gruben' (cf. Ps 57:7).
The versions read מקיץ (LXX, Symmachus ἐξυπνισθέντος, Pesch.); if הקיץ is kept, one must read בהקיץ: 'Wie ein Traum beim Erwachen'. בעיר — LXX ἐν τῇ πόλει σου, in Zion; צלמם remains dark.
Unintelligible; read a verb 'erglühen' (interchange of צ and ם): 'Als sich mein Herz ereiferte'.

entries.note: Not quite correct; leg. אשתומם with כליותי as accusativus respectivus, or outright the plural השתוממו, the ו absorbed from ואני (v.22).

Dark — the Greek rendering κτηνώδης is happy, but the Hebrew is without analogy and in the plural to boot! Wohl read 'ermangelte der Einsicht bei Dir' via multiple letter-interchanges; parallel Ps 92:7.

entries.note: Unintelligible; the כ of כבוד is to be drawn to ואחר, and the remaining letters read as 'by the hand' — 'und Dir nach nimm mich an der Hand' (vielleicht with תאחזני).

entries.note: After כלה שארי ולבבי the second לבבי is dittographed; leg. צורי וחלקי: 'mein Fels und mein Antheil ist Gott für immer'.

רחקיך is incorrect in form. Since יאבדו is future, הצמתה must also be future: leg. והצמתה, the ו absorbed by יאבדו; and כל זונה is to be taken as plural (o. S. 130): 'Du wirst hemmen alle, so von Dir abfallen'.

entries.emendation: divide: ואני קרבת אלהים לי / טוב שתי בה' מחסי
entries.note: Although the Masoretes indicated the right division by the accents, the interpreters draw טוב to a., where it is incongruent with קרבת: 'Mir aber ist Gottes Nähe; gut, dass ich in Gott meine Zuflucht gesetzt'.
LXX add ἐν ταῖς πύλαις τῆς θυγατρὸς Σιών = בשערי בת ציון, missing in the Hebrew text — the psalmist hopes to reach Zion, as he intimated in v.17 (cf. Pss 9:15, 102:22).
פעמיך 'feet' is secured (Symmachus), but one cannot say הרים רגל as one says הרים יד; wohl read a verb of hastening: 'Beschleunige Deine Schritte'.

entries.note: Cannot mean 'ewige Verwüstungen', of which nothing follows — the complaint is only of the foe's din and roaring (v.23 קול צרריך שאון קמיך); leg. לתשאות 'Geräusch': 'wider das andauernde Tosen'.

הרע cannot mean 'maltreat' (used only of persons, with dative); it must mean 'ertönen lassen', hence leg. קול statt כל (or even הרים קול); and for בקדש LXX have ἐν τοῖς ἁγίοις σου = במקדשיך: 'laut lärmt der Feind in Deinem Heiligthum'.
Not properly intelligible; אותות can only be 'Wahrzeichen' (not idols); vielleicht another reading — 'geben ihre Zeichen als Wahrzeichen aus'.

entries.note: Völlig unverständlich — only emendation helps. Targum's 'zerschlagen' read differently; rather leg. יריע (the roaring continues) and, for the dark כמביא למעלה, כמניף (interchanges, o. S. 130): 'Sie lärmen wie beim Hochschwingen der Beile am Baumgestrüppe' (קרדמות בסבך עץ).

All old versions except Targum have θύρας, i.e. פתחיה 'die Pforten' (also Rashi). ועת LXX and Pesch. curiously render as a verb ('they hewed down' — did they read גדעו?); Symmachus νῦν δέ. כשיל is Neo-Hebrew/Aramaic 'axe', כילפות Aramaic 'pick' — vielleicht leg. בכולבות.

Stands for שלחו אש במקדשך, since vv.3 and 7b presuppose the Temple still standing — fire was laid at the Temple gates in the time of Antiochus Epiphanes (1 Macc 4:38); לארץ חללו means profane, not destroy (לארץ = לעפר).

נינם is explicable neither as verb nor as substantive; Pesch. points to another reading. And for שרפו LXX's κατακαύσωμεν is surely a corruptel of the Sexta's καταπαύσωμεν — both render a verb 'let us make cease' rather than 'burn'.

entries.note: כלה is unintelligible; LXX's εἰς τέλος is the Sexta's constant rendering of סלה, which seems to have entered the LXX text from there — סלה must be the right reading, fitting since a new train of thought begins with v.12: למה תשיב ידך וימינך מקרב חיקך סלה.
Cannot be apposition; LXX λαοῖς τοῖς Αἰθίοψιν. Vielleicht leg. לעם לובים 'dem Volke der Lybier'.
Leg. למות or לשחת: 'Gieb nicht dem Tode preis die Seele Deiner Taube'.
LXX 'Thy covenant': the ך dropped before the following כ of כי. 'Dein Bündniss' here appears to mean the religion, Judaism, as in Daniel 11 (ברית קדש).

Dark as it stands: ארץ can only be object of מלאו, whose subject is to be read מחשיכים 'die Dunkelmachenden, Unglückbringenden' (cf. Jer 13:16), with נאות חמס as second accusative (as Ezek 8:17 מלאו את הארץ חמס).

LXX and Pesch.: leg. וקראי שמך — under 'those who call on the Lord's name' the Levites are meant (cf. Ps 99:6), who have praised (ספרו perfect) God's deeds after a deliverance just celebrated in the Temple.

אקח מועד is inexplicable; leg. אקרא מועד — the classical expression for summoning an assembly for judgment (קרא מועד, קרואי מועד): 'Wenn ich die Versammlung zusammenrufe, werde ich in Geradheit richten'. Vv.3-4 are placed in God's mouth.

תכנתי is surely incorrect — תכן means 'zählen' and תקן is late Hebrew; read a verb 'befestigen': though earth and dwellers melt, God holds its pillars firm (supply בל תמוט; cf. Pss 82:5, 93:1, 96:10).
entries.flag: proposed form garbled in OCR — verify

entries.note: Durchaus unverständlich; the parallel Job 15:26 is itself corrupt (as Job 16:14 shows). LXX κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ show בצואר to be a strong corruptel of באדני or באביר (interchange of צ and א): 'sprechet nicht vom Herrn mit Trotz'.
Leg. ממדבר והרים — the southern steppe of Judah and the Lebanon mountains in the north; supply יצא משפט (as Ps 17:2): judgment comes from no quarter of the compass but from God.

מסך = the wine-jug (Isa 65:11, Prov 23:30): in God's hand are cup and jug. LXX ἐκ τούτου εἰς τοῦτο, likewise Pesch.: leg. מזה אל זה 'Er giesset von diesem in jenen'; but the dregs remain for the wicked.
אגיד is out of place; LXX ἀγαλλιάσομαι = אגיל (interchange of ד and ל, o. S. 127): 'Ich aber werde mich für immer freuen'.
אגדע — who speaks that? Read another person ('wirst Du zerbrechen'); and statt צדיק leg. plural צדיקים, per Pesch.
entries.flag: person of the emended verb garbled in OCR — verify

entries.note: Leg. בירושלם (frequent confusion of ישראל and ירושלם; cf. Monatschrift 1880, S. 97): 'in Jerusalem ist gross Sein Name', parallel to 'kund in Juda'.

שלם is another form of שילה (properly שלון/שלום — LXX often render שילה by Σαλήμ): in Shiloh God had only a hut, a tent (Ps 78:60), but in Zion a fixed dwelling, the Temple (מעונה): 'In Silo war Sein Zelt, Seine feste Stätte aber in Zion'.

The closing סלה is suspect — the parallelism is incomplete, and one cannot say שבר מלחמה; reading כלה statt סלה (cf. at Ps 55:20), b. answers a. perfectly: 'Schild und Schwert und Kriegswehr hat Er vernichtet'. שמה is temporal, not local (Sennacherib's army perished at Pelusium, not by Jerusalem).
Theodotion φοβερὸς εἶ = נורא, as below v.8 ('Furchtbar bist Du'); and statt טרף leg. אלף 'Rinderberge' (cf. his emendation at Ps 68:16): 'mächtiger als Rinderberge'.
Incongruent; LXX ἐπιβεβηκότες τοὺς ἵππους, likewise Pesch.: 'entschlummerten Rossesreiter'.
The first אתה is to be emended to עתה: 'Jetzt hast Du Dich furchtbar erwiesen'.
מאז is Widersinn; leg. מעז (as Ps 90:11): 'wer könnte vor Dir bei Deines Zornes Macht bestehen?'
'Feared and was still' contradict each other; leg. ושקעה, as Amos 9:5 (הנוגע בארץ ... ושקעה): 'die Erde erschrak und sank'.

entries.mt: כִּי־חֲמַת אָדָם תּוֹדֶךָּ שְׁאֵרִית חֵמֹת תַּחְגֹּר
entries.note: Inexplicable as it stands. Leg. כי חמת ארם תודך, שארית חמת תחרג (from חרג 'zittern', o. S. 215): even Hamath will acknowledge God, for the remnant left it (after Tiglath-Pileser's deportations, 2 Kgs 16:9) will tremble — cf. Zech 9:2, where Hamath is to confess the God of Israel.

כל סביביו belongs to a. as vocative, and statt יובילו read the congruent imperative הובילו. And למורא is inexplicable even reading τῷ φοβερῷ with the versions; wohl leg. למרום (interchange of א and ם, o. S. 130), supplying למרום ציון, as Isa 18:7 (יובל שי ... אל מקום ... הר ציון).

entries.emendation: אֶצְעָקָה (no waw, temporal); imperative for the second verb
entries.note: The verse turns on correctly parsing the second verb, which must be imperative rather than indicative; accordingly אצעקה (without the waw, per the versions) is temporal, and the doubled קולי אל אלהים is deliberate repetition (palilogy).
entries.flag: the exact grammatical reconstruction is garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.mt: בְּיוֹם צָרָתִי אֲדֹנָי דָּרָשְׁתִּי יָדִי לַיְלָה נִגְּרָה וְלֹא תָפוּג
entries.emendation: בְּיוֹם צָרָתִי דְּרַשְׁתִּיךָ אֲדֹנָי, וְלַיְלָה עֵינִי נִגְּרָה
entries.note: The verse needs an antithesis (day/night) as at Ps 22:3, 42:4, 88:2. ידי cannot be subject of נגרה — the hand does not 'flow', the eye does (already noted by Ibn Ganach); Targum guessed similarly. Read: the corrupted ידי is really the suffix of דרשתי (= דרשתיך), and עיני has dropped out before נגרה.
The verb אזכרה ('I remember') is disturbing — the suffering is present, why remember it? (Ps 42:5 already uses אזכרה in its proper place.) Leg. אזעקה 'I cry out'.
נפעמתי is doubtful; Pesch. חרשת ('was silent'), i.e. leg. נאלמתי 'I was struck dumb'.

entries.emendation: draw מקדם from v.7 into v.6; supply a verb (וְאֶזְכְּרָה) to open v.7
entries.note: As transmitted the verse lacks parallelism; the versions rightly draw מקדם from the following verse into this one (חשבתי ימים מקדם | שנות עולמים). Accordingly v.7 must open with a verb — LXX καὶ ἐμελέτησα, Pesch. — leg. something like ואזכרה. The Masoretic accents divide wrongly; עם לבבי still belongs to the first half.
entries.flag: the exact verb supplied for v.7 is garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.note: יחפש cannot be right, since חפש means only 'search', not 'muse, agonize'. Per the parallel Ps 143:5 (ותתעטף עלי רוחי, בתוכי ישתומם לבי), read here either ויתעטף or וישתומם רוחי (the noun רוח being used as either gender).

entries.mt: הֶאָפֵס לָנֶצַח חַסְדּוֹ גָּמַר אֹמֶר לְדֹר וָדֹר
entries.emendation: delete or isolate אמר: גָּמַר alone (Aramaic 'be finished')
entries.note: 'גמר אמר' — what promise is meant? Most LXX codices lack the word אמר; it appears to be a dittography, or גמר should be read alone (an Aramaism for 'to come to an end').

entries.mt: וָאֹמַר חַלּוֹתִי הִיא שְׁנוֹת יְמִין עֶלְיוֹן
entries.note: Comparing the parallel in Isaiah 63-65, where the same question — has God withheld His mercy? (63:15, cf. 64:11 העל אלה תתאפק ה׳, matching קפץ רחמיו here) — is answered by attributing the plight to the people's own guilt (65:7, 59:2): so here too the psalmist can only cite guilt as cause. Leg. עונתי היא statt חלותי. שנות ימין simply means 'the change, the alteration' (of the right hand).

entries.mt: אזכור (קרי) / אזכיר (כתיב) מַעַלְלֵי־יָהּ כִּי־אֶזְכְּרָה מִקֶּדֶם פִּלְאֲךָ
entries.emendation: prefer Ketib אזכיר; second אזכרה → אזמרה; כי → כן
entries.note: The Ketib אזכיר is more correct than the Qere אזכור. But then the following אזכרה in b. is disturbing; wohl leg. אזמרה, and statt כי leg. כן (as at Ps 61:9).
Dark as it stands; vielleicht leg. מקדם 'from of old' statt בקדש. The following 'מי אל גדול כאלהים' is parenthetical.
entries.flag: exact form garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.note: בני יעקב ויוסף סלה is not symmetrical to a. Symmetry is restored at once if one reads העלית statt סלה (confusion of ס/ע with a dropped consonant; cf. his identical emendation of a closing סלה at Ps 49:14, o. S. 340).

entries.mt: רָאוּךָ מַּיִם ... יָחִילוּ אַף יִרְגְּזוּ תְהֹמוֹת
entries.note: The parallel with Habakkuk 3:10-11 begins here; without deciding at a glance which passage is original and which borrowed, the readings of each may be used to correct the other. Here מים is probably not original, since it would be tautological with תהמות; there (Habakkuk) הרים is the more correct reading.
entries.flag: whether he actually proposes emending Ps 77:17's מים to הרים, or only notes the relationship, is unclear from the garbled OCR — verify at high res

entries.emendation: if Pual retained: מֵעָבוֹת (מ absorbed by the identical letter)
entries.note: If זרמו is Kal, then עבות is its subject (so Pesch. and, per Syro-Hexapla, Aquila: 'the clouds poured forth water'). But if the Masoretic Pual זרמו is kept, one would have to read מעבות, the מ absorbed by the following עבות. Unlike the parallel in Habakkuk 3:10 (מים עבר עבר, which makes no good sense), Ps 77's זרמו מים עבות is here the more correct reading.

Corresponds to the parallel in Hab 3:11 (לאור חציך יהלכו), which is secure there given its own parallel לנגה ברק חניתך. Possibly here אור was corrupted to אף and the ל before חצציך dropped; alternatively, if אף חצציך is original here, the psalmist deliberately altered his Habakkuk source.
בגלגל makes no sense; leg. כגלגל 'like the sound of a wheel' (cf. Ps 97:4, which has ברקיו for the parallel; Pesch. here likewise ברקיך).

entries.mt: אֶפְתְּחָה בְמָשָׁל פִּי אַבִּיעָה חִידוֹת מִנִּי־קֶדֶם
entries.note: משל here means neither 'parable' nor 'maxim' — not a single verse in this long psalm contains a poetic image or a pointed saying. The word must instead carry the general sense 'poetry, verse-composition' (cf. משלים used of epic poets). Nor can חידות mean 'riddle', since everything here is stated plainly. Wahrscheinlich leg. תורות 'teachings', to which the pronoun in v.3 then refers; otherwise the accompanying מני קדם ('riddles of old'?) is also unintelligible.
The participle מספרים is syntactically out of place; leg. נספרה (Pesch. נשתעא 'we will tell'), or supply the infinitive מספר after נכחד — though the ending ־ים then remains unaccounted for.

נשקי רומי קשת cannot be precisely explained, since the etymology of נשק itself is uncertain, though it clearly means 'weapon' in general (sword and spear, not specifically bow). For רומי read רובי, as רבה קשת (Gen 21:20, Ps 18:15) — an archaic word for drawing the bow and loosing arrows. The construct state before an adjective denotes a superlative (as יעצי פרעה): 'the most weapon-skilled of the [archers]'.

entries.mt: וַיּוֹסִיפוּ עוֹד לַחֲטֹא־לוֹ לַמְרוֹת עֶלְיוֹן בַּצִּיָּה
entries.emendation: לַמְרוֹת → a form of מרר, not מרה
entries.note: למרות cannot derive from מרה, which would require את פי as its object (absent here); nor is a transgressed command at issue, only faint-hearted disbelief. LXX render παρεπίκραναν; Pesch. reads a feminine infinitive of מרר. He applies the identical correction at v.40 (כמה ימרוהו), v.56 (וימרו את אלהים), Ps 106:33 (המרו את רוחו), and Isa 63:10 (leg. המרו) — there being two parallel Hiphil patterns, as הניח/הנוח from נוח.
הכריע ('bowed down') can derive neither from כרע by transposition nor be emended to הכניע — both would be too weak beside the preceding ויהרג ('slew'); rather leg. הכרית 'cut off, destroyed'.
Aquila renders ὡς ἀτμόν = כהבל 'like a breath', far more sensible than בהבל. Then בהלה (in the parallel half) can mean 'in haste', as the old versions render it (cf. Lev 26:16 בהלה = בבהלה).
It is striking that the object is appended as a bare noun after the pronoun already implied; Pesch. more correctly has אליו, the ו absorbed by the following word's initial letter.
LXX render with a suffix, ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν = עונם 'their guilt'.

entries.emendation: וינסו traced to אות via הואיתו → התאוו → וינסו
entries.note: וינסו is unintelligible as it stands; probably from אות 'sign' (Hiphil הואיתו), transposed to התאוו and contracted to וינסו — similarly perhaps 1 Sam 21:14 ויתו = ויתאו 'made a sign' (Targum ורשם).
entries.flag: the exact mechanics of the proposed derivation are garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.note: הרג ('slay') is never used of inanimate things; Pesch. suggests another verb, perhaps יגדע 'cut down'. The hapax legomenon חנמל is also uncertain — perhaps a miswriting of אלגביש 'hailstones'.
Leg. the Hiphil וַיַּסְגֵּר (so too Dyserinck); רשף means 'arrow' (cf. Ps 76:4) and is also used of plague-arrows.

entries.mt: עֶבְרָה וָזַעַם וְצָרָה מִשְׁלַחַת מַלְאֲכֵי רָעִים
entries.emendation: וְצָרָה → יְצַו(?); מִשְׁלַחַת → לְמַשְׁחִית(?); מַלְאֲכֵי רָעִים → מַלְאָכָיו רָעִים
entries.note: The verse has no parallel structure, and וצרה does not fit among the synonyms for wrath — wohl statt וצרה leg. יצו. משלחת ('a mission of evil angels'?) is likewise irregular and unique — wohl emend to למשחית 'to destroy'. The construction מלאכי רעים is un-Hebrew; leg. מלאכיו רעים 'His messengers of evil'.
LXX render πρωτότοκα αὐτῶν, i.e. reading אונם with a suffix.

entries.mt: וַיִּטֹּשׁ מִשְׁכַּן שִׁלוֹ אֹהֶל שִׁכֵּן בָּאָדָם
entries.note: באדם gives no good sense; leg. באפרים 'in Ephraim'.
LXX ἐπενθήθησαν 'lamented' (active sense); leg. the active הילילו, matching תבכינה in the following verse.
Targum renders דמתפקח ('awakening'); leg. accordingly מתעורר 'rousing himself' statt מתרונן.

entries.emendation: a noun-form from root בר (purity), parallel to תחנונה from חנן
entries.note: 'With the understanding of his hands' makes no sense — hands are not intelligent. A Greek translator (Theodotion or Symmachus) renders κατὰ καθαρότητα 'in purity', i.e. reading a form from the root בר (as in בור כפיו 'purity of hands'); this would be a distinct noun-form comparable to תחנונה beside החנון (from חנן).
אכל must be read as the plural אכלו (LXX ἔφαγον), matching the parallel Jer 10:25 (כי אכלו את יעקב). ואת נוהו refers to the Temple, as 2 Sam 15:25 (אתו ואת נוהו).
Leg. plural אסירים, per LXX τῶν πεπεδημένων; likewise at Isa 10:4 (כרע תחת אסיר) he takes אסיר as = אסירים, and Pesch. there has אסירא.
A participle must be supplied ('הלך לפני', 'who went before'), parallel to the two preceding participial phrases רעה ישראל and נהג כצאן יוסף (v.2) — all these participles carry perfect (past) force.
After אלהים supply צבאות, as in the parallel refrains (vv.8, 20).
One cannot properly say 'smoke/rage against a prayer' — one can rage against a person, not a prayer. Vielleicht leg. שתמת בתפלה, as Lam 3:8 שתם תפלתי 'He shut out my prayer'.

entries.mt: הֶאֱכַלְתָּם לֶחֶם דִּמְעָה וַתַּשְׁקֵמוֹ בִּדְמָעוֹת שָׁלִישׁ
entries.note: LXX and Symmachus render the verbs with first-person-plural suffixes (ἐψώμισας ἡμᾶς, ἐπότισας ἡμᾶς): leg. האכלתנו ... ותשקנו. And שליש (elsewhere only Isa 40:12, a large dry-measure) cannot be right — one cannot drink from a measure! Vielleicht leg. ראש 'venom' (as in ראש ומרורה).
Statt מדון LXX have ἀντιλογία, Pesch. likewise; wohl the more correct reading is מריבה.

כסו is a Pual form with short o (like מְאֳדָּמִים and similar verbs); accordingly one must read הרים מצלה 'the mountains [were covered] by its shade' (so Pesch. טורא מן טללה). ארזי אל are the cedars of Lebanon, 'planted by God'.

That ארה means 'to pluck' is not certain — Cant 5:1 (ארתי מורי עם בשמי) cannot mean 'plucked' either, since fragrance is smelled, not plucked (perhaps leg. הרחתי there, 'I have smelled'). Here Pesch. renders the verb by דש 'trampled', which also fits the overall sense better.

entries.emendation: מִיָּעַר → מִיְּאֹר (with ל as litera suspensa)
entries.note: In חזיר מיער the ל is a litera suspensa, per talmudic evidence; the word was originally read מיאר ('from the Nile'), but to make the verse allude to the boar as symbol of Rome it was read מיער — not altered outright, but with a letter superscripted (as with נ in משה). The sense: the swine of the Nile — Egypt (יאר) — ravages the vine, Israel.
זיז שדי is not properly understood, and ירענה ('grazes it') is too weak a verb for the destruction described; leg. something stronger.
entries.flag: the proposed stronger verb is garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.mt: וְכַנָּה אֲשֶׁר־נָטְעָה יְמִינֶךָ וְעַל־בֵּן אִמַּצְתָּה לָּךְ
entries.emendation: transpose with v.17a; ועל בן → ועל בן אדם (as LXX/Pesch. at v.18)
entries.note: The second half of v.16 is very dark — בן 'shoot' is without analogy, and the preposition על (with פקד) denotes hostile treatment; moreover LXX and Peshitta read בן אדם here too, as at v.18, where the sense is decidedly hostile. If compelled to read ועל בן אדם here as well, it must be taken in malam partem — and then the abrupt v.17b (מגערת פניך יאבדו), whose subject is otherwise unclear, becomes intelligible: it can only refer to בן אדם, continuing v.16b's thought. The 'son of man' is the adversary who mistreats the vine and garden; אמצתה לך (used twice) means God strengthened this enemy to his own people's harm — he might be called איש ימינך, though better leg. איש ריבך. Both verses gain plain sense once v.17a (שרפה) is joined to v.16a and vice versa: 'ופקד גפן זאת וגנה אשר נטעה ימינך שרופה באש כסוחה, ועל בן אמצתה לך מגערת פניך יאבד'. The hostile prince is most likely Necho of Egypt, who dealt harshly with Judah after Josiah's death.
כסוחה, as Isa 5:25 (נבלתם כסוחה); supply the comparative כ, which drops before the identical letter: ככסוחה 'like a felled thorn-bush'.

'שאו זמרה' cannot properly be said in Hebrew (cf. Job 21:12 ישאו בתוף וכנור, where likewise one must read ישירו): leg. שירו 'sing' here too. And תנו is irregular — when and why would a hand-drum be 'given'? Leg. תפו תף 'beat the drum'.
עדות ביהוסף is an abstruse form; leg. עדות ביהודה ויוסף, equivalent to ביהודה וישראל or ביעקב וישראל — God appointed this feast for both halves of the nation, at the time He went out against Egypt.

entries.mt: הֲסִירוֹתִי מִסֵּבֶל שִׁכְמוֹ כַּפָּיו מִדּוּד תַּעֲבֹרְנָה
entries.note: דוד as 'basket' or 'pot' would be a tasteless image here. Pesch. more fittingly has 'from the fetters' (מן אסוריא). Vielleicht leg. מעבוד or מעבודה 'from servitude, labor'.

entries.mt: לוּ עַמִּי שֹׁמֵעַ לִי יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּדְרָכַי יְהַלֵּכוּ
entries.emendation: שֹׁמֵעַ → שָׁמַע (perfect); יְהַלֵּכוּ → הָלְכוּ (perfect, the extra י dittographed)
entries.note: לו is followed by the participle שמע; leg. instead the perfect שמע, per LXX εἰ ἤκουσε and Pesch. And the י in the last word (יהלכו) is dittographed; leg. the perfect הלכו (LXX ἐπορεύθη) — all perfects throughout, conveying that it is now over, beyond redress.

entries.mt: וַיַּאֲכִילֵהוּ מֵחֵלֶב חִטָּה וּמִצּוּר דְּבַשׁ אַשְׂבִּיעֶךָ
entries.emendation: וַיַּאֲכִילֵם ... מִצּוֹף דְּבַשׁ ... יַשְׂבִּיעֵם (all third-person plural)
entries.note: LXX render throughout with third-person-plural suffixes (ἐψώμισεν αὐτούς ... ἐχόρτασεν αὐτούς); Pesch. likewise has not אשביעך but the third person שבעם: leg. ויאכילם ... ישביעם. Also emend מצור to מצוף 'from the flow [of honey]' (so Schorr and Dyserinck).

entries.mt: אֱלֹהִים נִצָּב בַּעֲדַת־אֵל בְּקֶרֶב אֱלֹהִים יִשְׁפֹּט
entries.note: בקרב אלהים is surely a corruption; perhaps originally בית ישראל (cf. Hos 10:15 ככה אעשה לכם בית אל, LXX οἶκος τοῦ Ισραηλ). The separated syllable הים should be read הוא: 'בקרב ישראל הוא ישפט' — 'in Israel's midst He judges'.
דל ותום in v.3, repeating דל again at v.4 (דל ואביון), is stylistically inadmissible; leg. תם statt יתום.

entries.mt: אָכֵן כְּאָדָם תְּמוּתוּן וּכְאַחַד הַשָּׂרִים תִּפֹּלוּ
entries.note: כאדם fittingly means obscure people without family standing. But וכאחד השרים ('like one of the princes') is untenable; leg. instead a phrase meaning 'like one of the lowly ones' (הצעירים).

entries.mt: קוּמָה אֱלֹהִים שָׁפְטָה הָאָרֶץ כִּי־אַתָּה תִנְחַל בְּכָל־הַגּוֹיִם
entries.note: כי אתה תנחל is not properly intelligible; leg. תמשל 'for Thou dost rule over all the nations'.

אשור is probably a corruption of גשור; Pesch. has גשור for האשורי at 2 Sam 2:9, and Gen 25:18's באכה אשורה (of Ishmael's descendants) likely also equals גשורה — they can hardly have reached Assyria proper. The Geshurites of the northern Hauran border fit both the geography and Judas Maccabeus's campaigns (Karnaim, Bosra) far better than true Assyria.
En-Dor is nowhere else mentioned as a battle site; it is probably a miswriting for עין חרד, where Gideon encamped and struck the Midianites (Judg 7:1).
'Heart and flesh sing' cannot be right — heart and body can rejoice, but not sing or cry aloud. Leg. יכלו or יכספו, 'long, yearn for'.

entries.mt: גַּם־צִפּוֹר מָצְאָה בַיִת וּדְרוֹר קֵן לָהּ ... אֶת־מִזְבְּחוֹתֶיךָ ה׳ צְבָאוֹת
entries.emendation: supply הַרְאֵנִי (or רְאֵה) before את מזבחותיך
entries.note: A gap is presupposed before את מזבחותיך (Judah Ibn-Balam ad loc., cited by Ibn Ezra); supply a verb such as ראה or הראני, as 1 Sam 15:25 (הראני את...).

entries.mt: אַשְׁרֵי יוֹשְׁבֵי בֵיתֶךָ עוֹד יְהַלְלוּךָ סֶּלָה
entries.note: עוד יהללוך can mean neither 'still/future' nor 'constantly' fittingly here; LXX's rendering (εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων) guessed at עד עולם ועד, which doesn't even suit. Leg. סוד (confusion of ע/ס), turning יהללוך into the noun מהלליך: 'סוד מהלליך' — the circle of the Levites, elsewhere called קראי שמו (Ps 99:6).

entries.mt: אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם עוֹז־לוֹ בָךְ מְסִלּוֹת בִּלְבָבָם
entries.emendation: עוֹז־לוֹ → מְעוּזוֹ; מְסִלּוֹת בִּלְבָבָם → הָלֹךְ בָּם מְסִלּוֹת(?)
entries.note: אשרי אדם forms a contrast with ישבי ביתך (v.5) — those who do not dwell in the Temple but visit it from time to time. עז לו leg. מעוזו (the מ absorbed). And מסלות בלבבם is untenable — neither מעלות (ס/ע confusion, LXX ἀναβάσεις) nor Hupfeld's forced כסלות 'hope' works; in any case the plural בלבבם is incongruent with the singular עז — leg. a phrase such as 'הלך בם' along the lines of 'the highways [to Zion] are in their heart'.

entries.emendation: עֵמֶק הַבָּכָא → עֵמֶק הַבְּכָאִים (מ absorbed by the following מעין)
entries.note: עמק הבכא is a proper name (Kimchi, Gesenius, Olshausen), more properly עמק הבכאים, the מ absorbed by the following מעין — a locality where the בכא-shrub (a balsam) grew, in the Valley of Rephaim (2 Sam 5:23), sparsely fruitful per Isa 17:5; עמק רפאים and עמק הבכאים appear to be nearly identical places.

ברכות here means 'blessings' in the sense of fruitfulness (as ברכות שדים); more properly it would be בְּרֵכוֹת 'pools', but that does not suit מורה. Leg. יעטהו (referring back to עמק); מורה = יורה 'the early rain'.

entries.mt: יֵלְכוּ מֵחַיִל אֶל־חָיִל יֵרָאֶה אֶל־אֱלֹהִים בְּצִיּוֹן
entries.emendation: יֵלְכוּ לְהֵיכַל אֵל חַי לֵרָאֹת אֶל־אֱלֹהִים בְּצִיּוֹן
entries.note: מחיל אל חיל יראה makes no sense. Necessarily leg. להיכל אל חי, joining the ל of the second חיל with יראה to give the Niphal infinitive לראה. LXX confirm at the close not just אלהים בציון but אל אלהים, ὀφθήσεται ὁ θεὸς τῶν θεῶν — so the original read ילכו להיכל אל חי לראה(ת) אל אלהים בציון. The deliberate euphemistic change made the verb passive ('be seen') rather than active ('see') where God is the object — a tiqqun soferim. Through fusion of חי with the following ל, only חיל remained.

entries.mt: מָגִנֵּנוּ רְאֵה אֱלֹהִים וְהַבֵּט פְּנֵי מְשִׁיחֶךָ
entries.note: מגננו cannot be vocative — that disturbs the parallelism's symmetry — but must mean 'protector, prince' (cf. Ps 47:10). The verse makes sense once read as the plural משיחיך, 'anointed, favored ones' (as Ps 105:15 אל תגעו במשיחי), probably referring to priests here; accordingly one must also read the plural in a., מגננו 'our protectors'.
The old versions still preserve אחד with טוב (ἡμέραν μίαν, 'one day'); אחד was displaced by the following אלף.

entries.mt: כִּי שֶׁמֶשׁ וּמָגֵן ה׳ אֱלֹהִים חֵן וְכָבוֹד יִתֵּן ה׳ לֹא יִמְנַע־טוֹב
entries.emendation: draw אלהים into the second clause (with LXX)
entries.note: כי שמש ומגן is an unfitting image if שמש means 'sun' — an aggadic reading (Rashi; Midrash Tehillim) rightly takes שמש as 'city-wall battlement' instead (cf. Arabic šams also denoting a comb's radiating teeth), giving both this verse and Isa 54:12 a far better sense. Separately, LXX oddly render חן ואמת אהב ה' — more likely they draw אלהים into the second clause (ὁ θεὸς χάριν... δώσει), so that ה' in b. should be construed with לא ימנע.

entries.emendation: הֶאָסַפְתָּ (interrogative, ה drawn from the preceding סלה); הֱשִׁיבוֹתָ → הֵשַׁבְתָּ
entries.note: Taken categorically (as a statement) the interpreters create a contradiction with v.5b and הפר כעסך (v.7). One is compelled to take v.4 as a question: draw the ה of the preceding סלה to אספת, giving הֶאָסַפְתָּ. This is confirmed by השיבות itself — the Hiphil is never used in this construction, only the Kal (שוב מחרון אפך); so leg. הֵשַׁבְתָּ מֵחֲרוֹן.
הלא אתה would be superfluous; leg. עתה 'now' statt אתה (a frequent confusion of עתה/אתה; cf. Monatschrift 1880, p.1ff.).

entries.emendation: supply/restore בִּי: מַה יְדַבֵּר בִּי הָאֵל (per LXX)
entries.note: From here the psalm answers the desperate question of the opening, though the transition is a little obscured; sense is eased by the LXX's preserved addition τί λαλήσει ἐν ἐμοὶ ὁ θεός = מה ידבר בי האל. What the psalmist proclaims is not his own thought (מלבו) but divinely inspired, as if רוח ה׳ דבר בי, answering the opening complaint. Accordingly vv.10ff. are spoken in God's name but in the third person, not as direct quotation.

entries.mt: צֶדֶק לְפָנָיו יְהַלֵּךְ וְיָשֵׂם לְדֶרֶךְ פְּעָמָיו
entries.note: Doubtful whether this verse refers to God or to the people. Statt לדרך Pesch. has לארעא = לארץ, but that reading rather obscures the sense than clarifies it.
b. is too short; supply כי ידעתי, as Ps 56:10.

יחד לבבי, 'unite my heart', yields no graspable sense; LXX εὐφρανθήτω ἡ καρδία μου and Pesch. likewise point (from חדה 'to rejoice') to an apocopated imperfect: 'let my heart rejoice to fear Thy name'.

entries.emendation: supply an opening clause, e.g. מַה־טּוֹב מְעוֹן ה׳ or אַשְׁרֵי שֹׁכֵן מְעוֹן ה׳
entries.note: Before יסודתו בהררי קדש there is certainly a gap. Various fillers have been tried — Ewald's is nonsense; Olshausen's מה ידידה עיר אלהים does not fit, since עיר is feminine while the following יסדתו is masculine. Vielleicht מה טוב מעון ה', or אשרי שכן מעון ה' יסודתו וגו'.
מדבר בך is harsh; wohl a different reading is intended.
entries.flag: the proposed replacement is garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.emendation: הַאַזְכִּיר (interrogative); insert the divine name יָהּ, crowded out between לידעי and the next word
entries.note: אזכיר רהב ובבל is intelligible only as a question: leg. האזכיר, the interrogative ה absorbed by the following letters. הזכיר means 'praise, extol' (Isa 12:4, 62:6); רהב is Egypt, the storming sea. The divine name יה, originally present (should I extol these nations to those who know Yah?), was crowded out between the י of לידעי and the ה of the following word.

The hardest verse in the psalm, explicable only via Peshitta (וכל דאתמככו בכי = וכל מעני בך, 'all who are afflicted in thee'). ושרים is rendered 'singing' by Aquila and Symmachus (LXX omits it). For כחללים, Aquila has 'as with dances', Symmachus better 'as with flutes' — leg. כחלילים.
Not symmetrical with the psalm's own later usage; leg. שועתי, as at v.14.
נחשבתי is inexplicable; leg. נמשלתי, as Ps 143:7.

כמו חללים שכבי קבר should contain an intensification (beyond 'reckoned with the dead') that the received text doesn't convey. LXX add τραυματίαι καθεύδοντες, i.e. כמו חללים משלכים, recalling Isa 14:19 (ואתה השלכת מקברך) — 'thrown from the grave', unburied. Leg. accordingly כמו חללים משלכי קבר or מקבר.
Pesch. renders במצלות by 'in the shades of death', i.e. בצלמות.

entries.mt: עָלַי סָמְכָה חֲמָתֶךָ וְכָל־מִשְׁבָּרֶיךָ עִנִּיתָ סֶּלָה
entries.emendation: סָמְכָה → שֻׁפְּכָה (transposed letters); עִנִּיתָ → הֶעֱבַרְתָּ; סֶּלָה → עָלָי
entries.note: סמכה חמתך עלי is unintelligible; leg. by transposition שפכה 'poured out'. And וכל משבריך ענית סלה is wholly unintelligible — LXX 'all Thy waves Thou didst bring upon [me]', Pesch. similarly with no equivalent for סלה. Statt ענית leg. העברת (cf. Ps 42:8 משבריך עלי עברו), and statt סלה leg. עלי (confusion of ה/ע): the whole reading וכל משבריך העברת עלי.
דאבה cannot mean 'ache, hurt' here; Pesch. and Symmachus (ἐτάκη 'melted') point instead to a verb meaning 'flow' — either זבה or the Aramaic דבה.

entries.mt: עָנִי אֲנִי וְגֹוֵעַ מִנֹּעַר נָשָׂאתִי אֵמֶיךָ אָפוּנָה
entries.emendation: וְגֹוֵעַ → יָגֵעַ; מִנֹּעַר → מִכֶּלֶא; אֵמֶיךָ נָשָׂאתִי → אֶעֱנֶה(?); אָפוּנָה → אָפוּגָה
entries.note: וגוע would mean 'dying'; Pesch. and LXX ('in toils') point instead to a form of יגע/ינע 'weary'. מנער ('from youth') makes no sense; leg. מכלא 'from imprisonment' (cf. Ps 107:39, Isa 53:8). אמיך נשאתי is dark, since אימים is not secured in the plural and construes poorly with נשא; the versions render the phrase as a verb, suggesting אענה rather than אמיך, though נשאתי then remains unclear. And אפונה is untenable; leg. אפוגה (Michaelis), 'I grow numb'.
entries.flag: this crux is only partly resolved even by Graetz and is heavily garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.note: צמתתוני is redundant, too much; צתני would fully suffice.

entries.emendation: מַחְשָׁךְ → a verb form, חָשַׂכְתָּ (per Pesch.), or infinitive מֵחְשֹׁךְ (as v.10a)
entries.note: Readings vacillate between מהשך and מחשך (Rashi still read the latter); the transmitted form cannot be placed grammatically. Best is Pesch., which reads a verb ('Thou hast withheld from...'), or an infinitive parallel to v.10a.
LXX εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, i.e. לעולם, gives the most correct sense.

entries.mt: כִּי־אָמַרְתִּי עוֹלָם חֶסֶד יִבָּנֶה שָׁמַיִם תָּכִן אֱמוּנָתְךָ בָהֶם
entries.emendation: אָמַרְתִּי → אָמַרְתָּ (2nd person, God speaking); אֱמוּנָתְךָ → אֱמוּנָתִי; reorder to שָׁמַיִם תָּכִן בָּהֶם אֱמוּנָתִי
entries.note: LXX εἶπας: leg. אמרת — from here God's own speech begins. LXX/Pesch. render 'shall be established' for the heavens-clause: leg. congruently אמונתי statt אמונתך, since God is speaking; the ך was dittographed from the following ב (in בהם). The construction as transmitted is impossible, a kind of tmesis for the intended בשמים תכון אמונתי (Dyserinck emends similarly in part).
LXX μέγας καὶ φοβερός; leg. רב הוא ונורא.

entries.emendation: חֲסִין → חָסִיד; supply אִם before יָהּ
entries.note: חסין ('mighty') is out of place, since God's Huld — not His strength — is praised here; leg. instead a form of חסיד (cf. Jer 3:12, כי חסיד אני, used of God). Before יה LXX have εἰ, i.e. אם.
ידעי תרועה is unintelligible; leg. תעודה 'teaching, testimony' (cf. o. S. 154), perhaps also at Num 23:21 (leg. תעודת statt תרועת).
ירומו is not symmetrical with יגילון in the parallel half; leg. an equivalent verb of rejoicing there too.

entries.emendation: עֵזֶר → נֵזֶר ('crown'); שִׁוִּיתִי understood as שַׂתִּי, 'I have set'
entries.note: His translation ('Ich habe eine Krone auf einen Helden gelegt') shows he reads נזר 'crown' statt עזר 'help' (also Dyserinck).
entries.flag: exact letters of the OCR'd Hebrew proposal uncertain — verify at high res

entries.note: ישיא בו is unintelligible — deriving it from נשא 'lend' (so too LXX ὠφελήσει) is absurd; leg. ישאף בו 'shall snort/pant against him', the correct construction of the verb with ב.
Leg. אסיר statt אפיר (several interpreters).
ואתה זנחת leg. ועתה (cf. o. S. 116, 125, a recurring אתה/עתה confusion). And התעברת עם leg. על, Symmachus πρός, per the necessary construction.
נארת ברית cannot be said, since נאר/נער means 'shake off, overthrow'; leg. נבלת 'profaned'.
Passersby do not 'plunder' an unenclosed field, but trample it; leg. accordingly a verb of trampling rather than שסה 'plunder'.
entries.flag: the exact proposed verb is garbled in OCR — verify at high res

entries.note: Targum has 'backward' (לאחורא); leg. accordingly supply אחור: 'Thou hast turned back the edge of his sword'.
מטהרו is dark; vielleicht leg. עטרתו 'his crown' (in part per Krochmal).
ימי עלומיו as 'days of his youth' is senseless here; leg. שלומיו or שלותו 'his peace, tranquility'.
לנצח should be read with an interrogative ה prefixed, echoing the opening עד מה.
זכר leg. אדני, as v.51 (several interpreters). And מה חלד is unintelligible; the Syro-Hexapla's Symmachus points to מה חיי (cf. Ps 39:6).

entries.mt: זְכֹר אֲדֹנָי חֶרְפַּת עֲבָדֶיךָ שְׂאֵתִי בְחֵיקִי כָּל־רַבִּים עַמִּים
entries.emendation: עֲבָדֶיךָ → עַבְדֶּךָ (singular); בְחֵיקִי → בְּחַיַּי; כָּל־רַבִּים עַמִּים → כָּל דִּבַּת עַמִּים(?)
entries.note: חרפת עבדיך (plural) is incorrect; Pesch. has the singular עבדך. שאתי בחיקי is unintelligible; Pesch. has 'during my life' (בחיי). And כל רבים עמים is certainly incorrect, since in Hebrew the attributive adjective must follow its noun; Aquila read ἀδικίας = רעות, leg. instead רבות or more correctly רבה (cf. Ezek 36:6) — the whole phrase probably read שאתי בחיי כל דבת עמים 'the scorn of the peoples' (confusion of the endings ־ים/־ות).
Leg. מעוז 'stronghold' statt מעון 'dwelling' (cf. o. S. 428, his identical emendation elsewhere).

entries.emendation: keep אַתָּה אֵל together at the close of v.2 (against LXX, which draws אל into v.3 as a negation)
entries.note: LXX have only σὺ εἶ (=אתה) at the close of v.2, drawing אל into the next verse as the negative particle (אל תשב, 'return not'). Better: leg. אתה אל at the end of v.2 ('Thou art God'), which the unnegated form תשב in v.3 itself supports.

entries.mt: תָּשֵׁב אֱנוֹשׁ עַד־דַּכָּא וַתֹּאמֶר שׁוּבוּ בְנֵי־אָדָם
entries.emendation: עַד־דַּכָּא → עַד־דַּכְיוֹ (drawing the ו from ותאמר); וַתֹּאמֶר → וְתֹאמַר (future)
entries.note: Draw the ו of ותאמר back to form עד דכיו, and statt the perfect ותאמר leg. the future וְתֹאמַר, per Aquila's ἐρεῖς.

entries.mt: כִּי אֶלֶף שָׁנִים בְּעֵינֶיךָ כְּיוֹם אֶתְמוֹל כִּי יַעֲבֹר
entries.emendation: כִּי יַעֲבֹר → אֲשֶׁר עָבַר (the י of יעבר a dittograph)
entries.note: LXX 'yesterday', Pesch. 'that passed': leg. אשר עבר, the י of יעבר being dittographed, כי read as the relative אשר.

entries.mt: זְרַמְתָּם שֵׁנָה יִהְיוּ בַּבֹּקֶר כֶּחָצִיר יַחֲלֹף
entries.emendation: זְרַמְתָּם → זְרַמְתָּנוּ (or עַמְתָּנוּ); שֵׁנָה יִהְיוּ → שְׁנוֹת חַיֵּינוּ; delete the first בַּבֹּקֶר as dittograph (or read כַּיֶּרֶק)
entries.note: זרמתם is unclear as a verb, and its object is oddly third person when the psalm otherwise uses first-person plural throughout; leg. in any case זרמתנו (or, by letter-interchange, עמתנו). שנה ('sleep') cannot stand — what has sleep to do here? LXX 'years', Pesch. likewise: leg. שנים; but then יהיו is entirely unfitting — leg. שנות חיינו and delete the first בבקר as dittograph of the second (Hupfeld), or read כירק as at Ps 37:20: giving שנות חיינו כירק כחציר יחלף.

entries.mt: בַּבֹּקֶר יָצִיץ וְחָלָף לָעֶרֶב יְמוֹלֵל וְיָבֵשׁ
entries.emendation: וְחָלָף → corrupted, unresolved; יְמוֹלֵל → יִמַּל (the ל a dittograph)
entries.note: The morning/evening antithesis belongs properly to b.; hence וחלף here is unintelligible, clearly badly corrupted. ימולל should be read passively (de Wette) or, more correctly, יִמַּל — the ל being a dittograph.
עלמנו is inexplicable as usually pointed; Symmachus κρύφια ('hidden things') points to עלומנו.

entries.emendation: הֶגֶה → a Hebraized Persian word for 'spider/spider-web'
entries.note: הגה ('sound, thought, sigh') fits nothing here. LXX offer two translations, 'like a spider(-web)' and 'meditation' (from הגי); Pesch. likewise 'like a spider-web', a Persian loanword also found in the Talmud (Sanhedrin 99b, Sukkah 52a), rightly explained by Rashi as 'spider'. הגה is thus the Hebraized form of this Persian word.

entries.mt: יְמֵי־שְׁנוֹתֵינוּ בָהֶם שִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה וְאִם בִּגְבוּרֹת שְׁמוֹנִים שָׁנָה
entries.note: ימי שנותינו בהם yields no intelligible sense; leg. בחיים 'in life'. And בגבורות ('with strength'?) is likewise inexplicable, a makeshift rendering; leg. ואם בן גבורות, 'a son of strength, a vigorous one' (cf. idioms like בני חלוף, בני תמותה).

entries.mt: וְרָהְבָּם עָמָל וָאָוֶן כִּי־גָז חִישׁ וַנָּעֻפָה
entries.note: רהבם is more Aramaic than Hebrew — in Hebrew it means only 'the storming sea', but in Syriac 'restless, hasty activity'; עמל ואון is roughly 'trouble and hastiness'. But כי גז חיש ונעפה is extraordinarily dark, and the ancient versions' readings diverge sharply. A plausible reconstruction combining the variants is 'כי גז חיש מעלינו' — 'for it passes quickly away from us' — the predicate referring back to ימי שנותינו.
entries.flag: among the most heavily disputed cruxes in the psalm; the versional evidence is badly garbled in OCR — verify at high res before using

entries.note: וכיראתך עברתך is dark and surely corrupt. Vielleicht leg. ואך יראיך statt וכיראתך (cf. his note at Ps 119:38), then supply ישיבו, since the half-verse is otherwise too short: 'ואך יראיך ישיבו עברתך' — 'only those who fear Thee can turn back Thy wrath'.

entries.mt: לִמְנוֹת יָמֵינוּ כֵּן הוֹדַע וְנָבִא לְבַב חָכְמָה
entries.emendation: לִמְנוֹת → לְמַלְאוֹת; וְנָבִא → נָבִיא (drop the waw); reconstruct כֵּן הוֹדִיעָנוּ נָבִיא לְבַב חָכְמָה
entries.note: As transmitted the verse is wholly unintelligible. Given the frequent confusion of מ/ל, especially between the verbs מנה and מלא, it yields sense as למלאות ימינו 'to complete our days'. Targum and Talmud (Bava Batra 12a) already read נביא here as 'prophet'; the close should read כן הודיענו נביא לבב חכמה — 'so has a prophet of a wise heart made known to us' — referring to Deutero-Isaiah's promise of long life after the exile (Isa 65:20, 22), whose non-fulfillment the psalmist here laments.

The repetition of ומעשה ידינו כוננהו, missing in most LXX manuscripts, is perhaps a marginal variant that entered the text; in any case leg. כוננהו statt כוננה — it cannot be a liturgical refrain, since this psalm hardly served liturgical use.
